News.title: Two men killed by falling trees as Storm Boelo leaves 160,000 properties without power
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police were called to Dollis Road in Finchley at around 12:40 GMT to reports a tree had fallen onto a moving car, and the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

Chief Inspector Guy Ellwood, from the North West Command Unit, said: "This is a deeply tragic incident and our thoughts are with the loved ones of the young man who lost his life."

A London Ambulance Service spokesperson said it sent incident response officers, paramedics from its hazardous area response team, and a trauma team from London's Air Ambulance to the scene.

Earlier, Police Scotland said a man died after being hit by a falling tree in southern near Castle Douglas.

During Storm Boelo and the earlier Storm Austen, which hit the UK on Friday, 838,700 properties across the country faced power cuts, according to the ENA.

Wind gusts peaked on Sunday morning at 85mph in Machrihanish, in Argyll and Bute, and 84mph in both Stornoway in the Outer Hebrides, and Capel Curig in north Wales.

An amber wind warning issued by the Met Office was in place until 21:00 on Sunday across Scotland and parts of northern England.

A yellow warning that also covered other areas of the north of England, including Liverpool, Manchester, Leeds, Sheffield and Newcastle-upon-Tyne, as well as parts of the East and West Midlands and North Wales, also expired at 21:00.

The Met Office urged people to "stay indoors as much as possible", adding: "If you do go out, try not to walk, or shelter, close to buildings and trees."

The strongest gusts have continued to spread eastwards across the UK on Sunday.

News.title: Funding set to double for plan to get rough sleepers off streets by Christmas
News.content:
Funding is set to double to support a pledge by the prime minister to give every rough sleeper in England a route off the streets by Christmas.

Ending rough sleeping was one of Andy Burnham's first promises when he entered Downing Street, announcing a Â£442m package to provide emergency accommodation and practical support.

On the eve of the first Rough Sleeping Summit at Downing Street on Monday, No 10 has indicated a further Â£432m will be added to the initiative in Wednesday's Budget.

Shadow housing secretary Katie Lam said rough sleeping had hit "record highs under Labour" and criticised Burnham for failing to end rough sleeping when he was the Mayor of Greater Manchester.

The BBC understands the government's commitment is that every rough sleeper will be able to physically move into accommodation by Christmas and/or they will be offered support as a way to prevent them sleeping rough.

Some people may choose not to accept accommodation, but ministers say support will still be offered to them.

The government said initial funding had seen specialist outreach teams and new bed spaces operating in Coventry, with further provision being rolled out in places including Plymouth and Camden in north London over the coming weeks.

Money being added to the pot this week will extend support beyond March 2027 to the end of this Parliament, taking total investment to Â£874m.

Ahead of hosting the summit, Burnham said: "Rough sleeping isn't a fact of life. It's a thing governments either choose to accept or don't.

"Well I don't accept it. That's why we're doubling funding so that people aren't just offered a safe route off the streets this winter but have that same support right through the rest of this Parliament too.

"But we can't do it alone. If we're going to end rough sleeping, we need every part of society behind us on this. So today we're bringing together businesses, charities and local leaders in Downing Street to make sure this is a solution that lasts."

More than 30 organisations have pledged support for the plan with new partnerships, including commercial businesses and charities.

News.title: Letter making claims about Meghan's father written by his first wife, BBC understands
News.content:
A letter sent to the Metropolitan Police making a number of claims relating to the Duchess of Sussex's father was written by his ex-wife Roslyn Loveless, the BBC understands.

Meghan confirmed on Friday she had previously been informed about "disturbing allegations" about her estranged father, Thomas Markle.

On Saturday, the Met confirmed it received a letter relating to Markle in 2019, and it was shared with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time.

It has been reported that images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Markle, 82, had been found in his former home in the Philippines. Markle, who is based in the US, denies all such allegations.

Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan's half-siblings Samantha Markle and Thomas Markle Jr. Loveless divorced Markle in 1975 before he married the Duchess' mother Doria Ragland in 1979.

Meghan was born in 1981 and is the only daughter of Markle and Ragland.

In a statement shared on Friday, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.

Sources close to the duchess said Meghan warned Markle in a letter - sent while he was in hospital in the Philippines after having his leg amputated - that he would never meet his grandchildren.

News.title: End approaching for Carrick but Man Utd fans make clear who they blame
News.content:
There was an air of inevitability about Michael Carrick's walk around Old Trafford after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth.

It is not unusual for Carrick to applaud the Manchester United fans. If anything, his acknowledgements were not as pronounced as they were in Como after the equally devastating loss.

But after eight games without a win, the worst run since 2015-16 and two horrific defeats in a week, the end is approaching for the United boss.

However, if anyone in a senior position at the club thinks the issues at Old Trafford will be solved simply by changing the head coach and, more importantly, the fans will be appeased by a new face in the dugout, the reaction from the stands on an awful day on and off the pitch would have very clearly told them otherwise.

On Friday, as he looked back on that 4-1 loss to Como and ahead to Bournemouth, Carrick said: "We'll be a different team on Sunday. We have to be a different team on Sunday."

Sadly, they weren't.

Carrick could not answer if he will still be in charge for next Saturday's trip to Chelsea. He does not know.

"The responsibility is mine," he said. "What else can I say really right now? I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way. I love this place and I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club."

News.title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy
News.content:
He said both boys had been so excited and been snorkelling in shallow water as they sorted out their towels and bags on the beach when the boys got into difficulties.

Both parents went into the sea and tried to save them as they were swept out by the current, he added, and the whole ordeal happened in less than 10 minutes.

Nathan said the loss of his 36-year-old "childhood sweetheart" was "unimaginable", but she was a "hero... in life and in death" as she helped to rescue the two boys.

"I've known her since infant school," he told the BBC. "We first got together when we were 14... so 22 years."

"There are no words I can use to describe Leanne, same as anyone she has ever known.

"She was the purest of people, the most generous kind and beautiful person who ever walked the Earth.

"Our relationship was perfect. She was the perfect mother, the perfect wife, the foundation of our entire family."

Nathan added: "Royal Caribbean and Virgin Airlines were absolutely incredible to us and made an impossible journey home so much easier."

Now, as he "keeps strong for his boys", a fundraising page has generated nearly Â£9,000 in donations to support the family.

News.title: Burnham open to 'honest discussion' on EU free movement
News.content:
The prime minister says he would welcome an "honest discussion" about the prospect of returning to free movement between the UK and European Union.

Speaking to the Sunday Times, Andy Burnham said a new relationship with Brussels could include full EU membership or joining the single market, requiring free movement.

Asked about Burnham's remarks, Angela Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg "you can't take anything off the table", adding the prime minister was saying "we've got to be pragmatic to get the best deal for Britain and he wants to have the conversation."

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch responded that the prime minister "hasn't thought this through", while Reform UK's Robert Jenrick dismissed the idea as "mad".

Migration dominated debate during the 2016 Brexit campaign, with the Leave campaign raising issues about rules allowing any EU citizen to move to the UK.

Burnham has previously committed to Labour's 2024 election manifesto which ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.

He has said that any changes would require a mandate at a general election, would is due by 2029.

"I think you have to have a very factual, quite evidence-based debate about this," he told the Sunday Times, external, adding he believed the type of migration had changed from revolving door movement of young people.

"Revolving door migration where people would come and then go back is different," he said. "The balance of migration has changed, hasn't it, since then? I think we've just got to have an honest discussion about those things."

But he stressed: "I can't see myself ever recommending anything that would involve joining the euro or Schengen."

The Schengen Agreement allows passport-free travel across EU countries. The UK was able to keep the pound when it was an EU member, but the bloc has pushed new members to adopt the Euro.

His remarks were made ahead of an EU summit on 20 November in Brussels, where the prime minister is expected to pitch options for a reset of relations with the bloc.

On Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Rayner said she wanted to see the best possible deal with the European Union, which may well involve concessions.

"What the prime minister is saying now, and what I want, is that we have an honest conversation about the facts of what the trade-offs are to get the best deal for Britain going forward," she said.

"The frustration for me in the previous debate we had when we had the referendum is that a lot of those facts didn't get the airtime... So I would like us to have an honest conversation about what the trade-offs could be and then put that to the people at a general election."

Writing on X, Badenoch dismissed it as "yet another example of Burnham's foot in mouth syndrome".

She added: "Most people who voted for Brexit did so because they didn't want free movement. Too many politicians have failed to understand the significance and impact of immigration on communities."

Conservative MP and former chancellor Jeremy Hunt, who backed Remain, warned the Brexit debate was "incredibly divisive" and insisted the current Brexit deal can still be made to work.

"I was at the top of a government that was paralysed for several years while we were trying to wrestle with the implications of that vote and I think, having made the decision, we should stick with it and make the most of it - I think we can make it a success," he told Kuenssberg.

Pointing to the one million young people not in work or training, he added: "Surely our priority in that situation is to get those jobs filled by the young people we have here instead of parking them on welfare.

"Which is why I think it's astonishing to lead on the issue of free movement... Something that is actually going to stop young people here getting jobs."

But Liberal Democrat deputy leader Daisy Cooper told Kuenssberg she believed allowing freedom of movement would be "a really good thing for growth" and pushed for the UK to rejoin the single market, the customs union, and also be involved in the bloc's defence pact.

The UK currently has "the worst of both worlds" on immigration, she said, as it was excluded from the EU's "new asylum pact with biometric data" that could be used to "tackle the small boats crisis".

Reform UK's economy spokesperson Robert Jenrick told Kuenssberg he had never believed freedom of movement "was a good thing", despite supporting the Remain position before the 2016 referendum when he was a Conservative MP.

"I think it's completely mad, the idea that this country needs more immigration," he said, claiming data shows mass migration "has been a disaster for working people, for Brits".

"The last thing they want is their wages being undercut by a load of low wage, low-skilled migrants from overseas," he added.

News.title: Board of Deputies of British Jews declares Greens to be racist party
News.content:
The Green Party of England and Wales has been declared a racist organisation by the Board of Deputies of British Jews.

The Jewish body, which is the largest in the UK, was responding to the "Zionism is racism" policy motion passed at the Green Party's conference earlier this month.

Board of Deputies president Phil Rosenberg said a vote passed by 118 votes to one to declare that the Greens had, "by adopting an antisemitic platform, become a racist party".

A spokesman for the Greens insisted the party does not discriminate against people who hold Zionist views and said it rejected the Board of Deputies' "characterisation of this motion and our party".

They added the decision "will not stop us from speaking out against the genocide in Gaza and pushing for stronger sanctions against the Israeli government and its leaders". Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.

The motion passed by the Board of Deputies urged other parties not to do deals with the Greens unless they rejected the policy.

Forming coalition deals with Greens at local or national level would be "failing to take antisemitism with the requisite seriousness", it said, unless the party's local leadership have rejected the policy and committed to overturn it.

Labour has already issued an ultimatum to local Green groups it is currently in coalition with, telling them to disown the motion or lose the party's support.

Rosenberg said: "By adopting an antisemitic platform, the Green Party of England and Wales has become a racist party. We will treat it accordingly.

"No political party has the right to tell Jews that a central part of our identity, rooted in thousands of years of history, faith and peoplehood, is racist.

"The Green Party's policy brands much of our community, including our synagogues and communal organisations, with that slur. It gives prejudice against Jews a political licence.

"The Green Party's leadership must now take responsibility for reversing this policy and confronting the antisemitism it has legitimised."

The motion backed by Green members at its party conference earlier this month said Zionism was an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/ or domination of the non-Jewish population".

It was criticised by Jewish groups, as well as four Green MPs and two former leaders, and opposition political parties.

Responding when the Green motion was passed, the Board of Deputies and Jewish Leadership Council said in a joint statement that "Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it".

Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who is Jewish, did not take part in the vote on the motion as he left the conference early to campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election which was held days later.

He has since told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, he would not overturn the motion, which would be party policy until 2028.

News.title: Antonelli wins in US but has to wait to secure title
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli just missed out on clinching his first world title in a dominant victory in the United States Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old Italian leads Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 123 points after coming home ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

Antonelli will be crowned champion in Mexico City next weekend as long he does not lose more than 23 points to Russell or more than 24 to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

That means a ninth place would be enough to become champion even if Russell wins the race, and a 10th would be enough if Hamilton is victorious.

If Russell or Hamilton do not win, Antonelli will be champion next Sunday no matter where he finishes.

Antonelli stamped his authority on this race in the same way as he has on the season, and was out of touch even by the first corner as his rivals all battled behind him at the Circuit of the Americas.

The key stories of the race were:

Antonelli's sublime victory, his first since the Spanish Grand Prix last month

A race-long squabble between Leclerc and Verstappen for second place

Little else, frankly

Antonelli took control of the race from the very beginning, an excellent start combined with a gripping scrap through the first lap between Verstappen and Leclerc leaving him more than two seconds clear by the end of the first lap.

No-one got near him from then on.

Mercedes had chosen the medium tyres for the start, while Leclerc and the Red Bulls of Verstappen and Isack Hadjar started on new softs.

And Antonelli was able to convert that choice into a one-stop race while almost everyone else did two, emphasising his superiority as he finished 16 seconds clear of Leclerc.

The race was also a stamp of approval for the Mercedes upgrade package that was introduced two races ago in Malaysia but initially took them backwards.

Assiduous work ever since has moved it to the point where, while it remains tricky to optimise, it is definitively quicker than the older specification.

"It was the result we needed," Antonelli said. "All this time putting work on the new package and finally seeing the result was very pleasant, perfect strategy to call the one-stop."

As for the title, he said: "I know we are very close. We try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon."

Russell, who started sixth, had a frustrating race. He was given a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage, which dropped him to 10th after his pit stop. He could only make up two places and finished eighth.

Hamilton's fourth place means both he and fellow Briton Russell just about retain a mathematical chance of winning the championship.

News.title: Why the King's Caribbean tour could be 'biggest risk of his reign'
News.content:
The King will make three significant speeches during the Caribbean trip and will follow government advice not to issue an official apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade.

A senior royal aide said that the King would "not shy away from the darkest days of our past" but stressed that decisions over apologies and reparations were matters for government.

The current Burnham administration, like those before it, will not pay reparations.

Buckingham Palace says that acknowledging the wrongs of the past will be built into the King's programme in all three countries.

But apologies, reparations, and republicanism are rich pickings for campaigners and protests are likely.

This is the reality for the King and Buckingham Palace, and they are accepting of it.

Those who've worked on the planning of the trip view protests as part of the open debate in the region and security preparations include their possibility.

Lurking in the back of Royal Household minds will also be memories of the last tour by senior royals to the Caribbean in the early part of 2022.

Then, as the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge, William and Catherine found themselves facing criticism over the optics of the trip - images of the royal couple reaching out to touch the outstretched hands of Jamaican children through a wire fence looked clumsy. Engagements designed as tributes to past royal visits appeared outdated. And protests also caused the cancellation of a small part of the schedule.

Everything will have been done to avoid those kinds of missteps on the 2026 Caribbean tour.

News.title: Long queues after power surge at Stansted Airport
News.content:
Passengers arriving at Stansted Airport have described waiting in long queues to reach immigration control after a power surge shut down its systems.

Traveller Jill Stakem reported the airport's internal tram system had failed earlier and people were "being held in a corridor for over 90 minutes".

Stakem added: "It's horrendous. No communication, no seating for people, no-one offering watering."

In a statement, a spokesperson for Stansted Airport said: "Due to a power surge earlier today that affected the airport and local area, a number of airport systems were temporarily impacted."

They added: "All systems are now back in service with operational teams working hard to provide support to passengers on their journeys through the airport."

Another airport spokesperson confirmed the shuttle service "remained out-of-service due to a technical fault and contingency bussing is in operation to transfer passengers between the terminal and gates".

News.title: Four-year-old girl dies after fall from tower block
News.content:
A four-year-old girl has died after falling from a tower block in east London.

The Metropolitan Police said officers were called to the scene at an address in St Paul's Road, Barking, at about 11:00 BST on Saturday morning, following reports that a child had fallen from height.

Paramedics from the London Ambulance Service gave first aid and the child was taken to hospital, but later died from her injuries.

A Met spokesperson said the incident was not believed to be suspicious.

"Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with the child's family and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time," they said.

"An investigation into the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident is ongoing. However, at this time, the incident is not believed to be suspicious.

"We urge anyone with information about the incident to contact police on 101, quoting CAD 2424/24OCT."

News.title: Plan for Northern Olympics to get £7m in Healey's Budget
News.content:
The report will look in closer detail at how hosting the games could work.

It will consider the kinds of venues and transport links required, how different cities could share the games, how communities could benefit.

Crucially it will also examine how much it could cost as well as assess the chances of a bid succeeding. The Conservative-Lib Dem coalition government said in 2013 it estimated hosting in London had cost Â£8.9bn.

A report in 2013 by the UK Trade and Investment, which has since been replaced by the Department for International Trade, said it had sparked a Â£9.9bn boost to the economy through new contracts, sales and foreign investments.

But the estimated amount was queried by some, including the Federation of Small Businesses and the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (NIESR).

Conservative shadow sports minister Louie French said that while hosting an Olympic Games would "likely provide a positive boost for the country", the cost of proposals would require "careful scrutiny".

He said the chancellor should use the Budget to bring down everyday costs before looking to "spend millions in taxpayer cash on reheated announcements made by his predecessor".

French added: "The irony is that Labour's new tourism tax will create a cost barrier for sports fans wanting to visit the North of England for an Olympic Games."

The new feasibility study for the Northern Games will be done by government, UK Sport, the Northern Mayors and include the British Olympic and Paralympic associations.

Healey said: "Olympic legacy lasts way beyond the celebration of sport over the summer. The North hosting an event as big as this would be truly unforgettable.

"Britain's experience of London 2012 is proof we can host the world. I'm picking up the pace on our work to potentially bid for these prestigious games. It will lift communities, create opportunities and give the UK a huge boost."

News of the funding for the study was welcomed by the British Olympic Association, ParalympicsGB and UK Sport.

"We welcome the government's continued support for exploring the potential of a future bid for the Olympic and Paralympic Games in the UK in the 2040s," they said in a joint statement.

"Building on the success and legacy of London 2012, we look forward to working in partnership to explore this exciting opportunity and the benefits it could deliver for the nation, and for the global Olympic and Paralympic movements."

News.title: Budget to include £1bn for social and affordable housing
News.content:
Under the plans for the regions, an initial Â£285m in transitional seed funding will be allocated by the government next year to support mayors and local leaders - and reduce reliance on "fragmented bidding pots" in Whitehall, the Treasury said.

The government will also confirm that it will work with mayors to design a new Â£1.5bn borrowing facility from 2028, which would allow them to access capital needed to support local priorities.

The Treasury said this could be put towards new homes, bringing High Streets back to life, or improving transport links.

Healey said: "Mayors and local leaders know what their communities need to grow, which is why we are giving them more money, more power and more capacity to get projects moving, build homes and make the right decisions for their areas."

Areas across the country which are not yet strategic authorities will be able to access a share of the Â£285m to "unlock projects which will contribute to growth in their areas".

The prime minister said: "I'm calling time on local leaders going cap in hand to Westminster. That is no way to run a country."

Claire Ward, chairwoman of the UK Mayors Network and Labour's East Midlands mayor, said that having the "right powers and resources through increased devolution" would help turn "ambitious plans into reality and deliver real, lasting change" for communities.

Lord Sadiq Khan, Labour's mayor of London, said greater ability to invest could "help unlock transformational infrastructure projects" including the West London Orbital route, the extension of the Bakerloo Underground line and Docklands Light Railway, and the development of Stratford International station.

Departing Treasury entrepreneurship adviser, Alex Depledge, has criticised the government's treatment of start-ups ahead of her last day on Thursday - the day after the Budget.

She told the Sunday Times, external, that start-ups were being treated as a "sideshow" and should not be pushed to the "margins of economic policy".

"Keeping scale-ups on the fringes underestimates the contribution of our greatest companies, and we need to support and develop them on British shores at all costs," she said.

Leading up to the Budget, defence has also remained a key talking point. Healey resigned in June from his role as defence secretary in the previous government over the defence investment plan, which he claimed fell "well short" of what was needed to fund the armed forces.

He had called for defence spending to rise to 3% of the country's GDP by 2030, on the way to reaching a Nato target of 3.5% in 2035.

But urging him to commit to setting out plans to spend 3% of GDP on defence, the shadow chancellor said: "We are living in an era of extraordinary threats, and yet the chancellor is dithering over finding the money to pay the country's insurance premium... you cannot have a strong economy without a strong defence".

Responding to Andrew Griffith's comments, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the Conservatives were to blame for failing to invest in the military while in office.

Streeting said the prime minister had made it clear that his government was "determined to give our armed forces the investment needed to keep us safe".

News.title: Thousands of people gather in support of Drumcree Orangemen
News.content:
The first part of the parade was followed by a series of speeches, mainly from members of the Orange Order.

This was very much an Orange Order event and not a political rally but inevitably there was a political tone to many of the comments.

There was explicit criticism of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) Chief Constable Jon Boutcher, the secretary of state and the first minister, but also implicit criticism of the leaders of the two biggest unionist parties - the DUP and Ulster Unionist Party.

Traditional Unionist Voice leader Jim Allister was applauded but by far the loudest cheers were for the Orange Order's legal adviser Jamie Bryson and the local MP Lockhart.

She was invited on to the stage and presented with a special gift for her support of the Orangemen.

Lockhart was the only politician to take to the stage, where she repeated her challenge to the DUP leadership: "Profound consequences must mean profound consequences. Michelle O'Neill must go.

"That's where I stand, and this lady is not for turning."

Portadown District Master Nigel Dawson warned politicians that they could face consequences at the next election over the Drumcree dispute.

"Politicians need to remember that we put them into office and we can take them out of office," he said.

He added that the Orange Order had won the right "to return home via our traditional route and Portadown District intends to exercise that right on a date and time of our choosing, and if necessary, without further recourse".

Orange Order Deputy District Master Alistair Power said Drumcree must not be allowed to divide unionism.

"It should not be used by parties to attack each other publicly over differences of opinion," he added. "We need to stand united."

News.title: Habitat destroyed by Cairngorms fire to be restored with government funding
News.content:
More than Â£1m is to be spent on nature recovery projects, including the restoration of habitats destroyed by a fire which ripped through a huge area of hillside in the Cairngorms.

The Scottish government funding will support habitat, species and river restoration, control of invasive non-native species and deer management across Scotland.

It includes Â£150,100 for recovery and nature restoration work following the Abernethy wildfire in the Cairngorms in July, to restore damaged habitats, help wildlife recover and reduce the risk of future wildfires.

Further funding will be provided to a range of other projects.

News.title: Reward offered over murder in flat used as brothel
News.content:
A Â£20,000 reward is being offered by Crimestoppers in connection with the murder of a man who was found dead in a Birmingham flat in 2022.

Jinming Zhang had been stabbed multiple times before he was found in the property, which police said was being used as a brothel, in Moseley Street in Digbeth.

West Midlands Police previously released CCTV of a suspect, while a DNA sample from the suspected killer found at the scene did not produce a match on the national database.

The case was featured in the BBC series of Forensics: The Real CSI last year, which revealed police believed the murder suspect may have sustained a hand injury in the frenzied attack.

Jenny Birch, who has been overseeing the investigation, urged anyone with information "no matter how small" to contact police.

"Someone out there knows something, and we won't give up until we have answers," she said.

News.title: Sunderland remain bottom of Premier League table after stalemate with Leeds
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Sunderland and Leeds were forced to share the spoils in a goalless stalemate at the Stadium of Light.

A scrappy first half saw Brian Brobbey have two promising opportunities to put the Black Cats ahead but he was denied both times by James Trafford.

Both sides threatened after the break and Nilson Angulo enjoyed the better chances for Sunderland before Ao Tanaka came close for the visitors.

A point snaps the Wearsiders’ four-game losing run in the Premier League but they remain bottom of the standings, while Leeds stay in the top half of the table, sat seventh.

Brobbey made his return from injury with a place in the starting line-up as one of six changes from Sunderland’s midweek Europa League draw against Lech Poznan and Daniel Farke made three switches to the side who drew 1-1 with Manchester United last weekend.

Leeds sniffed around the Sunderland box in the early stages as Jayden Bogle skewed wide and Harry Wilson’s free-kick was met by Jaka Bijol, but his flicked header was easily held by Robin Roefs.

The Black Cats had an excellent opportunity to take the lead when Brobbey fired towards the bottom left corner, forcing Trafford into a low save.

Brobbey was in the thick of the action again, pouncing on the ball following a tame exchange of passes between the Leeds defence, and Trafford was quick off his line to block the striker’s shot.

The chance spurred Sunderland on as they enjoyed a bright spell around the Leeds box, but neither side was able to put a shot away as the half petered out.

A bizarre incident at the start of the second half saw Nordi Mukiele caught around the throat by team-mate Luke O’Nien and the defender was forced off, with Omar Alderete replacing him seven minutes after the restart.

The centre-half was immediately called into action to clear a dangerous Leeds delivery into the area and Sunderland were forced to scramble away an overhead kick attempt from Brenden Aaronson.

Tarik Muharemovic’s header from a corner was held by Roefs as Leeds continued to pile on the pressure.

Angulo had a fierce effort pushed away by Trafford and minutes later the winger was again denied by a diving save from the Leeds goalkeeper.

An inswinging corner from Granit Xhaka was cleared as far as Angulo, who had another effort blocked for the Black Cats.

Leeds broke through substitute Anton Stach down the middle and a cross from Bogle on the right was hooked away at the back post by Noah Sadiki.

Tanaka’s shot was stopped by Roefs and O’Nien and Dominic Calvert-Lewin raced for the loose ball, which was eventually cleared.

A mistake at the back nearly allowed Chemsdine Talbi through, but the substitute’s strike was blocked by Bijol.

In the final minutes, Sean Longstaff was denied by a low stop from Roefs and the midfielder had a strike blocked by bodies in front of the goal line as the points were shared.

News.title: Kylian Mbappe’s Clasico double condemns Barcelona to first La Liga defeat of season
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Real Madrid became the first side to beat Barcelona in La Liga this season, defeating the league leaders 2-1 at Camp Nou with a brace from Kylian Mbappe.

Mbappe's 11th goal in 10 top-flight games secured victory ⁠for Jose Mourinho in his return to El Clasico 13 years after his first spell at Real Madrid ended, as the visitors halved the gap at the top to three points.

Both sides created a series of half-chances early on, but Real's forays forward came with far more resolve. Barca manager ​Hansi ⁠Flick's frustration on the touchline served as evidence that Mourinho's game plan was functioning better than his own.

In the 41st minute Yan Diomande crossed from the left and Gerard Martin's soft clearance hit the onrushing Mbappe, bouncing off him and into the net. Barcelona had the chance to level before the break after a fortunate ricochet, but Lamine Yamal couldn't convert from close range.

It was a set piece that undid Real in the 61st minute, with Pedri's reverse pass finding Raphinha in space in the box and the Brazilian finishing into the corner.

Real's swift movement of the ball in their own half continued ⁠to expose the Barcelona backline in the early stages of the second half. However, following the goal, the visitors found it increasingly hard to escape Barcelona's pressing.

Barcelona's attacks were now finishing with last-ditch blocks from the Real defence, even if Mourinho's side continued to carry a threat going forward.

open image in gallery Raphinha levelled the score after a disguised pass from Pedri ( Getty )

That defensive conviction was rewarded with three minutes remaining. A loose touch from Barcelona ‌substitute Gabriel Jesus set Real on the counter-attack, and substitute ​Eduardo Camavinga had enough pace to get in behind the defence, ‌before squaring the ball for ⁠Mbappe to tap into the empty net.

Barcelona remain top of the standings with 27 points from 10 games, one ahead of Atletico Madrid in second place and three ahead of Real Madrid.

Earlier Athletic Club beat Getafe ‌4-0 and Real Sociedad won 2-1 ​against Levante. Real Betis remain fourth after drawing 0-0 with Celta Vigo.

News.title: Government commits extra £432m to get rough sleepers off streets by Christmas
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Chancellor John Healey will use his Budget statement on Wednesday to confirm an additional £432m aimed at addressing rough sleeping.

The money will double the funding pot for tackling the problem, according to an announcement made ahead of the statement.

Andy Burnham pledged in August to offer every rough sleeper in England a pathway off the streets by Christmas.

The prime minister will bring private firms, charities and local leaders together at a rough sleeping summit at Downing Street on Monday to consider ways of tackling the issue.

Mr Burnham said that “every part of society” needs to contribute to ending rough sleeping.

open image in gallery A rough sleeper’s tent on the banks of the River Thames ( AFP/Getty )

“Rough sleeping isn’t a fact of life. It’s a thing governments either choose to accept or don’t,” he said.

“Well, I don’t accept it. That’s why we’re doubling funding so that people aren’t just offered a safe route off the streets this winter but have that same support right through the rest of this parliament, too.

“But we can’t do it alone. If we’re going to end rough sleeping, we need every part of society behind us on this.”

The most up-to-date annual national statistics estimated there were 4,793 people sleeping rough on a single night in autumn 2025 in England.

The new Budget funding comes on top of £442m committed earlier this year.

It will allow the rough sleeping programme to continue until the end of the current parliament in 2029.

open image in gallery A rough sleeper lies on a suitcase in central London ( AFP via Getty Images )

Organisations attending the summit include the National Housing Federation, which will work with housing associations to identify at least 2,000 potential homes and bed spaces.

Beauty firm L’Oréal Group will launch a social salon partnership with St Mungo’s and Haircuts4Homeless, while Virgin Media O2 will provide digital support to organisations working with the homeless.

Other attendees at the summit include the Salvation Army, Ikea, the Morrisons Foundation and Comic Relief.

Housing secretary Angela Rayner said: “This is a big ambition – we know that. But we will not back down from making sure everyone has the offer of a route off the streets this Christmas.

“This summit is about bringing every part of society together behind that mission.”

Thierry Cheval, the boss of L’Oreal Group UK and Ireland, said: “Beauty plays an essential role in restoring dignity and a positive sense of self.

“For people rebuilding their lives, this simple act of care provides a crucial boost in confidence and wellbeing as they re-engage with the world and take their next steps towards social integration.”

open image in gallery Prime minister Andy Burnham says every rough sleeper in England will be offered a way off the streets by Christmas ( PA Wire )

Mairi MacRae, acting chief executive at homelessness charity Shelter, said: “Matching the money with new commitments from businesses, local leaders and charities demonstrates that we can choose to end rough sleeping as a society.

“Helping people off the streets is the first step, the next is ensuring everyone has a long-term settled home with the right wraparound support, for which this extra injection of cash is vital.

“To keep people from returning to the streets and eradicate homelessness in all its forms, the government must not waver from its promise to deliver a council housing revolution.”

Mr Burnham pledged as his “first instruction” on day one in No 10 in July to “finally end long-term, rough sleeping across the UK at the earliest opportunity”.

But he has faced criticism from the Conservatives over his record as mayor of Greater Manchester on the issue.

Shadow housing secretary Katie Lam said: “Burnham is throwing another £432m at a problem he failed to solve in Greater Manchester. Under Labour, rough sleeping has hit record highs – yet their answer is always more taxpayers’ money and more empty promises.

“Healey must use his Budget this week to cut taxes for working people, get the ballooning benefits bill under control, and stop pushing up energy prices.

“Instead of piling more costs onto hard-working people, Healey must focus on easing the cost of living and delivering real value for taxpayers’ money.”

The £432m will be confirmed in the chancellor’s statement on Wednesday, on top of the £442m already committed.

News.title: Kimi Antonelli moves to brink of F1 title with supreme United States GP triumph
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kimi Antonelli demonstrated his title-winning prowess with a thumping victory at the United States Grand Prix but his coronation as champion was put on ice.

The 20-year-old delivered everything he needed to in his first shot at becoming the youngest Formula One champion in history by converting his pole position into a resounding win in Austin – crossing the line 13.0 seconds ahead of Charles Leclerc.

For the title to be wrapped up, the Italian needed major slip ups from his rivals. Lewis Hamilton extended the championship race by finishing fourth and George Russell just about did his bit despite only managing a disappointing eighth.

Antonelli will head to Mexico City next week with a whopping 123-point lead over Russell, with Hamilton a point further back. A finish of ninth or higher will seal the title, no matter where his rivals finish.

He leapt from his Mercedes and launched himself into the arms of his mechanics for the ninth time in this dominant season.

Leclerc claimed second for successive weeks after an impressive race for Ferrari, making a late move on Max Verstappen who completed the podium.

Lando Norris made a one-stop strategy work to claim fifth for McLaren.

Antonelli believed it would take something “catastrophic” from his rivals for him to clinch the crown in Texas, but knew winning the race was required for his end of the bargain.

He then needed Russell, whose faint title challenge has evaporated over recent races, to finish ninth or lower and Hamilton to be fifth or lower.

Part one of Antonelli’s job was done on Saturday as he soared to a magnificent pole as the sun began to drop on the Circuit of the Americas. With Hamilton only fifth and Russell sixth, his chances of getting over the line increased.

open image in gallery Antonelli stormed off the line from pole position ( Getty )

If the Italian was feeling any nerves as he sat on the grid waiting for his shot at history, he certainly did not show them as he blasted off the line and left Verstappen in his wake.

Top-10 - United States Grand Prix 1. Kimi Antonelli 2. Charles Leclerc 3. Max Verstappen 4. Lewis Hamilton 5. Lando Norris 6. Isack Hadjar 7. Oscar Piastri 8. George Russell 9. Liam Lawson 10. Pierre Gasly

The Dutchman was swallowed up by the fast-starting Leclerc, who also jumped Isack Hadjar, while Verstappen then had to fend off Hamilton who rose to fourth. The Ferrari pair went wheel-to-wheel before Leclerc’s magnificent move on Verstappen.

The four-time world champion was soon up to speed and rocketed up the inside of Leclerc to reclaim second but Antonelli had already checked out – 2.4 seconds ahead at the end of the opening lap.

Russell’s role in the celebration-delaying picture was hampered as he was investigated for leaving the track and staying ahead of Oscar Piastri – with whom he banged wheels as he rejoined.

A five-second penalty was dished out to the Mercedes man. In a race fraught with jeopardy, Russell and Hamilton were now both on the cusp of handing Antonelli his crowning moment.

Verstappen was the first to pull the trigger on a pit stop on lap 14, swiftly followed by Hamilton and Leclerc but Antonelli – who started on the more durable medium tyres – and Mercedes chose not to respond.

Russell pitted and served his penalty on lap 24, rejoining a net eighth before Antonelli pitted a lap later and was now a net third – on much fresher tyres than those ahead.

New race leader Verstappen was showing strong pace, while Hamilton was promoted to fourth when Hadjar boxed.

open image in gallery Hamilton needed to be in the top four to extend the title race

The Dutchman pitted for a second time with 25 laps remaining, as Antonelli charged through on Leclerc to lead once more.

Leclerc and Hamilton stopped again in the final 16 laps, rejoining fourth and sixth – with the British driver needing to make up two places to ensure he kept Antonelli from the trophy.

He dispatched Hadjar swiftly but Norris had done a magnificent job on a one-stop strategy. The reigning champion – about to yield his crown – was reeled in on lap 47 by Verstappen and Leclerc, and Hamilton rose to fourth the following lap.

All the action was taking place behind Antonelli, who marched on serenely out front.

Antonelli has been the standout performer of the 2026 season and will be crowned a worthy champion over the coming weeks, fittingly shining brightest once again in the Lone Star State.

News.title: Jaguar Land Rover cyber-attack was ‘state-sponsored’, former minister suggests
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A cyber-attack which caused up to £2.1bn of damage to Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) last year was state-sponsored, a former armed forces minister has suggested.

Estimated at £1.9bn (ranging from £1.6bn to £2.1bn by the Cyber Monitoring Centre), the cyber-attack was the most economically damaging in UK history. In June, a New York Times investigation linked the attack to a Russian hacking group.

Al Carns, former armed forces minister, made the comments in July at an event at the Chatham House think tank. He was asked about how the UK could deter “threats in the absence of political leadership”, according to a report in The Telegraph.

Mr Carns reportedly replied: “We have all the detail. We know all of the information, we know all of the threats. Sometimes it comes out sporadically, but it’s not a centrally coherent national conversation between government and society.

“We know there is £15bn of cyber-attacks, we know there’s espionage going on, we know there’s 35,000 casualties a month-ish in Ukraine. We know the Jaguar Land Rover attack was state-sponsored, etc, etc.”

open image in gallery Former defence minister Al Carns ( PA Wire )

Mr Carns told The Telegraph that his comments were not based on an official Ministry of Defence assessment, adding: “It would be highly unlikely for an attack of that scale to emanate from anywhere without the host state knowing about it”.

Jaguar Land Rover had to halt production for five weeks last September after the cyber attack. They were forced to shut down their computer networks, leaving them unable to operate their production lines.

They arranged a war room to fight the hackers comprising of cybersecurity investigators, and representatives from the National Crime Agency, the National Cyber Security Centre, Google and the FBI, according to The New York Times.

open image in gallery Defence Secretary Wes Streeting warned of the need to be ready in case businesses were hit by cyber attacks ( PA Wire )

Microsoft, who had reportedly been tracking the Russian group responsible, apparently alerted Jaguar to who had breached their systems. The encryption used by the group was described as “really, really complicated”.

MPs have been pushing the UK government to be more transparent about who they believe to be behind the damaging hack. Labour MP Graeme Downie said this Summer that ministers should be more open about the incident “so the British people can see we are already in a conflict with Russia”.

This weekend, defence secretary Wes Streeting warned that Britain must be ready for war in 1,000 days.

open image in gallery Jaguar Land Rover temporarily shut production following its cyber attack ( PA Media )

Writing in The Telegraph, Mr Streeting warns Britain’s adversaries could be ready to attack the UK in 2030.

He wrote: “Our adversaries’ willingness to harm us is not new. What has changed is their capacity. By 2030 their force strength and war economy could put them in a position to attack.

“That gives us a little over 1,000 days to complete our mission: to be ready with our allies to fight and win.”

News.title: Antonelli just two points from F1 title after winning US Grand Prix
News.content:
Hamilton and Leclerc were next in, switching to mediums, with Leclerc in particular coming to life. Mercedes stuck to their guns. Russell came in on lap 22 for a set off hard compound tyres and re-emerged in 10th, with Antonelli doing likewise two laps later.

That put Verstappen into the lead of the race, but the Dutchman seemed stressed. His radio was not working brilliantly, limiting his communications with his race engineer Tom Hart, while he was furious that the team did not order team-mate Hadjar out of the way when he came up behind him after stopping. “Thanks guys. Really good strategy there. Stuck in the dirty air. F---.”

His mood was not helped by a slow stop on lap 31 to switch to a set of medium tyres.

On lap 38, Hamilton pitted and came out in sixth. Russell, meanwhile, was languishing perilously in eighth, unable to pass Piastri in seventh despite having fresher tyres.

At this point, Antonelli was within a whisker of being crowned champion. All it would have taken was Russell to lose one spot. Admittedly, he was 28 seconds ahead of Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson, but all it would have taken was a mistake, or a power unit failure and the title race was over.

Rather incredibly, it is the first time Verstappen has been out of title contention since the final race of 2020. “Yeah, I think our overall pace was not good enough and probably the tyres we had available were probably not the right ones. For whatever reason it didn’t work out. We still managed to get on the podium... I’ll take it.”

A late virtual safety car after Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac ground to a halt by the side of the track, made the final laps rather processional, denying us the opportunity of seeing the fast-closing Hamilton take on Verstappen for the final podium spot. But it hardly mattered. The day belonged once again to Antonelli, who should be champion by the end of next week.

News.title: Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick
News.content:
Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

News.title: Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1
News.content:
Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

News.title: England pay price for toothless bowling in astonishing defeat by Pakistan
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, over-by-over coverage of Pakistan v England in Lahore. In the UK, the clocks went back an hour overnight; England would love to wind them back 72 hours and have another go at defending 429 against Sri Lanka. That unfathomable defeat in Rawalpindi has left them on the brink in this tri-series.

England won’t be mathematically eliminated if they lose to Pakistan today, but it would leave them needing snookers if they are to reach Saturday’s final. Realistically, they need to win the last two group games, and there’s a chance even that might not be enough.

“It’s my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup styles and pressures,” said the England all-rounder Will Jacks. “You can’t replicate that in training or a bilateral series. In World Cups you have to bounce back. I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward.

“I’m not saying it’s the same thing but it’s a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins.”

Jacks’ Surrey team-mate Sam Curran suffered the most against Sri Lanka, conceding an eye-watering 103 from his nine overs.

“They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in and he bowls a lot of pressure overs – that’s his role in the team,” said Jacks. “He’s been so successful with that for England over a number of years. There are some days where it doesn’t quite work.”

Curran has kept his place in the side – but Josh Tongue is replaced by Henry Crocombe, who makes his international debut. And there’s no recall for Adil Rashid. We’ll have the toss and full team news in a moment.

News.title: Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off
News.content:
This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

News.title: Antonelli takes another step closer to F1 title with US GP pole position
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, just outside of Austin. This is one of the finest tracks that we have on the Formula One calendar and is a fitting place for the US Grand Prix. The races are usually entertaining, the drivers love the track (though have complained about the bumps this year) and it comfortably the best on-track action of the three races in the US.

What might we see this weekend? Well, Kimi Antonelli could be crowned world champion if results go his way. The way the results need to go make that fairly unlikely, but stranger things have happened in F1 and they often do. In any case, it would take a catastrophic implosion for Antonelli to lose the championship from here, so it is a case of when rather than if.

Who looks in good form? Well, Ferrari do. They have brought an updated car here this weekend it, so far, is paying off. Charles Leclerc had good pace yesterday and Lewis Hamilton, his team-mate, was fastest earlier today in final practice. Hamilton’s time of 1min34.893sec was a tenth or two quicker than the Red Bull of Max Verstappen, with Leclerc not too far behind. Then it was Antonelli, George Russell in the second Mercedes and Oscar Piastri making up the top six, though the Australian was nearly half a second off the ultimate pace of Hamilton.

Qualifying begins in about 50 minutes and we will be here with all the updates from that.

News.title: Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head
News.content:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

News.title: Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Sports.title: Man Utd need to sack Michael Carrick after Bournemouth but buck can’t stop with him – Jason Wilcox must go as well
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED supporters know the manager has to go but the buck cannot stop with Michael Carrick.

United matchgoers have booed the manager before. On Sunday, they turned on the players as soon as Carrick disappeared down the tunnel.



Diogo Dalot had dozily lingered longer on the pitch than teammates, so was the last player left on it. The boos grew louder for a United player who has outstayed his welcome.

United have lost 3-0 at home to Bournemouth three times within three years under three different managers. That is ample evidence that Carrick cannot be the only one who goes.



There was gallows humour on the Stretford End as they told Sir Jim Ratcliffe to shove his new stadium up his backside.

There were sinister songs about kissing Ratcliffe and the Glazers on a bonfire. Ousting the Glazers is wishful thinking but jettisoning director of football Jason Wilcox is not just doable but advisable.



Ratcliffe said last year he would not have “tolerated” Ed Woodward. Wilcox has mimicked Woodward by promoting a former player from interim to permanent head coach only for United to spiral.

It has been sooner and more spectacular than under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Carrick is cut from the same cloth as his colleague and friend, who was also in the running to replace Ruben Amorim in January.



That Wilcox considered Solskjaer was a red flag. Wilcox’s treatment of Amorim in their infamous Wolves debrief last season convinced the Portuguese to engineer his own sacking.

Sports.title: Barcelona 1 Real Madrid 2: Mbappe rains on Lamine Yamal’s parade to claim El Clasico win after Bellingham brilliance
Sports.content:
Next

KYLIAN MBAPPE will not win the Ballon d’Or – but he heads to London having firmly wiped the smile from Lamine Yamal’s face.

Mbappe’s double, a comical opener and a shock late winner, ended Barcelona’s perfect LaLiga start.



This is why Jose Mourinho was brought back.

Ahead of the Ballon d’Or showdown between Yamal and Harry Kane tonight, Barca’s teenage terror was, in prime Mourinho fashion, booted to the Clasico fringes by Real.



Mbappe has touted himself for football’s top individual prize, but surely cannot top either Kane or his LaLiga rival tomorrow night.

But in cutting the gap to the top a from six to three points, he and Real remain in the title hunt, Raphinha’s goal irrelevant and Barca hearts broken.



Mourinho had said there was to be no specific plan to stop Barcelona’s young phenom.

He may not have altered his tactics, but Marc Cucurella had certainly been given clear guidance: make his life hell.

Whether he was walloping his Spain teammate into the air, trying to relieve him of his shirt or just snapping at his heels the frizzy-haired full-back was sticking to his task with gusto and causing clear frustration.

LaLiga’s two grandest clubs have been freescoring this season but both were struggling to create clear openings.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Raphinha fired high and then, after a fine back-heel layoff from Anthony Gordon, sent another wide.

Mbappe attempted some acrobatics but was closer to the building site of a top-tier than Joan Garcia’s goal.

Perhaps then it was inevitable that, with the eyes of the world on Camp Nou, the opener would be more by accident than design.

Taking a break from shamelessly kicking lumps out of Yamal, Cucurella fed Yan Diomande down the left.



The winger drove forward and guided a low cross with the outside of his boot, which is where the quality ended and the slapstick took over.

Gerard Martin arrived on the scene to clear, but thumped the ball straight into Mbappe, who was flinching instead of finishing but still ended up celebrating as it cannoned in off of his knee.

Yamal had the chance to hit back almost immediately, fed on the edge of the six-yard box by Fermin Lopez but duffed his finish entirely.



A superb Bellingham run five minutes after the restart opened the door for Real to double their lead.

Two-on-one with Mbappe all the Englishman had to do was square the ball, but he opted to go alone and made a mess of it.

There was much better to come, however.



After Raphinha’s leveller looked to have this Clasico on course for a point-a-piece, Bellingham, belatedly, rose to the moment.

Some stunning skill, sidestepping one Barca shirt and rolling another, sent Eduardo Camavinga haring down the right.

The French sub squared for his compatriot to prod home and seal a first Real Madrid win here in three years.

Mourinho dropped to his knees and pumped his fist as bottles rained down on his players who celebrated in front of the Barca fans.

A bit more of that and this time next year, the Ballon d’Or and a bit more may be in the hands of Mbappe.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker and Harry Kane’s old bosses on why striker should be England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years
Sports.content:
Next

HARRY KANE is the bookies’ favourite to win the Ballon d’Or tonight — as it comes to London for the first time.

The 70th anniversary ceremony is being held at the London Palladium Theatre, in tribute to its first winner, England great Stanley Matthews.



Three Lions captain Kane bagged an astonishing 73 GOALS for club and country last season — only ­bettered by Lionel Messi’s 82 in 2011-12.

Kane, a league winner with Bayern Munich, faces fierce competition from the likes of Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.



Gary Lineker and Kane’s former bosses Harry Redknapp and Tim Sherwood told SunSport’s Jack Rosser and Isabelle Barker why Kane should be the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

GARY LINEKER

I’ve got a feeling it will be Harry. What he’s done has been amazing.



There are a lot of really, really good players in the world at the moment.

The Ballon d’Or is the Ballon d’Or. It’s way more important than it was in my day. I should have won it. I was robbed in 1986!

It’s between Harry and Lamine Yamal, if you look at the bookmakers — and you could make a case for both, obviously.

Kylian Mbappe and Yamal have made cases for themselves, as has Harry in a way — he’s done all the interviews.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

I’ve never seen him appear so much all over the place. And that’s great.

That’s how it is nowadays.

So you put yourself out there without quite saying it to everybody, classically British in his modesty, I suppose.

But he’s absolutely deserving if he wins it. And I hope he does, it would be great to see an English player win it.



He’s also a really good bloke, as well as a magnificent all-round centre-forward.

And to score that many goals this season, he totally merits it.

If you’re talking about the best footballer, it’s hard to look past Yamal. But I’d actually say this year’s Lionel Messi is still the world’s best player.

He was easily the best player at the World Cup. He really was. Spain won it, so therefore, Rodri won it. And he deserved it, too.



But Messi was unbelievable. He’s won enough. I think it’ll come down to Harry, I’ve got a feeling it’ll be him.

There are certain things that those voting have to weigh up about the success of your season.

But Harry won a double for Bayern Munich and hit a multitude of goals.

He won the European Golden Boot. He scored six goals at the World Cup.



Didn’t quite manage it at the end.

Will not winning a World Cup or Champions League count against him in some people’s eyes?

Because Spain won the World Cup and the World Cup is generally the big thing of the year.

Someone like Mbappe would have been running him close.



But Real Madrid didn’t win anything either — and France didn’t quite make it.

Kane was also brilliant at the World Cup. So you’re in among the game’s absolute elite.

I think it’s 50-50 between Harry and Yamal, ultimately — and it’s in London!

HARRY REDKNAPP

I have a funny story about Harry Kane, who I worked with when I was Tottenham manager.



I loaned him out when he was 17 to Barry Hearn, who was the chairman of Leyton Orient.

Hearn rang me and said ‘We’re going to get relegated. Have you got any players at Tottenham you could loan me?’

So I said, ‘Yeah, I’ve got three kids here you can have, take them, it will do them the world of good to go and play’.

So I loaned him three players, and I was at a function the other week where he spoke.



He said, ‘Harry loaned me three players — and at the end of the season we stayed up’.

Hearn recalled saying at the time ‘Andros Townsend, he could go back and play for Tottenham’, which he did, he played for England.

‘Stephen Caulker, he could go back and play for Tottenham’, he did — and he played for England, too.

He said, ‘Kane, no, he’ll never be good enough to play for Tottenham’, but he said at the function, ‘Shows you what I knew about football!’



To be fair, I don’t think any of us saw him going on to become the best centre-forward in the world, which he is.

And he should now win the Ballon d’Or.

He was a boy, like Frank Lampard, who would practise after training for an hour, every day, with Jermain Defoe, shooting, finishing, practising, wanting to be a success.

“I gave him his senior debut at Spurs in a Europa League qualifier in 2011 against Hearts.



Last 10 Ballon d'Or winners 2025 – Ousmane Dembele

2024 – Rodri

2023 – Lionel Messi

2022 – Karim Benzema

2021 – Lionel Messi

“Our progression to the group stage was all but secure following a 5-0 victory in the first leg in Edinburgh.

“We got a penalty, and he’s only a kid, and he grabbed the ball and he wanted to take it, but he actually missed it!

“That shows what he was like — you had all those fantastic players in that team — but he didn’t care.

“He has remained humble, and he’s got time for everybody. He’s a fantastic human being. Really genuine.”

TIM SHERWOOD

Didn’t hesitate to give Harry Kane his first ­Premier League start.



Emmanuel Adebayor was a big player on big money — who we had signed from Manchester City.

Roberto Soldado, the top goalscorer in Spain, had come to Tottenham for a record fee.

He had a lot of traffic in his way. We know how many goals Jermain Defoe scored in the Prem.



But I judged everyone on a level playing field.

I watched Harry every day in training and decided the time was right to give him the opportunity.

I knew he wouldn’t be fazed by it.

He almost looked at me when I told him he was going to play against ­Sunderland on a Monday as if to say, ‘about time!’

I knew there wasn’t any danger of him going home and not ­sleeping properly.



He backed his ability and needed someone to back him too. I gave him that little bit of love he needed.

He took his opportunity with both hands.

A lot of people talk to me about Harry Kane’s failed loans. I don’t see any of them as failures.

They were better development pathways than playing with the Under-21s.



I always felt we needed him to go out and play competitive football.

It was the environment of meaning something.

The boys he played with at Orient needed to pay their mortgages.

He’s about the team before himself. That’s why everyone loves him.

If I asked him, he would pick winning the Champions League this season with Bayern Munich over the Ballon d’Or.



He’s just a model ­professional and that is why Alan Shearer is ­quaking in his boots.

I think he will eventually look for a team that might win trophies in England.

He wants to come back to beat that Shearer’s Prem goalscoring record.

Because of his professionalism and durability, I think he would be able to.

Sports.title: Sean Dyche ‘lined up for Premier League return’ after eight months out as manager on brink of being sacked

SEAN DYCHE could be handed a surprise Premier League lifeline as Crystal Palace consider making a change in the dugout.

The 55-year-old has been without a club since being axed by Nottingham Forest in February but is now being tipped to make a comeback in South London.



According to The Telegraph, Dyche is high on Palace’s list of potential replacements for Pierre Sage, who is facing an uncertain future following another miserable result.

The Eagles were booed off by their own fans after Newcastle cruised to a 2-0 victory at Selhurst Park.



Will Osula broke the deadlock just two minutes after the restart before Harvey Barnes doubled the visitors’ lead.

It was another afternoon to forget for Sage, whose side were battered 5-0 by bitter rivals Brighton the previous weekend.

And the Frenchman’s troubles are mounting, with Palace sitting just one point above the drop zone after winning only two of their opening eight league games.

The Eagles have also shipped a staggering 19 goals in those matches, giving them the worst defensive record in the division.

Sage, 47, only arrived in the summer to replace Oliver Glasner, who had guided Palace to FA Cup and Europa Conference League glory.

Dyche also faces competition from former Tottenham and Brentford boss Thomas Frank, while ex-Ipswich boss Kieran McKenna could also contend for the Eagles job.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Dyche, meanwhile, could offer some much-needed experience after spending almost a decade at Burnley, where he earned two promotions and even secured European football on a shoestring budget.

He also helped Everton beat the drop before his brief spell at Forest ended after just 114 days.

But Sage remains in charge for now and faces a huge test against Tottenham next weekend, with Liverpool also on the horizon before the international break.

Sports.title: Incredible moment goalkeeper steps up and scores late free-kick as subs pour onto pitch to celebrate
Sports.content:
