World.title: Bayern beat Freiburg to reclaim top spot as Kompany remains hospitalised
World.content:
Bayern Munich’s English forward #09 Harry Kane (C) and team mates stand in front of the fans after the German first division Bundesliga football match between SC Freiburg and FC Bayern Munich in Freiburg, south-western Germany, on October 25, 2026. (Photo by THOMAS KIENZLE / AFP) / DFL REGULATIONS PROHIBIT ANY USE OF PHOTOGRAPHS AS IMAGE SEQUENCES AND/OR QUASI-VIDEO

Bayern Munich reclaimed top spot in the Bundesliga with a 3-1 win at Freiburg on Sunday, days after coach Vincent Kompany was hospitalised when he collapsed at training.

Bayern were missing several first-team players and Kompany, but cruised to a two-goal lead at half-time with Dayot Upamecano and Serge Gnabry scoring.

Freiburg pulled one back and were pushing for a point in stoppage time when goalkeeper Mio Backhaus was caught out up the field, allowing Michael Olise to slide the ball into an empty net.

Kompany remains in hospital and is being treated for a mystery virus, with Bayern saying Saturday the coach is likely to be out for “days, not weeks”.

“I just opened my phone to a message from Vince saying ‘well done’ and he was happy,” assistant coach Aaron Danks told DAZN.

“I just replied saying ‘brilliant — now go rest’. I sent him a kissing emoji, so hopefully he rests up.”

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl gave an update on Kompany’s condition.

“He’s stable. He no longer has a headache. He’s now undergoing a thorough examination. Everything is being handled,” he said.

“There’s no diagnosis, nothing final yet.”

With victory Bayern leapfrogged Borussia Dortmund to top the table ahead of the duo’s clash in Munich next week.

Harry Kane had a close-range effort saved late in the second half but failed to find the net a day before the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, with the England captain among the favourites.

Bayern arrived in the Black Forest after a tumultuous few days which left them lacking leaders. With coach Kompany still in hospital after collapsing on Friday, Englishman Danks was in the dugout.

The visitors were also without injured captain Manuel Neuer, Luis Diaz, Jamal Musiala, Aleksandar Pavlovic and Kim Min-jae, while midfielder and Germany captain Joshua Kimmich was on bereavement leave due to the sudden death of his father.

Bayern were in the unusual position of sitting back and absorbing pressure as Freiburg pushed, but took the lead after 16 minutes when Upamecano started and finished a length-of-the-field counter.

The France defender won possession near his own box, played a one-two with Olise before thundering goalwards and sending a cool shot past Backhaus.

Bayern doubled up just before the break when Gnabry latched onto a Nathaniel Brown pass and nutmegged Backhaus to score.

With 10 minutes remaining, Kane stung Backhaus’s palms from close range and the hosts went on an immediate counter, forcing Tom Bischof into conceding an own goal.

The goal sparked Freiburg to life and Bayern ‘keeper Jonas Urbig needed to make crucial saves from Igor Matanovic in the dying moments.

With Freiburg and Backhaus pushing high, Olise won possession and scored to wrap up the victory.

– Hoffenheim hit 1,000 mark –

Hoffenheim scored three goals in the final 11 minutes, including the 1,000th league goal in their history, as they snapped Bayer Leverkusen’s six-game winning streak with a 3-0 home victory.

Hoffenheim, who beat Lyon by the same scoreline in the Europa League on Thursday, have now won three in a row.

The best chance of the opening half fell to former Leverkusen forward Adam Hlozek when he rattled the post with 38 minutes gone.

With the match looking headed for a scoreless draw, Leverkusen captain Edmond Tapsoba swept Fisnik Asllani’s ankle while defending a cross, with the referee pointing to the spot after a VAR review.

Andrej Kramaric’s 79th-minute penalty was the milestone goal and put Hoffenheim on track for victory.

With Leverkusen pushing for an equaliser, Hoffenheim broke on the counter and Alexander Prass scored, but he picked up a second yellow for removing his shirt in celebration, before leaving the pitch slapping himself on the forehead in dismay.

Max Moerstedt added a third despite the one-man disadvantage in the sixth minute of stoppage time.

Vanguard News

World.title: Summit Calls for Women’s Inclusion in Water Policy Decisions
World.content:
Policy advocates and cultural leaders have called for greater representation of women in water governance and budgetary decisions in Nigeria.

They urged institutions to move beyond token participation to give women meaningful decision-making power.

The call was made at the UNFPA Office in Copenhagen during a multimedia exhibition titled ‘Stories of a Broken Water Cycle’, organised by the Lokoja Dialogues Climate Initiative.

Featuring creative expressions, panel sessions and community perspectives from regions including Argungu, the exhibition highlighted how failing water infrastructure disproportionately affects women’s health, privacy, menstrual hygiene and economic mobility.

The summit was attended by prominent figures, including the Head of the UN Women Nordic Liaison Office, Sarah Brun; UNFPA Nordic Representative, Ulla E. Muller; Nigeria’s Ambassador to Denmark, Sweden and Finland, Lola Akande; Polly Alakija and Adwoa Edun, both co-founders of Lokoja Dialogues Climate.

Speaking during a panel session on gender and governance, advocate Patricia Emmanuel said women must be included in decisions on water management.

“We cannot fix the broken water cycle with half the population excluded from the solution. We must move women from water carriers to water governance,” she said.

Panellists criticised development models that treat women as passive participants in consultative workshops rather than as leaders capable of managing resources and influencing budget allocations.

“When we talk about inclusion, women are often just invited to participate in a roundtable, conference, or workshop, and at the end, it stops there,” speaker Flora Asieri said, calling for institutional reforms beyond superficial representation.

Sarah Brun of UN Women also stressed the connection between visibility, political influence and budgetary allocations.

“What remains invisible remains unfunded. The real question for us here is whether our institutions are prepared to listen to them, but also to share our power,” Brun said.

In her opening remarks, Polly Alakija, Trustee and CEO of Lokoja Dialogues, observed that equitable access to water in Nigeria had worsened over the past 37 years since she first arrived in the country.

She emphasised that women’s daily experiences of water insecurity should directly inform government spending and utility management.

By bringing community perspectives into discussions with policymakers, the Copenhagen exhibition seeks to promote women’s participation in shaping water policies and improving national water security.

World.title: NAF Spends Nearly N18 Billion on Jet A-1 Fuel in 10 Months to Support National Security Operations
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has spent nearly N18 billion on Jet A-1 aviation fuel between November 2025 and September 2026 to sustain air operations in support of national security, the Service has revealed.

Security and aviation experts said the expenditure underscores the critical role of aviation fuel in powering combat missions, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, as well as air mobility operations across the country.

In a statement highlighting the NAF’s operational successes to commemorate the first year anniversary of the incumbent Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, the Director of Public Relations and Information, Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed: “Between November 2025 and September 2026, the NAF recorded over 6,100 flying hours and more than 2,900 sorties, consuming close to 10 million litres of Jet A-1 fuel in support of national security operations.

“These missions encompassed precision air strikes, armed reconnaissance, surveillance, close air support and other tasks designed to degrade hostile elements, disrupt their freedom of action and enhance the effectiveness of surface forces.

“Central to this effort has been intelligence-led mission planning, with operations guided by actionable intelligence, defined objectives and assessments of mission outcomes. The emphasis remains on ensuring that every sortie serves a clear operational purpose and contributes meaningfully to national security.”

Air Commodore Ejodame said the NAF had recorded significant operational, personnel, training, infrastructure and force modernisation milestones under the leadership of Air Marshal Aneke as he approaches his first anniversary in office on 30 October 2026.

He stressed that, guided by the CAS’s command philosophy of sustaining a highly motivated, professional and mission-ready force capable of delivering decisive airpower effects in synergy with surface forces, the Service had pursued a focused transformation agenda anchored on operational effectiveness, personnel welfare, technological advancement and institutional accountability.

Recognising personnel as the Service’s most valuable asset, Air Marshal Aneke has placed welfare at the heart of his leadership philosophy, encapsulated in the principle of ‘Welfare for Enhanced Warfare.’

“This approach recognises that adequately supported, professionally developed and highly motivated personnel are essential to sustained operational effectiveness. Accordingly, the Service has pursued improvements in personnel allowances and medical support, alongside the provision of accommodation and the development of supporting infrastructure to enhance living and working conditions across its formations,” he said.

Ejodame stressed that these initiatives, complemented by the reactivation of welfare airlift services for personnel in frontline operational theatres, reflected a deliberate commitment to strengthening morale, improving the well-being of personnel and their families, and enhancing readiness to discharge the NAF’s constitutional responsibilities of defending Nigeria’s territorial integrity and protecting its citizens.

He further disclosed that, in recognition of professional service and career progression, 57 senior officers had been promoted to the ranks of Air Vice Marshal and Air Commodore, while 1,534 senior non-commissioned officers and 1,936 non-commissioned officers had advanced to higher ranks.

In addition, more than 550 personnel had participated in international training and professional engagements, while over 6,000 had received local training, strengthening specialised competencies, technical proficiency and leadership capacity.

Beyond personnel development, the NAF has also advanced efforts to modernise its fleet and improve aircraft availability.

Ejodame said, “In September 2026, the Service received five additional helicopters comprising three AW-109 Trekker Type B helicopters and two H125 helicopters, expanding its operational flexibility and support capacity. Beyond these deliveries, the Service is pursuing a broader acquisition programme that includes 12 AH-1Z attack helicopters and other planned aircraft and unmanned aerial systems intended to strengthen airlift, combat, training, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities.

“Maintenance and fleet regeneration efforts have also progressed, including the reactivation and upgrade of six L-39ZA aircraft in Slovakia and Nigeria, as well as the ongoing Periodic Depot Maintenance of a C-130 aircraft in Portugal. These efforts complement investments in technical support, indigenous upgrades and emerging aviation technologies.”

He added that safety, accountability and the responsible employment of airpower remained important pillars of the CAS’s transformation agenda.

According to the NAF spokesperson, the establishment of an Operational and Safety Audit Committee is intended to support independent assessments of operational, engineering and armament units. Meanwhile, a strengthened Safety Management System promotes leadership engagement, proactive risk management and a data-driven safety culture.

The Service is also advancing Civilian Harm Mitigation and Response through dedicated structures, standardised training, and enhanced assessment and investigation capabilities, he said.

“Plans to establish an Open-Source Intelligence Centre further reflect the drive to improve situational awareness and operational planning through better exploitation of available information and emerging technologies.

“Infrastructure development and indigenous capability remain central to sustaining these gains. The NAF has approved 284 infrastructure projects, of which 145 have been completed and 139 remain ongoing. Covering residential accommodation, academic and medical facilities, administrative and operational infrastructure, roads, power, water supply and recreational facilities, these projects are designed to improve personnel welfare and strengthen the Service’s operational and institutional capacity.

“Complementing these investments are local production initiatives involving Aircraft Release Device 863 impulse release cartridges, a 250-kilogram bomb-loading trolley, and the development and ground testing of locally produced 57-millimetre rockets. Community-focused healthcare, educational and other special projects have also continued to strengthen civil-military relations and public confidence,” the statement further revealed.

As Air Marshal Aneke approaches his first anniversary in office, the NAF remains focused on translating investments in personnel, platforms, training, technology and infrastructure into tangible operational results.

Ejodame said that, through stronger joint operations, strategic partnerships, improved maintenance, professional development and the responsible employment of airpower, the Service continued to pursue greater readiness and effectiveness in addressing Nigeria’s security challenges.

He said the objective was not simply to expand capability but to sustain a professional, accountable and responsive force prepared to address evolving threats. He concluded that the enduring commitment remained clear: stronger airpower, safer skies and a more secure Nigeria.

However, the statement was silent on air mishaps, unintended killings of unarmed and Innocent civilians during air operations, and the number of personnel who paid the supreme price in defence of the nation within the period under review.

World.title: Ishowo Urges Kwara to Convert KWASUED to Medical Varsity to Address Shortage of Medical Doctors
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

A Kwara-based Public Affairs Analyst, Comrade Ishowo Olanrewaju, weekend called on the Kwara State government to urgently convert the recently established Kwara State University of Education (KWASUED) to a specialised medical university to address the worsening and chronic shortage of doctors and other healthcare professionals in the state hospitals.

He therefore cited the Bayelsa Medical University in Bayelsa State, the state University of Medicine and Applied Sciences in Enugu State, and the University of Medical Sciences in Ondo State as existing examples.

Ishowo made the call in Ilorin while speaking with newsmen on the sidelines of the incessant strike embarked upon by medical doctors in the state hospitals.

Ishowo however expressed concern over the shortage of medical personnel in the state, noting that the available doctors were already overstretched and overwhelmed by the sheer volume of patients they were required to attend to daily.

He lamented that this situation made industrial action embarked upon by the doctors particularly troubling.

He argued that the state government should have prioritised a medical university over a university of education, insisting that Kwara’s more pressing challenge was the severe shortage of healthcare professionals rather than educators.

According to him, existing institutions, including the University of Ilorin, Kwara State University (KWASU) and Al-Hikmah University, already have faculties of education that produce graduates annually.

He added that several public and private colleges of education across the state also train teachers.

“The number of educators we produce far exceeds what we need or can employ. Our challenge is not a lack of teachers. It is a dangerous shortage of doctors, nurses and other medical professionals.

“That reality should have informed the government’s decision when it was considering establishing a new university,” he said.

Ishowo maintained that establishing a specialised medical university would help build a steady supply of doctors and other healthcare professionals to meet the state’s needs and serve other parts of the country.

“To address the persistent shortage of doctors and other medical personnel, I am calling for the conversion of KWASUED into a specialised medical institution,” he said.

He also proposed scholarships for Kwara indigenes admitted to the proposed institution, with beneficiaries required to sign a five-year service bond to work in the state after graduation before seeking opportunities elsewhere.

Ishowo said the arrangement would help retain locally trained medical professionals and strengthen the state’s healthcare system.

“Let the government provide scholarships for Kwara indigenes who want to study medicine and other related health courses, and bond them to serve the state for five years post-graduation.

“This is how we begin to systematically solve the shortage of medical personnel that has plagued us for years,” Ishowo noted.

He further stated that some state governments across Nigeria had already recognised the value of dedicated medical universities and taken steps to establish them.

According to Ishowo, “The Lagos State government is also pursuing plans to establish a standard one university of medicine and health sciences to tackle the doctor and healthcare worker deficit in the state.

“These states identified a need and responded to it strategically. Kwara can and should do the same. The conversion of KWASUED into a specialized medical university will be a response to a documented crisis that is costing Kwarans their health and their lives.”

World.title: The Convergence Supports Creative Enterprise, Promotes Nigerian Art, Says Adenowo
World.content:
The Convergence: The Iconic Architect & the Icons of Art, an exhibition celebrating the intersection of architecture and visual art, has concluded successfully in Lagos, highlighting the role of creative platforms in supporting artistic enterprise, promoting Nigerian art and strengthening connections across the creative industry.

Presented by AD Consulting in partnership with Ecobank Nigeria, at the Ecobank Pan African Centre (EPAC), Lagos, it brought together renowned artists, architects, collectors, patrons and members of the public to celebrate Nigeria’s creative heritage and explore opportunities for collaboration across the creative ecosystem.

Speaking at the exhibition, Olajumoke Adenowo said The Convergence provided a platform for meaningful engagement between architecture and visual art while fostering stronger relationships across the creative industry.

“The Convergence provided a platform for enlightening conversations on architecture and visual art, strengthening connections among architects, artists, collectors, patrons and the wider public. Beyond celebrating artistic excellence, it underscores the importance of supporting creative enterprise and encouraging greater appreciation of Nigerian art,” Adenowo said.

The exhibition featured projects from Adenowo’s 32 years of architectural practice alongside works by distinguished Nigerian artists, including Abiodun Olaku, Duke Asidere, Edosa Oguigo, Bunmi Babatunde, Kehinde Adewuyi, Tayo Quaye, Alex Nwokolo, Kassi Nathalie, Dotun Popoola, Steve Ekpenisi, Collins Abinoro and Joshua Nmesirionye, among others.

Their works showcased the depth and diversity of Nigerian artistic expression, demonstrating how architecture and visual art can preserve cultural heritage, inspire innovation and shape contemporary perspectives.

Head of Marketing and Corporate Communications at Ecobank Nigeria, Austen Osokpor, said the bank’s support for the exhibition reflected its commitment to creating platforms that celebrate African creativity and connect talent with opportunities.

“Art and culture are important expressions of our identity and powerful platforms for connecting people, ideas and opportunities. By supporting initiatives such as The Convergence, Ecobank is helping to showcase Nigerian talent, encourage wider appreciation of our creative heritage and demonstrate the potential of the creative industry to contribute to enterprise development and national growth,” Osokpor said.

He maintained that: “The exhibition also highlighted the broader contribution of the creative industry to national development. By promoting cultural preservation, encouraging innovation and supporting creative enterprise, initiatives of this nature can generate economic opportunities, strengthen Nigeria’s cultural identity and enhance the country’s visibility on the global stage.”

The successful conclusion of The Convergence underscores the value of collaboration among artists, cultural institutions, collectors and corporate organisations in building a vibrant creative ecosystem that celebrates Nigerian art, supports creative enterprise and contributes to sustainable economic growth.

World.title: Deputy Speaker Kalu Meets Tompolo, Strategises For Tinubu’s 2027 Victory
World.content:
Deputy Speaker, House of Representatives and Deputy Director-General, South II, of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC PCC), Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu, has met with High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, to discuss strategies for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 general elections.

The meeting came on the heels of the commissioning of the national secretariat of PBAT Door-to-Door in Abuja on Friday.

It focused on grassroots mobilization and the consolidation of support for President Tinubu across the South-South and South-East geopolitical zones.

The strategic meeting also touched on enhancing a joint operational framework for voter sensitization, youth engagement, and ward-level coordination in the States under the South II Directorate.

Kalu described the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement as a critical vehicle for the 2027 project, noting that the election would be won at the polling unit and household level.

The Deputy Speaker said that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has taken bold, reform-driven decisions that are stabilizing the economy and securing our nation.

He added the campaign trail will ensure that the message of the Renewed Hope reaches every doorstep, emphasizing that an alliance with Tompolo as Convener of the Movement is strategic.

Earlier at the commissioning of the national secretariat, the Deputy Speaker said that President Tinubu’s commitment to a stronger, more productive and inclusive Nigeria was evident in initiatives such as the student loan programme through NELFUND, which provides financial support for eligible young Nigerians to pursue higher education, and the establishment of regional development commissions

He also expressed profound gratitude to the President for assenting to the South-East Development Commission Act, which he said was an important step towards addressing reconstruction, infrastructure and development priorities in the South-East.

“As a representative of Bende Federal Constituency, I particularly appreciate President Tinubu’s assent to the South-East Development Commission Act, an important step towards addressing reconstruction, infrastructure and development priorities in our region”, Kalu said.

Commending Tompolo for the initiative, commitment and resources in establishing the national secretariat, Kalu charged members of the Movement to strengthen its grassroots structure to mobilise support across the 774 Local Government Areas and 8,809 wards for President Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, by taking the initiatives to the nooks and crannies of the country.

He also urged the Movement to embody the highest standards of democratic participation by listening to citizens’ concerns.

“Nigeria benefits when citizens can exchange ideas peacefully and participate in public life with confidence and dignity,” Kalu said.

World.title: Falana to Headline Screening of Documentary on Osun LG Crisis
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana (SAN), is set to deliver the keynote address at the public screening of ‘LG Billions in the Dark’, an investigative documentary on the prolonged local government leadership crisis in Osun State, scheduled to hold on October 29, at the University of Lagos (UNILAG).

The documentary, produced by DevReporting, examines the crisis and its implications for public finance, accountability and service delivery at the grassroots.

The screening will be chaired by the Publisher of Premium Times and Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), Dapo Olorunyomi.

Falana will speak on the theme, ‘Accountability, Resources and Citizen Voices: Building Local Governments that Work for the People,’ addressing local government autonomy, public resource management, citizens’ rights and accountability.

The event will also feature a panel discussion involving public officials, civil society leaders, governance experts and academics.

The panellists include Osun State Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Dosu Babatunde; Executive Director of the Resource Centre for Human Rights and Civic Education (CHRICED), Zikirullahi Ibrahim; and Executive Director of Spaces for Change, Victoria Ibezim-Ohaeri.

Others are Head of Tracka at BudgIT, Joshua Osiyemi; a lecturer in the Department of Political Science at UNILAG, Vera Amaechi; and Senior Multimedia Strategist at DevReporting, Bukola Adebayo.

DevReporting Team Lead, Mojeed Alabi, said the documentary reflected the organisation’s commitment to public-interest journalism and investigating governance issues affecting citizens.

He said the event would also feature the unveiling of the Development Reporting Africa Foundation (DRAF), a non-profit initiative established to strengthen development reporting, promote public engagement and advance accountability across African communities.

A fundraising initiative will be launched to support the foundation’s work.

Alabi added: “DevReporting is developing a civic education and youth engagement programme to take the documentary to tertiary institutions across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones.”

The initiative, he noted, will feature campus screenings, training, mentorship and youth-led accountability projects aimed at improving undergraduates’ understanding of local government administration, public finance and citizen participation.

“Local governments are responsible for essential services, including primary healthcare, sanitation and basic infrastructure. However, concerns over financial control, political interference and council autonomy have continued to feature prominently in debates about grassroots governance,” Alabi stated.

The documentary was produced with support from the Royal Norwegian Embassy through the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development.

World.title: FCE Yola Graduates 3,555 At 16th Convocation As Stakeholders Renew Demand for Upgrade to Varsity of Education
World.content:
Daji Sani in Yola

The Federal College of Education, Yola, weekend held its 16th combined convocation ceremony for the 2023/2024 and 2024/2025 academic sessions, with 3,555 graduands awarded the Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE), as stakeholders renewed calls for the 52-year-old institution to be upgraded to a University of Education.

The ceremony, which comes two years after the last convocation in November 2024, was attended by Adamawa State Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri; Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa; Chairman of the Governing Council, Mr. Saheed O. Johnson; the Lamido of Adamawa, Dr. Muhammadu Barkindo Aliyu Mustapha; Provost, Dr. Mohammed Usman Degereji and other dignitaries.

Stakeholders at the event said the college, which has clocked 52 years since its establishment as FATC in 1974 and currently runs degree programmes in affiliation with universities, has earned the status for upgrade.

They appealed to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to, as a matter of urgency, upgrade the college to a full-fledged University of Education to meet the growing demand for teacher education in the North-east.

In his welcome address, Johnson described the convocation as a significant milestone in the history of the institution.

He noted that despite daunting challenges facing teacher-producing institutions in Nigeria, FCE Yola has sustained quality delivery, timely release of results and consistency in its academic calendar.

Johnson commended the Federal Government under President Tinubu for far-reaching education reforms, particularly the National Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) and the dual mandate policy for Colleges of Education.

He said without the support of the Federal Ministry of Education, TETFund and the National Commission for Colleges of Education, the college could not have recorded progress in infrastructure, employment, promotions, new programmes and accreditations.

Charging the graduands, the council chairman congratulated them and urged them to remain worthy ambassadors of the college.

He said they should not be distracted by economic crisis, infrastructure deficit, climate change and job deficits, but should deploy the confidence and tools acquired to confront poverty, deprivation, hunger and intolerance.

The Provost, Dr. Degereji, announced that the graduands comprise 1,818 for 2024 and 1,737 for 2025, found worthy in character and learning, with many earning classified prizes.

He said the ceremony is the second since he assumed office in 2022 and described the output as a great addition to the teaching profession in Adamawa, the North-east and Nigeria.

Reviewing his four-year stewardship, Degereji said the college has been repositioned for greater productivity since 2022.

He listed the achievements to include establishment of a Students’ Digital Hub for certificates and transcripts, improved ICT facilities, renovation of 70 per cent of the hostels, reintroduction of common-room and cafeteria services, and construction and renovation of lecture theatres, laboratories and offices.

He added that management introduced annual staff dialogue and productivity awards since 2023, reinvigorated capacity building, entrenched fiscal discipline, established an entrepreneurship skills and career service centre, and reduced local debt from over N100 million inherited in 2022 to less than N1 million in 2026.

He thanked the Federal Government, TETFund, NEDC and the Adamawa State Government for their interventions.

Governor Fintiri, in his address, reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to revitalizing education through pro-people policies, increased funding and institutional strengthening.

He said his government has improved access through investment in schools, strengthened scholarship programmes, teacher training and ICT programmes, with priority allocation to education in the 2026 budget.

The governor disclosed that his administration is constructing Model Science Secondary Schools in each zone and has implemented the Teacher Recruitment, Deployment and Retention Policy to align with 21st-century goals.

He lauded the college’s history of producing over 40,000 teachers in 50 years, assured the audience of continued support for federal tertiary institutions, adding that his government remains committed to UNESCO’s 26 per cent budget target despite insurgency challenges.

On his part, the Minister of Education commended the Governing Council, management and staff for sustaining the mandate, describing strong institutions as products of effective leadership.

He highlighted NELFUND, the dual mandate that now enables FCE Yola to award degrees, and disclosed that the college emerged best among Colleges of Education in judicious utilisation of the 2022-2023 Needs Assessment intervention.

The minister, while acknowledging the stakeholders’ demand, maintained that there is no need for a University of Education as the dual mandate already empowers the college to award degrees and do more in the future.

He listed other reforms including TVET across 25 trade areas, the Tertiary Institution Staff Support Fund offering zero-interest loans up to N10 million through the Bank of Industry (BoI), and the Student Venture Grant, urging the college to build partnerships with the private sector and development partners to complement government funding.

The ceremony ended with congratulations to graduands and their parents, with speakers urging them to prove their worth through positive societal impact, while the Council Chairman thanked the Adamawa State Government, the Lamido of Adamawa, neighbouring states, communities and parents for their support and wished guests safe journey.

World.title: Enugu Catholic Diocese Launches Initiative To Hold Public Officials Accountable
World.content:
Gideon Arinze in Enugu

The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has launched an initiative to promote good governance, civic engagement and voter education, while encouraging citizens to demand accountability and quality representation from elected officials.

The initiative, known as Church for Community Care and Good Governance (CCGG), was launched Sunday by the Catholic Institute for Development, Justice and Peace (CIDJAP).

Speaking at the flag-off ceremony, the Project Lead, Rev. Fr. Longinus Ugonwa, said the initiative would connect the church with citizens’ everyday concerns, including education, healthcare, roads, security, employment, youth development and responsible leadership.

He said CCGG was neither a political party nor a platform for promoting or attacking political personalities, but was committed to truth, responsible citizenship and the common good.

According to him, the initiative would help citizens understand public issues, ask informed questions, examine evidence and make responsible decisions rather than dictate what they should think.

“CCGG would also promote constructive engagement between citizens and political leaders,” he said, adding that governance worked better when citizens were informed and institutions remained open to dialogue.

He said the initiative would use podcasts, radio programmes, interviews, documentaries, social media and community engagement to listen to citizens, examine public concerns, recognise genuine progress and encourage practical solutions.

In his remarks, the Chairman of Enugu East Local Government Area, Beloved-Dan Anike, said the church could not separate itself from governance.

He expressed his readiness to partner with CCGG to achieve its objectives.

World.title: Cats to burps: The Kiffness trolls President Trump [video]
World.content:
The Kiffness has spoofed President Donald Trump's burp. Images via YouTube screenshot

The Kiffness has done it again with another catchy jingle after by putting his unique spin on viral sound – this time poking fun at President Donald Trump burping mid-sentence.

The quirky artist has amassed millions of views with his samples of everything from animal sounds to singing children.

THE KIFFNESS TROLLS TRUMP’S BURP

The Kiffness’s latest music offering has poked fun at viral video of President Donald Trump burping mid-sentence.



The US leader was speaking at a campaign rally in South Carolina, in which he supported a local senator.

During his address, the 80-year-old appeared to loudl belch. Without excusing himself, he continued talking.

The video quickly went viral with many expressing disgust and concern.

Adding his spin was Cape Tow muso, The Kiffness who managed to turn the president’s ill-mannered actions into a catchy tune.

The “remix” was posted on Facebook, receiving hundreds and thousands of views, and almost 10 000 comments.

EATING THE CATS

It’s not the first time, The Kiffness has spoofed comments made by Trump.



Last year, the outspoken muso raised nearly R2 million for an SPCA shelter in the US from the proceeds of his catchy song Eating The Cats, featuring the then President-elect.

The song sampled the incoming statesman’s viral comments about immigrants, particularly Haitian people, whom he claimed eat domesticated animals.

An official music video has over 14 million YouTube views and many more millions on other streaming sites.

World.title: Sarah Langa gushes over Sacha: ‘Love of my life’

Sarah Langa and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu are Instagram feed official. pic.twitter.com/lYtzgMnDsG — Precious Shange (@PreciousShange) October 21, 2026

World.title: St Stithians murder-suicide: Disturbing new claims revealed
World.content:
St Stithians teens Caeron Waldeck-Cooks and Ethan Coetzee died in a reported murder suicide. Image via FB

A disturbing new claim in the St Stithians murder-suicide alleges that Ethan Coetzee displayed controlling and abusive behaviour towards his girlfriend, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, sending well over 750 texts a day.

The teens’ bodies were discovered at a Mpumalanga lodge in August following a hiking trip.

Cameron, 17, allegedly died from strangulation/suffocation, while it has been reported that Ethan, 19, took his own life.

‘ABUSIVE’ RELATIONSHIP COMES UNDER THE SPOTLIGHT

Over the weekend, new details in the St Stithians murder-suicide investigation came to light.

The report shared information about the couples’s alleged toxic relationship, with claims that Ethan Coetzee, a 2025 matriculant, bombarded his Grade 11 girlfriend over 22 000 WhatsApp texts in a four week period – over 785 texts a day.

The messages, sent from early morning to late at night, included thousands of declarations of love.

They also included demands, questions, and accusations of a reported jealous and controlling nature.

Ethan reportedly demanded to monitor Cameron’s study sessions and insisted she “behave like a wife”.

The phone records shared by Cameron’s family representatives claimed that she had ended their relationship in early July.

A few weeks later, the couple was found dead during a hiking trip at a holiday lodge in the town of Sabie.

Subsequent autopsies indicated Cameron died by strangulation/suffocation, while Ethan died by suicide.

Police initially opened an inquest, but later confirmed that they were investigating a murder-suicide.

In recent weeks, the Waldeck-Cooks’ have expressed their concerns about police ignoring phone records, claiming that the deceased’s cellphones had been returned without a full forensic data download on the same day their bodies had been discovered.

COERCIVE CONTROL, SAYS GBV ACTIVIST

Meanwhile, GBV activist Bella Monsoon has suggested that the relationship between the teens exhibited signs of “coercive control”

In previous reports, it emerged that Ethan Coetzee, a 2025 matriculant who played in the first-team rugby for the Gauteng school, was a “jealous” and “controlling” boyfriend who had access to Cameron Waldeck Cooks’ social media accounts and phone.

Ethan had reportedly become “enraged” at his girlfriend, who had befriended male learners at school. He also allegedly withdrew from studying at Stellenbosch University, as he did not want to be away from her.

Monsoon said of his behaviour: “Coercive control does not just exist physically; it can be digital too. Monitoring messages, demanding passwords, policing who someone speaks to, tracking their activity, becoming angry over ordinary interactions.

She continued: “None of these behaviours automatically means somebody will become violent, but together they can form a wide pattern of coercive control. And when a young woman loses her life and circumstances are already being investigated as murder, digital evidence, relating to control, intimidation or relationship dynamic can be incredibly important”.

World.title: How Kaizer Chiefs can start winning trophies again, club legend explains
World.content:
Former Kaizer Chiefs midfielder Willard Katsande has identified ways Amakhosi can go back to winning trophies.

In the past 11 years, the Soweto giants have only won one trophy. With another trophyless season looking likely, Katsande has given his thoughts on how Amakhosi can return to the top again.

“For me I just feel like they just need to have consistency. When you want to compete with the big boys and you want to be part and parcel of that top three we were last season, we need to be consistent,” Katsande told KickOff.



“Each and every game we need to be competent, you know the culture of Kaizer Chiefs, you just need to win, no matter you are having a bad day at the office but you need to win.”

“Salt and Pepper” explained the importance for the club winning trophies.

Chiefs finding it difficult to win trophies

“For people to fall in love with Chiefs is about winning and winning trophies, so those guys need to know where they are, the coach also needs to know that the people are thirsty to win silverware and bring back the club where it is supposed to be,” Katsande added.



Amakhosi crashed out of the CAF Confederation Cup on Friday and on Tuesday, they host TS Galaxy in the Carling Knockout round of 16. Failure to win the match, could see Chiefs only banking on the Nedbank Cup next year.

With Mamelodi Sundowns and Orlando Pirates looking strong, it remains unlikely that Amakhosi will win a trophy in the near future.

Can Amakhosi steal one trophy this season?

World.title: Dakar Rally 2027 to be moved from Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Next year's Dakar Rally will be relocated from Saudi Arabia over safety concerns. Image: Giuseppe CACACE / AFP

The 2027 Dakar Rally will be moved from Saudi Arabia “following recent developments in the region”, organisers said on Sunday, after repeated attacks on the kingdom by Yemen’s Houthis.

“Dakar 2027 will go ahead. The 2027 edition will take place in a different territory” but still be organised by ASO, which runs the Dakar along with Saudi Motorsport Company (SMC), read a statement from the organisers.

A new location will be announced in the “coming days”, it added.



Fallout from US-Iran war

It is the latest sporting event to be cancelled, postponed or relocated amid the fallout from the wider US-Iran war that erupted in February.

Saudi Arabia and the government it backs in Yemen have come under sustained attack in recent weeks from the Houthis as a years-long truce broke down in the summer, shifting the focus of the war.

Yemen’s civil war, pitting the Iran-backed Houthis against the Saudi-supported and internationally recognised government, had been dormant since a ceasefire in 2022, but reignited in July as the wider Middle East war roiled the region.

According to specialist media, the preferred option for next year’s Dakar would be a start in Spain with Morocco as the destination.

It would be the first time since 2007 that the gruelling multi-stage rally, created in 1978, returns to Africa.

The race, formerly called the Paris-Dakar, used to be staged from the French capital following a route to the Senegalese capital Dakar.



But security threats along its route in North Africa meant that from 2009 it was held in South America and from 2020 in Saudi Arabia.

Could return in 2028

Organisers said they intend to bring the rally back to Saudi Arabia in 2028 to celebrate its 50th edition.

This season’s Formula One grand prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the race in Bahrain was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia.

The final round of the World Rally Championship in Saudi Arabia next month has also been scrapped.

An exhibition tennis tournament due to feature Novak Djokovic, Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev has been postponed until late December.

The WTA Finals were also scheduled to be held in Riyadh next month but will instead take place at Indian Wells in the US.

The last two races of the F1 season in Qatar (November 29) and Abu Dhabi (December 6) are still on the calendar, as is the Qatar MotoGP next month, but they are the subject of intense internal debate.

New route impossible

Dakar Rally organisers had hoped to keep the 2027 race in Saudi Arabia by working on a new route in the northern part of the country.

But the latest strikes, including one targeting Riyadh airport this month, which killed 13 people and injured hundreds more, have rendered that impossible.

In recent weeks, Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure have reached a scale unprecedented since the start of the conflict in Yemen in 2014.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Penny Lebyane reflects on daughter’s matric dance [photos]
World.content:
Media personality Penny Lebyane recently melted hearts on Instagram after sharing heartfelt motherhood reflections and behind-the-scenes moments from her daughter’s matric dance.

PENNY LEBYANE REFLECTS ON DAUGHTER’S MATRIC DANCE

Tamuka, the daughter of Penny, looked absolutely stunning in her blue dress by Lufi D.

Her glamorous look was complemented by an elegant hairstyle and flawless makeup, while the last two photos showed her posing beside swanky cars.



In her heartfelt caption, Penny reflected on her daughter’s milestone and expressed immense pride in the person Tamuka has grown into.

She also acknowledged her supportive circle for holding her down throughout her motherhood journey.

“I have been trying to come to terms with the fact that this is where we are. We are here, my little heart in form #TamukaNakaThe1st. I am so proud of the amazing, beautiful being you are,” she began.

“Thank you to all the aunties and uncles who have held my hand through it all. l am nothing without you all, and you know yourselves,” she added.

CONGRATULATORY MESSAGES POUR IN

Ms Cassandra Gud: My goodness, how gorgeous is she? Congratulations on the milestone.
