World.title: Police: Signs of radicalization visible among younger teens
World.content:
Signs of radicalization are appearing in increasingly younger people and are already evident among 12- and 13-year-olds, said Pärtel Preinvalts, head of the radicalization prevention group at the Police and Border Guard Board's Northern Prefecture.

Preinvalts said the change in Estonia is not happening in isolation and can also be seen in other Western countries, including the United States.

"The age threshold is moving steadily downward in terms of young people's development. Whereas previously it was 15- and 16-year-olds, today it is 12- and 13-year-olds or even younger," Preinvalts said.

The number of violent crimes carried out by juveniles has risen over the last decade. There are fewer incidents such as shoplifting or vandalism and significantly more cases involving violence.

The proportion of juvenile crimes carried out against another person rose significantly from 2016 (27.5 percent) to 2022 (48.8 percent) Last year, the rate was recorded at 44.7 percent.

"Although the overall numbers may be falling, the proportion of crimes that have a much greater impact on victims and the community is increasing," Preinvalts said.

A sense of belonging

The head of the radicalization prevention group said young people often develop a sense of belonging through shared activities that may not initially appear to have anything to do with radicalization.

Many teenagers who join a group may not even realize what kind of gang they have joined until an adult explains it to them.

"Unfortunately, a recurring motive is so-called patriotism, which quite quickly turns into hatred," Preinvalts said. He added that, under the guise of patriotism and love of one's country, what often actually takes place is hostility toward minority groups and the seeking of conflict. This happens both in the media and in public spaces.

"It all starts online and quite soon moves into public spaces, for example through the distribution of stickers and other propaganda materials," Preinvalts said.

Democracies encourage civic activism regardless of age, he said, adding that a radical worldview and strongly defined views of the surrounding world are often part of a young person's development.

"Many grow out of it and pose no threat," Preinvalts added.

Glorification of violence

Radicalization becomes a problem when it is accompanied by the glorification of violence or, in the worst-case scenario, its use. Preinvalts said ideological influence has never been as accessible to young people as it is today.

"Content is often determined by algorithms, and after stumbling upon something a few times, a person may unknowingly become a consumer of material that gradually normalizes unlawful behavior," he explained.

"However, it is important to understand that thoughts and beliefs play an important role in maintaining democracy. We have a free society," the official continued.

Preinvalts added that the state cannot and does not want to interfere with people's beliefs, but it has a responsibility is to ensure the safety and security of all residents.

Ministry wants to stop repeat offenders

The Ministry of Justice is now looking for a service provider to help young people with extremist views avoid further offenses and return to education or the labor market. The ministry has announced a small-scale procurement with an estimated value of €40,000.

The service is aimed at young people aged 14 to 29 whose offenses are linked to extremist views or an interest in them. The goal is to reduce the risk of further similar offenses and support young people in distancing themselves from extremist views, developing social skills and reintegrating into society.

The counselor providing the service must have at least two years of experience working with young people or young people exhibiting risky behavior. They must also have knowledge of how extremist views and radicalization develop, including young people's need for belonging, identity crises and the spread of extremist ideologies online.

World.title: Estonia planning to send 'substantial number of locomotives' to Ukraine
World.content:
Estonia is planning to send a "substantial number" of locomotives to Ukraine to help replace those destroyed by Russia, Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) has said.

Tsahkna held a telephone call with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha last week and discussed the current situation in Ukraine, Russia's attacks, and the need for assistance this upcoming winter.

He said Ukraine must receive even "more extensive" practical assistance in the coming months.

"As Russia has targeted critical infrastructure, including the transport network, and has already destroyed or damaged 340 railway carriages this year, we are working to send a substantial number of locomotives to Ukraine. This will help keep the country's transport links operational even under the most difficult conditions," Tsahkna said.

No additional details were given in the press release.

However, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs told ERR's Russian portal on Thursday over 60 locomotives have been identified that could potentially be sent to Ukraine.

The ministry said a Ukrainian Railways expert group visited Estonia earlier this month to assess how the locomotives meet the needs of the Ukrainian railway. The Estonian side is awaiting the experts' response, after which it will continue to seek funding through international mechanisms.

Estonia will also provide Ukraine with an additional €10 million through NATO's PURL initiative, bringing the country's total contribution to €30 million.

Tsahkna also outlined the current situation in Ukraine: "In recent weeks, drone and missile attacks, along with power cuts affecting hundreds of thousands of people, have become part of everyday life in Ukraine. The number of civilian casualties rose by 85 percent in September, and more than 2,000 energy infrastructure facilities have been attacked since July. The conditions for serious peace negotiations will not exist until Russia changes its behaviour."

World.title: EKA graphic design students look 'beyond the veil' in new exhibition
World.content:
An exhibition by graphic design students inspired by an archive hidden in the basement of the Estonian Academy of Arts (EKA) library opened at the university's Billboard Gallery on Friday.

"Who is haunting the school walls, lurking beyond the veil? Hidden in the basement of the EKA library lies an archive of ghosts and restless spirits who are asking to be released. Using the archive as a starting point, the graphic design students have developed an exhibition for the EKA Billboard Gallery, which also became a publication and, finally, an exorcism. This, of course, meant that all working materials were haunted: everything was spooky," a press release says, explaining the exhibition.

Andrew Kuus-Hill, the curator of the exhibition, described the process: "We have enchanted 250 A3-sized prints, pasted them on the billboard, and with the phantoms by our side, performed an exorcism to set them free. Sorcerer hats will be provided on site."

The exhibition "Beyond the Veil" is open at the EKA Billboard Gallery on Kotzebue tänav in Tallinn until December 24.

World.title: Defense minister: Light fighter jets could be procured within 4 years
World.content:
Minister of Defense Martin Herem has said Estonia could need around a dozen light fighter jets to counter jet-powered attack drones, and a procurement could take up to four years.

The Baltic air forces do not have a single fighter jet between them, and NATO's Air Defense Mission monitors the region's skies instead.

Fighter jets cost between €15 million and €100 million each, and while Estonia has wanted them for years, funding has been an obstacle.

For the last 15 years, the Estonian Air Force has used two Czech L-39 light fighter jets for training. But now Herem believes aircraft capable of intercepting jet-powered drones are needed.

"The Ukrainians use F-16 fighter jets to destroy nearly half of them. But we certainly could not afford to go down that route. However, smaller jet-powered aircraft could fulfill that role, whether manned or unmanned," he said.

Minister of Defense Martin Herem. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"Today we know that manned aircraft definitely work. We still do not know very much about unmanned aircraft," the defense minister added.

Light fighter jets would also have a role in hunting loitering munitions, former Air Force commander Vello Loemaa said.

"These aircraft need to be used against drones with speeds ranging from just over 100 to 600 kilometers per hour. The rest of the process – everything involved in engaging a drone, from detection to destruction – is exactly the same as with larger fighter aircraft," he said.

Estonia has pilots for light fighter jets, but they have not been trained to engage aerial targets. "We have the expertise needed to provide further training. But we lack expertise in the specific field of engaging aerial targets," Loemaa said.

A squadron would consist of around a dozen fighter jets, and training would take a year or two.

Vello Loemaa. Source: ERR

Herem believes the aircraft could be procured within four years or even sooner.

"Where and when exactly we will procure them is still quite unclear at the moment. The same goes for where they will be based. But there are certain tasks for which we have no other good alternative," the minister said.

The air force has planned to acquire fighter jets for decades, but its ability to lobby has been weak.

"I would also say there has been a lack of expertise. What is happening now in the war in the skies over Ukraine could have been foreseen. But better late than never, now that this knowledge is reaching others as well," Loemaa said.

He noted that cooperation between the Baltic navies once gave rise to BALTRON, while the air forces also discussed Baltwing, a joint air squadron. However, a lack of resources and common plans has been an obstacle.

World.title: Tallinn Zoo hosts annual Pumpkin Party
World.content:
Although Halloween is still a week away, the pumpkin-loving residents of Tallinn Zoo were presented with more than four tons of donated vegetables for their annual party this weekend.

The zoo's traditional Pumpkin Party took place on Saturday, with the residents being treated to carrots, beetroots, apples, turnips, potatoes, and cabbage alongside the seasonal gourds.

The elephants were one of the most popular attractions, and they were happy to demonstrate their pumpkin-handling skills to the crowds of excited children.

"They love pumpkins the most. The elephant eats the largest quantity of pumpkins – 600 kilograms a year," said Anita Tamm, a communications specialist at Tallinn Zoo.

"Many other animals at the zoo eat them too. The pygmy marmoset eats the least pumpkin at the zoo – just 120 grams a year. Other enthusiasts include hoofed animals, rhinos, apes and monkeys, and reptiles," Tamm said.

The only animals that do not like gourds are carnivores, such as the big cats.

The pumpkin party marks the end of the zoo's vegetable collection campaign. However, anyone can still bring their garden produce to the donation box at the zoo's north gate.

Tallinn Zoo's Pumpkin Party. Source: ERR

World.title: Police tackle underage drinking, illegal scooters in Tartu
World.content:
Police are cracking down on banned electric scooters and minors disturbing public order in Estonia's second-biggest city, Tartu, and carried out one of their largest recent operations targeting young people on Friday.

People out and about in Tartu in southern Estonia late on Friday night may have encountered an unusually large police presence.

Dozens of law enforcement officers were focused on light electric vehicle compliance in the Annelinn and Ülenurme areas. They identified two prohibited scooters, which can travel faster than the legal limit, and two cases of people riding two to a single electric scooter.

Officers also monitored helmet use and spoke with young people.

Kristo Kooskora, a senior inspector at the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA), said that the weather had worked against them this time.

"It rained to some extent throughout the evening, and we saw very few scooters, but that does not mean the problem has disappeared. Various scooter gatherings have also become popular recently, and we have been dealing with those as well. Our work in this area is not over," she told ERR's evening news show "Aktuaalne kaamera."

There was more activity in the city center after midnight.

Nearly 50 police officers patrolled Küüni tänav, which leads from Kaubamaja shopping center to the main square, in an unprecedented operation.

"The checks were conducted by officers simply moving in from both ends and checking everyone caught between the police teams until the officers eventually met in the middle," Kooskora said.

According to preliminary information, police identified nearly 30 intoxicated minors, including some who were severely intoxicated. There were also minors using e-cigarettes and cases involving suspected drug use.

Handcuffs had to be used in several cases because the young people became aggressive. Some also attempted to flee, but their attempts were unsuccessful.

Officers said the operation confirmed the problem with minors is serious. Checks should be carried out more frequently, including on weekdays.

World.title: Justice chancellor: Wild boar cannot be made to suffer when training hunting dogs
World.content:
The Ministry of Regional Affairs and the Ministry of Climate should establish clear legal rules for training hunting dogs using live wild boars to ensure animal welfare and legal clarity, the Chancellor of Justice's Office says.

Four years ago in May, the regional affairs minister issued a regulation on measures to prevent and control African swine fever, introducing an exemption under which the ban on keeping pigs outdoors does not apply to wild boars kept for training hunting dogs.

The Estonian Union for the Protection of Animals asked the chancellor of justice to examine whether the regulation complies with the Animal Protection Act. The organization also pointed out that the law provides no legal basis for using wild boars kept in artificial environments to train hunting dogs and that no detailed requirements have been established for such training.

Deputy Chancellor of Justice-Adviser Olari Koppel said the ban on keeping pigs outdoors is a biosecurity measure and that the minister has the authority to introduce exemptions, provided they comply with EU law and do not undermine animal disease prevention. Koppel therefore sees no reason to believe that the exemption for training hunting dogs violates these conditions.

However, he noted that the regulation only provides an exemption from the ban on keeping pigs outdoors. It does not provide a legal basis for using wild boars to train hunting dogs or authorize activities prohibited under the Animal Protection Act.

"The absence of a specific legal provision does not, however, mean that such an activity is prohibited, provided other applicable rules are followed," Koppel said, adding that it must be possible to conduct training without endangering the animal's welfare.

The law does not establish a specific legal basis or detailed requirements for training hunting dogs using live wild boars. The activity is primarily governed by the Nature Conservation Act and the general animal welfare requirements arising from it.

Under the Animal Protection Act, animals must not be subjected to suffering or pain. According to Koppel, if hunting dog training cannot be conducted without causing such harm, the executive branch cannot make the activity permissible through regulations, guidelines or administrative practices.

"In that case, only the Riigikogu can decide through legislation whether the objective of the training and the benefits it provides justify making an exception to the prohibition established by law," Koppel said.

Koppel said the lack of clarity in the regulations is a problem. To address it, the Ministry of Regional Affairs and the Ministry of Climate should establish the conditions for training hunting dogs in legislation rather than merely in guidelines or explanatory memorandums. This would ensure compliance with animal welfare requirements and provide legal clarity.

Wild boar. Photo is illustrative. Source: Kalmer Saar/minupilt.err.ee

World.title: Isamaa party promises to close the climate ministry and create scandals committee
World.content:
Isamaa leader Urmas Reinsalu said at the party's council meeting in Tallinn that the campaign for Estonia's parliamentary elections has begun and is intensifying.

"Those same three parties that, under SALK's leadership, have established a politics of lies under both Kaja Kallas' and Kristen Michal's governments are now maneuvering to escape political punishment and put up camouflage nets," Reinsalu said, referring to the coalition Reform Party and Eesti 200, as well as the opposition Social Democrats.

According to the Isamaa chairman, Eesti 200 is being pressured to withdraw from the elections so that its remaining voters will instead bolster the Reform Party and the Social Democrats.

"So much for political accountability," Reinsalu said. "With the prime minister's speech to the party council, the Reform Party has launched a new wave of fearmongering and lies. This is being dressed up in a marketing campaign whose underlying message is that, yes, we have failed, but we will do better in the future."

"The Reform Party is featuring a beloved actor in its campaign, while the Social Democrats have adopted a different tactic, attempting to conceal their complicity in the Kallas-Michal government by maneuvering to put forward the secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as their candidate for prime minister. This maneuver will not succeed!" the Isamaa chairman said.

Reinsalu summed up Isamaa's political plans following the 2027 Riigikogu elections with the words "Let the citizens decide."

The party plans to give citizens the right to initiate early elections, following the Latvian model, and to establish a commission of inquiry into scandals after the elections. Lying before the commission would be a criminal offense.

In the area of defense, the party plans to close the border with Russia.

Isamaa also pledged to introduce a supplementary budget that would cut spending.

"Cost-cutting starts at the top: parliamentary and ministerial salaries, closing the Ministry of Climate and a critical review of foundations and subsidies," the party pledged.

On taxes, Isamaa promised to abolish the motor vehicle tax and reduce value-added tax on basic foodstuffs (meat, fish, milk, fruit, vegetables and bread) to 13 percent starting July 1, 2027.

The party also promised to end what it described as the harassment of businesses. "The Climate Act will be thrown in the trash. Investment certainty and a stable operating environment will be restored for the resource-based economy."

The party pledged to carry out an artificial intelligence revolution with the same boldness that Estonia once demonstrated in building its digital state. "The goal is genuine productivity growth, exports and simpler government operations. Sovereignty risks will be taken into account."

Isamaa promised to protect fundamental freedoms and repeal unnecessary restrictions.

The party also pledged to ease the burden of raising children on families and protect teachers' incomes.

In the energy sector, the party will emphasize oil shale. "The energy sector will be provided with dispatchable generation capacity, domestic resources (including oil shale) and affordable prices. Efforts to render oil shale-based energy production unviable will be halted."

The party also promised stricter requirements for the use of Estonian in public spaces, a conservative immigration policy and the restoration of regional balance.

Parliamentary elections will take place in March 2027.

World.title: Iraq, US discuss prospects to strengthen joint cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Defense Nayef al-Shammari and Chargé d’Affaires at the US Embassy in Baghdad Steven Fagin discussed approaches to strengthen cooperation between Baghdad and Washington on Sunday.

During their meeting in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, the two sides discussed bilateral ties and strategies to enhance cooperation between the two countries, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The meeting took place after the US-led international coalition formally completed its full withdrawal and ended Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq on September 30, 2026.

Operation Inherent Resolve—the multinational military campaign formed in 2014 to fight ISIS—officially wrapped up after a 12-year presence.

The end of the combat mission shifts the relationship to a bilateral framework focused on non-combat intelligence sharing, targeted training, and security cooperation rather than active foreign military bases.

Iraqi security forces have assumed full operational control, and the government has set goals to bring remaining armed factions under state regulation.

World.title: Drone attack targets Iranian Kurdish base in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A drone attack carried out by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted on Saturday evening a base belonging to an Iranian Kurdish opposition group in the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

According to reports, the strike hit the headquarters and a guard post of the Komala party. The base is located in the Alana Valley within the Balisan region, northeast of Erbil.

Local security and party officials confirmed the strike caused material damage to buildings but resulted in no casualties.

This attack is a part of Tehran’s intensified campaign against Iraqi-based Iranian Kurdish opposition groups.

Since the military conflict broke out in the region on February 28, Iran has launched over 1,000 drones and missiles into Iraqi Kurdistan, claiming that these groups are directly endangering its national security and have Israeli support.

In mid-August, two explosive-laden drones launched from Iranian territory targeted Iraqi Kurdistan Prime Minister Masrour Barzani’s private office and the home of a top intelligence official.

The strikes took place in Erbil province’s Pirmam area, which is around 30 kilometers north of the capital.

Security personnel recognized the drone as an Iranian-designed “Hadid-110” kamikaze drone carrying explosive payloads.

While Tehran and Iran-backed armed groups have previously accused Iraqi Kurdistan of hosting hostile Iranian Kurdish opposition groups, the authorities in the Kurdistan region of Iraq have always denied using their territory to threaten neighboring nations.

World.title: Iraq, KBR discuss oil sector development
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister for Energy Affairs Mohsen al-Mandalawi and a delegation from US-based KBR discussed on Thursday developing the country’s oil and gas sectors.

KBR’s delegation headed by the company’s president for sustainable technology solutions, Jay Ibrahim, discussed prospects for joint cooperation in the oil, gas, and energy sectors, as well as leveraging the firm’s expertise to develop infrastructure and enhance the efficiency of strategic projects, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The meeting addressed the recovery of associated gas, the development of oil fields, the enhancement of production efficiency, and the modernization of oil facilities.

The two sides also discussed leveraging KBR’s cutting-edge technology solutions to help Iraq’s oil industry grow and to make it easier to carry out key projects that meet requirements for effectiveness, quality, and financial sustainability.

The Iraqi official stressed the importance of ongoing coordination among Iraqi authorities to identify potential areas for collaboration.

Al-Mandalawi noted that the government aims to develop actionable programs related to the Majnoon oil field, the recovery of associated gas at the West Qurna field, initiatives for ammonia production, and efforts to reduce gas flaring at oil fields.

World.title: Iraq sells 10 million barrels of oil at discounts up to $28
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq recently sold 10 million barrels of oil via its southern ports at a discount ranging from $25 to $28 per barrel.

Sources told Attaqa News that most of these shipments were acquired by Indian companies and that the loading took place at the southern ports a few days ago.

Iraq has been unable to sell any oil at a price higher than $100 per barrel since the outbreak of the military conflict in the Middle East, according to two more sources, even though world prices have risen to almost $117 per barrel.

A source at the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) said that Iraq has not been able to sell oil for more than $85 per barrel.

About a month ago, the company sold some shipments of light crude at around $90 per barrel.

The spokesperson for the Ministry of Oil, Salim al-Rikabi, said that oil sales are still being conducted via the southern ports, and there are variable discounts in place to cover transportation and insurance costs for the purchasing companies.

Recently, Iraq’s average oil exports have risen to approximately 3.2 million barrels per day, according to statements made by Oil Minister Basim Khudair to the official news agency.

Oil shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz account for roughly 3 million barrels per day.

Due to its inadequate tanker fleet, Iraq has resorted to giving substantial discounts on its oil since the start of the conflict in the region, often as much as $32 per barrel.

World.title: Iraq sells 10 million barrels of crude at steep discounts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq recently sold approximately 10 million barrels of crude oil via its southern export terminals at steep discounts ranging between $25 and $28 per barrel against prevailing international benchmarks, according to industry sources cited by the energy platform Attaqa on Sunday, October 25, 2026.

Trade sources confirmed that Indian refining companies secured the bulk of the discounted shipments, which were loaded at southern offshore terminals in recent days.

Market participants highlighted that Baghdad has been unable to market its crude above $100 per barrel since the outbreak of regional hostilities involving Iran, even as international oil benchmarks surged toward $117 per barrel during recent trading sessions amid maritime risk and escalating conflict dynamics.

Confirming the pricing constraints, an official source at the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) disclosed that recent spot transactions have struggled to clear above $85 per barrel.

The source noted that approximately one month prior, SOMO managed to offload select Basrah Light cargoes at around $90 per barrel before market pressures widened discount spreads. The steep price differentials emerge as the economic observatory “Eco Iraq” reported on Saturday that Iraq’s aggregate crude oil export revenues totaled $37.39 billion from shipments of 533.46 million barrels across the first nine months of 2026.

World.title: Iraq increases port capacity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has announced that the country’s ports can now handle twice as much cargo as they could in the past.

The ministry’s media director, Hussein Ahmed, said on Sunday that the current capacity of Iraqi ports exceeds 79 million tons of cargo and more than 3.6 million containers.

Ahmed noted that Iraqi ports can now handle twice the cargo volume previously recorded, which was over 40 million tons, as reported by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The Iraqi official mentioned that improvements have been made to the ports, including the construction of new roads, upgrades to existing streets leading to the ports, and the establishment of marshaling yards to alleviate internal congestion.

Iraq’s State Company for Maritime Transport (SCMT), a government-owned maritime company operating under the Iraqi Ministry of Transport, announced on Sunday the reactivation of the Iraqi Line, marked by the arrival of the vessel Basra at the port of Umm Qasr.

SCMT’s director Ahmed Jassim said that the vessel arrived at the port of Umm Qasr carrying containers from the port of Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates, signaling the reactivation of the maritime route and the resumption of its commercial voyages after a hiatus that lasted for decades.

World.title: Iraq advances Japanese loan port projects as Grand Faw reach 98%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Transport is moving to activate two major maritime infrastructure projects—a new floating dock and an integrated shipyards city—financed under the Japanese official development assistance (ODA) loan framework.

The initiative is aimed at expanding vessel repair, maintenance, and auxiliary maritime services across Iraqi ports, coinciding with significant construction milestones at the strategic Grand Faw Port in Basra.

According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Hussein Ahmed, Director of Media and Government Communications at the Ministry of Transport, ministry officials held technical consultations with representatives of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) loan authority.

The discussions centered on selecting construction locations and addressing civil and logistical engineering requirements for both the floating dry dock and the specialized shipyard zone to modernize national maritime support capabilities.

The operational expansion coincides with near-completion across primary infrastructure phases at the Grand Faw Port. General Director of the General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Abdullah Aati Abdullah, announced that the port’s core breakwater works have reached 100% completion.

Additionally, the submerged immersed tunnel connecting the port to Umm Qasr has achieved a 98% execution rate, while foundational infrastructure across the facility stands at 94%.

Speaking at a press conference, Abdullah stated that technical teams are preparing to transition toward superstructure and terminal installation phases under the oversight of Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Transport Minister Wahab Al-Hasani.

Abdullah confirmed that preliminary operational trials are scheduled to commence in the upcoming period. He noted that while broader regional shipping traffic has felt the ripple effects of security dynamics around the Strait of Hormuz, work remains focused on expanding container handling capacity, securing yard storage, and cementing Grand Faw’s position as a regional logistics hub connecting the Gulf to Europe.

World.title: Iraq to construct six dams with Turkey and 13 rainwater harvesting barriers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Water Resources revealed plans on Sunday, October 25, 2026, to construct six new dams under the bilateral framework agreement with Turkey, while advancing technical designs and assessments for 13 additional rainwater and seasonal flood harvesting barriers across several governorates to bolster strategic water reserves, support agriculture, and combat desertification.

According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Ministry Spokesperson and Director General of the General Authority for Irrigation and Reclamation Projects, Khaled Shamal, technical blueprints have been finalized for three dams under the first package of the Turkish framework agreement, preparing them for on-ground execution by Turkish contractors.

The three initial structures comprise the Kharaz Dam in Al-Muthanna Governorate, the Al-Abyad Dam in Ain Al-Tamr in Karbala Governorate, and the Abu Takiya Dam in Nineveh Governorate, with site evaluations underway for an additional three dams proposed under a secondary implementation package.

In parallel with the Turkish cooperation framework, Shamal detailed progress on domestic water harvesting infrastructure designed to capture torrential flash floods and surface runoffs. Technical engineering designs are complete for five submerged check dams in Nineveh Governorate—Sheikh Bakr 1 and 2, Ain Alaq, Ain Ba’shiqa, and Ain Bahzani—with active construction already launched at two sites.

An additional eight water barriers are undergoing hydrologic surveys and final design studies, distributed across Nineveh (3 dams), Najaf (2 dams), Al-Muthanna (2 dams), and Diyala (1 dam), providing vital localized water reserves to support nomadic resettlement, pastoral communities, and regional land reclamation initiatives.

World.title: Massive fire engulfs Shiv Market near Jammu Railway Station, 35-40 shops gutted

Massive fire broke out at Shiv Market, opposite Jammu Railway Station

NEW DELHI: Around 35 to 40 shops were completely gutted after a massive fire broke out at Shiv Market, opposite Jammu Railway Station, in the early hours of Monday. No casualties or injuries have been reported so far, while fire and emergency services teams were working to bring the blaze under control. The cause of the fire remains unknown.BJP MLA Vikram Randhawa said the fire reportedly began due to a short circuit in one shop before spreading rapidly to adjoining establishments. Shiv Market is a major commercial hub with shops selling dry fruits and blankets, as well as eateries and dhabas.âThe fire started with a short circuit in one shop and spread rapidly, engulfing surrounding shops. By the time the fire brigade arrived, the entire market had been consumed by the flames. In my estimation, about 35 to 40 shops have been completely gutted,â Randhawa said.Describing the firefighting efforts, the MLA said the blaze had engulfed the entire market by the time the situation could be brought under control. He added that police personnel and senior officers were actively involved in managing the situation.âAs it kept growing, by the time the whole system came under control, it had already engulfed the entire market.Right now, our police are completely alert and actively controlling the situation. You can see that from the SHO to our SP, everyone is personally involved, even holding and dragging pipes all the way to the shops,â Randhawa said.A shopkeeper said at least 25 to 30 shops had suffered total losses and urged the administration to provide compensation to those affected.âThe entire market has been reduced to ashes. At least 25 to 30 shops are a total loss. We pray to God to grant everyone the strength to cope with this â the loss is immense, a total loss. I also urge the administration to step in as quickly as possible and ensure that compensation is provided without delay,â the shopkeeper said.Randhawa said the full extent of the damage could be assessed only after the situation was completely under control. He said shopkeepers were cooperating with the administration, with the deputy commissioner, SP South, DSP, SHO and their teams present at the site. Members of civil society were also helping with relief efforts.On compensation for affected shopkeepers, Randhawa said the matter would be discussed with the administration later, describing the damage as massive.

World.title: Jaishankar to attend G20, Quad meets in US
World.content:
Quad foreign ministers will meet this week in Atlanta on the sidelines of a G20 ministerial gathering, official sources confirmed, signalling the strategic forum remains resilient despite recent India-US diplomatic turbulence.

This will be the second meeting of the grouping this year, after the event India hosted in May.

The foreign ministers will look to outline the agenda for the Quad leadersâ summit in Manila next month on the margins of Asean meetings. EAM S

will travel to Atlanta for the G20 and Quad foreign ministersâ meetings that US secretary of state Marco Rubio will host on Oct 30-31.

The event in Manila, likely on Nov 16, will be the first Quad leadersâ summit in two years, following the downturn in India-US ties that prevented India from hosting the summit last year. The summit will be significant in terms of both its timing and venue. It will take place in the middle of raging maritime tensions between Manila and Beijing, and days before another visit to China by President Donald Trump this year for the APEC summit.

World.title: ‘Creamy layer case in SC won’t hit seniority of CSE-2025 batch’
World.content:
File photo: Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: The pendency of the case regarding the OBC creamy layer in Supreme Court will not affect the seniority of successful candidates of 2025 batch even though their service allocation and foundation course are still to be finalised, official sources said on Sunday.DoPT officials said, âThe department and all training institutes are prepared to allocate services expeditiously to CSE- 2025 candidates and commence foundation course at the earliest. Delay in commencement of the foundation course will have no bearing on the seniority, gradation or other service conditions of the candidates.âThe clarification concerns the fate of successful candidates in the wake of SCâs Rohith Nathan judgement of March 11 in which it had said âsalaryâ cannot be added to âincomeâ for defining âcreamy layerâ criteria for any category of OBC candidates, including those whose parents are employed in PSUs/banks, etc. The judgement pertained to the case of candidates from PSU background being categorised over the years as âcreamy layerâ by including âsalaryâ in the âincomeâ of their parents.

World.title: CBSE makes AI a part of formal teaching, NCERT develops module
World.content:
NCERT has developed a 20-hour introductory module for Classes IX-XII, which CBSE has earmarked for school-based assessment.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From spotting deepfake to questioning a chatbotâs confident but incorrect answers, artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from being an optional subject towards becoming a basic skill for CBSE schoolchildren. Taking a step towards more formal AI teaching in schools, NCERT has developed a 20-hour introductory module for Classes IX-XII, which it has earmarked for school-based assessment. Separate AI textbooks are also being prepared for students pursuing the subject at a more advanced level.The move is part of a wider effort to make AI literacy accessible to students, irrespective of whether they study computers or choose AI as an elective. The idea is to first familiarise children with how the technology works, its uses and limitations, before moving towards more structured teaching through textbooks.NCERT developed the module on computational thinking (CT) and AI in consultation with IIT Madras and IIT Jodhpur.In an April-9 circular, CBSE had announced that NCERT would provide modules for Classes IX-XII for internal assessment during the 2026-27 academic session.Under the boardâs revised scheme, CT and AI modules are compulsory for Class IX, while Class X continues under the existing scheme.A senior education ministry official said AI had become an important part of everyday activities, from education and research to content writing and career guidance. âAI tools are being used for studies, research, content writing and even career advice. Students will be taught how to use AI tools correctly and fact-check information,â they said.

World.title: EC refuses to give details of SIR software, cites ‘trade secrets, IPR'

has declined to disclose the name and version of the software it used to identify errors and anomalies in voter rolls during SIR, saying the information was related to âcommercial confidence, trade secrets and intellectual propertyâ and, thus, exempt under RTI Act.

World.title: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to government than needed, says Justice Kaul
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to the govt than necessary in matters of judicial appointments, former SC judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has said in his forthcoming book âWithout Fear Or Favourâ, and claimed that he was prevented from hearing petitions for re-examination of the validity of provisions of PMLA.

Kaul also claimed Justice Chandrachud had, allegedly under pressure from govt, withdrawn a case from him in which a bench headed by him had questioned delays in implementation of the SC collegiumâs resolutions for appointment of judges. This, he said, âtroubled him the mostâ as the case was assigned years ago and was taken away all of a sudden.

Reacting to the claims, Justice Chandrachud said, âThere was never even a dissent by any member of the collegium over any name during discussions for appointments to the SC.â

âDYC asked if he should call government on collegium picksâ

Sources said resolutions passed by the collegium for appointments to the SC during Justice Chandrachudâs tenure were unanimous and signed by all members of the collegium without recording a single dissent.

In this case, a bench of Justices Kaul and Sudhanshu Dhulia had pulled up govt for its alleged pick-and-choose policy in clearing names sent by the collegium and had on Nov 20, 2023, asked why Centre was not transferring four judges from Gujarat HC and not appointing two Sikh lawyers for Punjab and Haryana HC as recommended by the collegium.





The case was thereafter taken away from his bench and it has not been listed in the last three years.

In an interview to Karan Thapar for The Wire, Justice Kaul claimed the former CJI took him aside during a collegium meeting and asked whether he should telephone govt to ascertain its views on the proposed appointments. Justice Kaul said pre-approval from govt before discussions in the collegium was a matter of concern.

âThis has unfortunately become a practice of names being discussed, and some kind of previous discussion with govt. That used to happen. It has been happening, I think before CJI Chandrachud and after. That is why it troubles me,â he said, adding that there was nothing wrong in holding consultations with govt, but it should happen only after the collegiumâs decision and not before.

Asked whether Justice Chandrachud was too deferential to govt, Justice Kaul said, âThere is a judicial side and there is an administrative side of the Chief Justice of India.

I wouldnât be concerned with the judicial side. I believe he had both the intellectual heft and the capacity and hard work to do so. But in consultations with govt and collaboration, I felt he was more deferential than necessary to carry it forward.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

â

Justice Kaul said he tried to discourage Justice Chandrachud from discussing everything with govt beforehand as it could create its own problems. Asked whether Justice Chandrachud failed to live up to the high expectations from him, Justice Kaul said, âI would say that expectations were higher from him.â

TOI has reported how Justice Kaul had vigorously and successfully pushed many names for judgeship as part of the SC and HC collegiums and three of his proposals had met with resistance from other members of the panel. The then CJI had tactically refrained from holding collegium meetings to avoid embarrassing situations.

In reply to the TOI article, Justice Kaul had sent a rejoinder and said, âThere was no question of insistence of appointment of those suggested by me and all recommendations have been made by consensus. That other collegium members had reservations and I pushed the names, thus, seem to be a flight of your imagination.â

World.title: EPFO considers Rs 25,000cr war chest to stabilise interest payouts
World.content:
File photo: Employees Provident Fund Organisation- EPFO

Report on ISR sent to panel studying EPFO investment framework

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Employeesâ Provident Fund Organisation is discussing a dedicated Rs 25,000-crore Interest Stabilisation Reserve, designed to insulate the annual interest payouts of its nearly 30 crore members from the turbulence caused by corporate bond defaults and forced-exit losses.Officials said EPFO and government want a stable regime for its subscribers and wish to avoid any sharp fall or spike in rates due to market conditions or defaults.Under existing regulatory frameworks, credit losses and exit haircuts, resulting from downgraded securities, directly impact EPFOâs interest account and depress the annual interest rate for members.A proposal submitted by IIM Kozhikode, which among other things studied the feasibility of creating an Interest Stabilisation Reserve (ISR), was discussed in detail by EPFOâs investment committee (IC) Thursday, TOI has learnt.The report has now been sent to a high-poweredJ panel constituted to examine the agencyâs investment framework and recognise non-performing investments.The report suggested building the stabilisation reserve progressively via surplus ETF capital gains and excess interest income and investing it strictly in liquid govt securities (G-Secs) to ensure absolute capital safety, sovereign backing, immediate liquidity, and risk-free yield, said persons familiar with the deliberations.The reserve will not only shield subscribers but will also back active exit policies and empower portfolio managers to execute disciplined, multi-year exits from troubled assets without hesitation.The report took into account the current realities of Indiaâs over-the-counter (OTC) corporate bond market, which remains shallow and illiquid, such that when institutional holders such as EPFO are forced to exit distressed assets, thin market depth results in severe haircuts.Historically, EPFO relied heavily on equity ETF capital gains to offset credit stress.The report, however, noted that the volatile market downturn of FY 2019-20 coincided with major credit events like the IL&FS default, which exposed a critical vulnerability.âCredit stress and equity market crashes are highly correlated. Relying solely on ETF gains is dangerous; a standalone prudential reserve is a structural necessity,â it said.The study evaluated absolute worst-case liquidation scenarios across the portfolio netted against available ETF gains, pinpointing a cumulative baseline shortfall of approximately Rs 23,837 crore.âTo account for incomplete market data and ensure a bulletproof prudential buffer, the report recommends formalising an ISR Fund of Rs 25,000 crore,â it said.The study also ran a historical back-testing simulation which modelled portfolio returns from 2010-11 to 2023-24, demonstrating that a Rs 25,000-crore baseline successfully absorbs annual shortfalls and stabilises declared interest rates across typical economic cycles.The only exception was 2019-20, where portfolio deficit spiked to Rs 55,640 crore, leading to deep drawdown from the reserve.âHowever, the subsequent recovery in investment performance in later years indicates that such a shortfall would likely have been temporary in nature.In such a scenario, EPFO could have bridged the temporary deficit through a short-term advance or loan mechanism, which could subsequently be repaid from future surpluses generated during recovery years,â the study said.

World.title: Govt. to set up medical rooms in all schools: Sood
World.content:
Education Minister Ashish Sood said on Sunday that the Delhi government will set up medical rooms in all 1,086 government schools at a cost of ₹48.87 crore to provide immediate first aid and care to students during school hours.

The medical rooms will provide basic first aid, including wound dressing, administration of ORS and temporary rest under trained supervision. However, diagnostic services and prescription medicines will not be provided in schools.

Mr. Sood said a trained health worker, such as an Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM) or a multipurpose health worker, will be engaged in each school to address immediate health needs and provide adolescent health support.

“Every child in our government schools deserves a safe and caring environment. When a student falls sick or gets hurt during school hours, parents and teachers should have peace of mind knowing that immediate first aid and proper care are readily available right inside the school campus,” he said.

He said the scheme, aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, aimed to make schools safe, inclusive and supportive spaces.

World.title: Raj Thackeray deletes Modi-Adani documentary post after Mumbai Police chief’s request, vows to continue fight
World.content:
Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray on Sunday (October 25, 2026) said he had deleted a social media post featuring a documentary on Prime Minister Narendra Modi and industrialist Gautam Adani following a request from the Mumbai Police Commissioner. However, he maintained that his opposition to corporate monopolies would continue, asserting that the documentary had already achieved its purpose of bringing the issue to public attention.

In a statement posted on X, Mr. Thackeray said he had shared a documentary by Sabeer Bhatia highlighting the alleged longstanding relationship between Mr. Modi and Mr. Adani and raising questions about the concentration of India’s industrial assets. The video, which he shared on October 22, received more than 4.8 million views on X alone, besides widespread engagement on Facebook and other platforms, he claimed.

Mr. Thackeray alleged that the documentary’s popularity had unsettled those in power, prompting a request for its removal through the Mumbai Police Commissioner.

He said he decided to honour the request out of respect for the police force. Describing Mumbai and Maharashtra Police as among the country’s most efficient police forces, Mr. Thackeray maintained that his decision should not be interpreted as a retreat from his position.

“The fire has already been lit,” he said, adding that the campaign against monopolistic practices would continue.

Opposition to corporate monopolies

Clarifying his position, Mr. Thackeray said his criticism was not directed at any particular industrialist but at policies that allegedly favoured a select few.

He argued that the Prime Minister should encourage multiple industrialists to expand their businesses, generate employment and compete internationally, rather than extend preferential treatment to a single business group.

Referring to his January 2026 public meeting at Shivtirth in Mumbai, Mr. Thackeray said he had already presented his concerns about the Adani Group’s growing influence across sectors. He added that portions of that presentation had been incorporated into Bhatia’s documentary.

The videos of his January presentation remain available on his social media accounts, he said, adding that he was sharing portions of the presentation again.

Raises concerns over Maharashtra forest land

Mr. Thackeray also accused the central and State governments of facilitating the transfer of Maharashtra’s forest land to select industrial groups.

He specifically alleged that the Centre had instructed the State government to hand over several hundred hectares of forest land in Bhimashankar to the Gujarat-based Torrent Group.

Questioning the silence of Maharashtra’s elected representatives, Mr. Thackeray asked why Marathi MPs, MLAs and ministers were not speaking out against what he described as the transfer of the State’s resources to private interests.

He criticised political leaders for invoking Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj while allegedly remaining silent as Maharashtra’s assets were handed over to industrialists.

Reiterating that the documentary had been produced by others, Mr. Thackeray said his objective in circulating it was to make the information accessible to a wider audience.

He maintained that this objective had been achieved and that removing the documentary would not affect his continuing campaign against monopolistic practices.

World.title: BJP to hold nationwide protest on October 26 against Kharge’s remark on Modi
World.content:
The BJP has announced a nationwide protest on Monday (October 26, 2026) against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's "indecent and offensive" remarks targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Mr. Kharge’s remarks at a Patna event on Sunday (October 25, 2026), in which he dragged Mr. Modi’s late father, triggered a sharp reaction from senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders, who accused the principal Opposition, under Rahul Gandhi’s leadership, of increasingly resorting to personal attacks against Mr. Modi and his family.

Criticising the “Modi ka baap bhi jayega [even Modi’s father will go]” comment, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Mr. Kharge has “torn apart all norms of decorum”.

"In protest against the insulting, indecent, and offensive remarks made by the Congress national president in Patna regarding Prime Minister Narendra Modi's late father, the BJP will stage strong demonstrations tomorrow (Monday) across all state headquarters in the country," the BJP said in a statement.

The Bihar BJP also will hold protest march and effigy burning against Mr. Kharge’s statement. The march will beging at party headquerters in Patna.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: Sirsa chairs meeting with NCR officials, reiterates need for regional cooperation to fight air pollution
World.content:
Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Sunday (October 25, 2026) held a virtual meeting with officials from neighbouring districts and said that air pollution is a regional issue that requires coordinated action by Delhi and neighbouring NCR states.

The meeting focused on strengthening inter-state coordination and ensuring effective implementation of pollution-control measures under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) and directions issued by the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and adjoining areas (CAQM).

“The Delhi government is working in close coordination with the Government of India and Central agencies, with continued support for measures aimed at improving air quality, strengthening clean mobility, reducing road dust and ensuring coordinated enforcement across the NCR,” Mr. Sirsa said.

Senior traffic police officials from Noida, Faridabad, Gurugram, Sonipat and Bahadurgarh participated in the meeting, and Delhi Police Special Commissioner (Traffic) and the Transport Commissioner of Delhi were also present.

Mr. Sirsa said that traffic movements will be synchronised, and adequate traffic personnel will be deployed at identified high-traffic corridors and congestion-prone locations, particularly near NCR border areas, to ensure smoother traffic flow and minimise vehicular emissions caused by prolonged congestion.

“Vigilance and enforcement of Pollution Under Control (PUC) norms will be strengthened. Visibly polluting vehicles will be stopped, and strict action will be taken, including impounding vehicles and imposing the maximum permissible penalties, wherever applicable,” an official statement said.

The directions of the Supreme Court regarding the diversion of truck traffic not destined for Delhi through the Eastern and Western Peripheral Expressways will be strictly enforced to reduce unnecessary heavy-vehicle movement through the city, according to officials. Also, existing restrictions on the plying of overage diesel and petrol vehicles, along with other restrictions, will be strictly implemented.

The Minister said that effective border management, strict enforcement, smoother traffic movement, cleaner public transport and coordinated action against non-compliant vehicles will remain important components of Delhi’s winter pollution-control strategy.

Meanwhile, Delhi’s air quality remained in the ‘moderate’ category for the second consecutive day on Sunday.

The 24-hour average AQI stood at 153 (moderate) at 4 p.m. on Sunday (October 25, 2026), down from 191 (moderate) a day earlier, according to the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) daily bulletin, which provides the official AQI for the day. A higher AQI indicates worsening of air quality.

The air quality of Delhi is expected to deteriorate to the “poor” category on Monday and remain at the same level till Wednesday (October 28, 2026), as per Sunday’s (October 25, 2026) bulletin by the Central government’s ‘Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi’.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and the bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

World.title: String theory pioneer Ashoke Sen wins Oskar Klein Medal
World.content:
Theoretical physicist Ashoke Sen has been awarded the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal, becoming the first Indian laureate to receive the honour, awarded by Stockholm University and the Nobel Committee for Physics of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

The Medal recognises significant contributions to theoretical physics. Dr. Sen is the ICTS-Infosys Madhava Chair Professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS), Bengaluru. He also delivered the memorial lecture accompanying the Medal in Stockholm on October 22, under the title ‘Gravity from Strings and Strings from Gravity’.

World.title: BJP slams Kharge over ‘indecent’ remarks on PM Modi
World.content:
The BJP on Sunday (October 25, 2002) hit out at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for his remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The party said it would hold nationwide protests on Monday (October 26, 2026) against the “inappropriate and offensive remarks”.

Criticising the “Modi ka baap bhi jayega [even Modi’s father will go]” comment, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Mr. Kharge has “torn apart all norms of decorum”.

“This is not the first time that the Congress party has used abusive language against Modi ji or his family,” he said, accusing the party of having hurled insults at the Prime Minister’s mother, calling him a “merchant of death”, and mocking his poverty by addressing him as a “chaiwala” in the past.

“Under Rahul Gandhi’s leadership, the Congress party keeps crossing the limits of indecency every day,” he said, alleging that repeated electoral defeats over the past 12 years had bred “desperation and frustration” within the party.

कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन खरगे ने आज पटना में मोदी जी के पिताजी के बारे में अभद्र टिप्पणी कर सारी मर्यादाएँ तार-तार कर दी हैं। यह पहली बार नहीं है, जब कांग्रेस पार्टी ने मोदी जी या उनके परिवार को अपशब्द कहे हों। कभी उनकी पूजनीय माताजी के विषय में अपशब्द कहे, कभी उन्हें 'मौत का सौदागर' कहा, तो कभी 'चायवाला' कहकर उनकी गरीबी का उपहास उड़ाया। राहुल गांधी के नेतृत्व में कांग्रेस पार्टी हर रोज अभद्रता की सीमाएँ पार करती जा रही है। बीते 12 वर्षों में लगातार मिल रही चुनावी हार से कांग्रेस पार्टी में हताशा व निराशा इतनी बढ़ चुकी है कि अब उसके पास न कोई नीति बची है, न कोई मुद्दा, बस गाली-गलौज की राजनीति बची है। जनता के बीच जनाधार खो चुकी कांग्रेस, अब अपने कार्यकर्ताओं में भी आधार खोती जा रही है। जब-जब इन्होंने मोदी जी या उनके परिवार पर घृणित टिप्पणियाँ की हैं, तब-तब जनता ने कांग्रेस को करारा जवाब दिया है। — Amit Shah (@AmitShah) October 25, 2026

“Only the politics of slander remains. Having lost its public base among the people, Congress is now steadily losing its base even among its own workers. Whenever they have made hateful comments against Modi ji or his family, the public has given Congress a resounding response every time,” said Mr. Shah on X.

Terming Mr. Kharge’s language “indecent and unparliamentary”, BJP chief Nitin Nabin said: “There is a certain dignity to political opposition as well, but dragging the departed family members into speeches from public platforms has now become the real ‘culture’ of Rahul Gandhi and the whole Opposition. This is not Kharge ji’s personal statement, but a reflection of the entire Congress party’s lack of decorum in its thinking.”

“Frustrated by repeated electoral defeats, the Congress party is venting its political spite against Prime Minister Modi ji and his family through baseless and irresponsible comments. The Opposition’s panic — stemming from Modi ji’s rising popularity at home and abroad, and the public’s unwavering trust in him — is now plainly evident in its language and conduct,” said Union Minister J.P. Nadda.

He said that in a democracy, opponents must not “cross the bounds of propriety”, and the people will respond to such politics. “The Congress must realise that the trust of the people cannot be won through a politics of hatred and humiliation. The people of the country will surely deliver their response to such petty politics through democratic means,” he said.

World.title: BJP ‘failed’ to distribute all textbooks in government schools: AAP
World.content:
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Sunday (October 25, 2026) alleged that the BJP government has failed to distribute all textbooks to government school students even after about six months since the academic session began.

Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj asked Education Minister Ashish Sood to disclose whether the contractor supplying the textbooks has been fined under the rule mandating a 5% penalty for every week of delay.

“Is it true that the Education Secretary is refusing to sign the file until a penalty is imposed on the contractor for the late delivery of textbooks? Did the minister call the Education Secretary to his office to discuss this issue?” Mr. Bharadwaj said.

Mr. Bharadwaj said that he talked to students at a school and claimed that they had yet to receive different textbooks. “Class 8 students said they had not yet received Part 2 of their Mathematics textbook. Class 7 students said they were still waiting for Science, Part 2 of Mathematics and Part 2 of Social Studies (SST). Class 6 students said they had not received the Kaushal Bodh textbook, while Class 9 students said they were still waiting for their Social Science textbook,” he said.

World.title: Jamia student protest intensifies amid restrictions, heavy police deployment
World.content:
A day after attempts were made to forcibly remove protesting students at Jamia Millia Islamia university, students gathered around the campus and tried to enter by climbing the gates on Sunday (October 25, 2026). With classes suspended, water facilities on the campus were cut off and no entry or exit was allowed. Amid heavy police deployment, students still gathered in large numbers and staged a protest.

On Saturday (October 24), security personnel, teaching and non-teaching staff attempted to remove the students protesting since October 11 for restoration of their students’ union. The tent was uprooted from the lawn inside gate no. 7, campus electricity and water facilities suspended, gates and libraries closed and all classes announced to be conducted online until further notice.

Following this, students gathered in large numbers and stayed through the night, singing songs, raising slogans and demanding the restoration of JMISU. On Sunday (October 25), a similar scenario was observed, with heavy CRPF and Delhi Police personnel guarding the entry gates and dispersing the students who were trying to enter.

“We have been trying to go inside the campus but the security personnel are not allowing us. They have barricaded gate no. 7 and no entry is allowed from other gates as well. In the afternoon, some students from the hostel tried to access the health centre from gate no. 4 but were not allowed,” said Md. Zubair, a second year Bachelor’s student.

With entry and exit banned, students inside the campus were unable to access filtered water, had to rely on friends to get water for them. Some students wanting to join the protest also climbed gates and entered. Delhi Police personnel stopped many students from entering by pulling and physically handling them. Some students were also detained.

Around 1:00 p.m., the Vice-Chancellor, along with administration and other staff, visited the campus, inspected the gates and security arrangements and left without interacting with the students. “We have been demanding a dialogue with the V-C and the Chief Proctor on the restoration of JMISU that has been non-existent since 2006. After inviting students for a dialogue, the V-C used force to remove us and end our protest,” alleged Habeeba, one of the students removed from the hostel.

FIR registered

An FIR has been registered under the charges of trespassing, defacement of property and confinement against political leaders and students following a complaint sent by Jamia administration, the police officials said.

The complaint was sent by the Economics department mentioning trespassing and damage to public property. “The complaint contains names of MPs, leaders, students and ex-students who were trying to trespass on campus property. The FIR has been registered under the charges of criminal trespassing, wrongful confinement and voluntarily causing hurt under BNS. We have also added Sections from Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, as per the complaint,” Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police, South East, said.

Three persons including two women were detained from outside the campus on Sunday. “The two women were not connected with Jamia at all. They were neither students, nor ex-students or associated with any student party or union. They were creating law and order problems and were detained. They were released before sunset,” the officer said.

“Another person was held under Preventive Detention. The man works with a food delivery app and is educated only till class 10. We found his activities suspicious and are currently questioning him for his purpose of being at the site. We will present him before the SEM tomorrow,” the officer added.

Festive season

Students were informally being told to vacate the hostel on account of online classes and upcoming festivals. “The campus has moved online. There is no reason for anyone to stay on campus. They are also being asked to vacate informally as it is the festive season and parents like to see them at home,” an official from the Jamia administration said.

“Dialogue has been happening since day one. On Saturday (October 24), the entire Jamia, including professors, the administration and even the non-teaching staff, went to meet the students, but they did not want to end their protest,” the official said. On being asked why the students were forcibly removed, the official said, “If they had been removed, they would not have been there still.”

Responding to water facilities being suspended, the official said that since the campus was moved online, there was no question for students or anyone else to access these facilities. “The staff is not there. The gates and libraries are closed. The classes are happening online. They have no business being there,” the official said.

World.title: Shadab Khan's maiden ODI century steers Pakistan into tri-series final after thrilling chase against England
World.content:
Fortune favours the brave, and on Sunday it favoured Shadab Khan just when he seemed to have been abandoned by it.

He had dragged Pakistan from the brink of defeat to within touching distance of victory in the One-day International tri-series match against England. And it had taken extraordinary bravery to do so.

With the last wicket standing and Haris Rauf holding firm at the other end, Pakistan needed 27 runs when Shadab swept Gus Atkinson for six over fine leg.

Before the sparse crowd at the Gaddafi Stadium could finish celebrating, Atkinson fired a full delivery into Shadab’s pads. England appealed in unison and the umpire raised his finger.

Shadab, already regretting the momentary lapse, tapped his bat against his helmet in frustration before reviewing the decision, more out of obligation than hope.

Then came the twist. The big screen showed a spike on UltraEdge as the ball passed the bat. The decision was overturned, disbelief gave way to delight and Shadab returned to the crease with a smile.

He responded by squeezing Atkinson for four between short third and backward point to bring up his maiden ODI century off 91 balls, then whipped another full delivery through square leg for four.

After two dot balls, he pumped Atkinson over long-off for six, leaving Pakistan one hit away from victory.

Haris, who had faced 18 balls for his three runs, settled the contest in the next over, drilling debutant Henry Crocombe straight down the ground for four.

Pakistan reached 243-9 in 47.1 overs to complete a remarkable one-wicket victory, seal their place in the Oct 31 final and condemn England to another agonising defeat.

Shadab remained unbeaten on 113 off 96 balls, with 13 fours and five sixes, while his unbroken 89-run stand with Haris set a record for the highest 10th-wicket partnership in a successful ODI chase, surpassing the previous mark of 64.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, extending his heartiest congratulations to the team, wrote on X: “The last wicket partnership between Shadab and Haris turned the game around. Shadab’s century was spectacular. Well done boys!”

He said, “Every run, every wicket and every catch showed the grit, discipline and fighting spirit that define Pakistan.”

The unlikely rescue began when Shadab walked in at 103-5 after Arafat Minhas fell for one.

Pakistan had been chasing England’s 241 all out but were already in trouble, having lost Fakhar Zaman (10), Saim Ayub (six) and Babar Azam (10) inside seven overs. Saad Baig briefly counter-attacked with 32 off 22 balls, including seven fours, before falling at 74-4.

Hasan Nawaz made 15 before Liam Dawson dismissed him at 102, and Arafat followed in the next over.

Shadab initially worked his way into the innings, but his task grew harder when Salman Ali Agha, who had made 26 off 49 balls, was caught off Dawson at 121-6.

Shaheen Shah Afridi and Razaullah also fell, leaving Pakistan 154-9 after 33.5 overs and still needing 88 runs.

Shadab, however, refused to surrender. He reached 32 before Haris arrived, then began to attack with greater conviction.

He drove Atkinson over mid-off and pulled him through deep midwicket for boundaries, while a six over midwicket from Razaullah at the other end briefly lifted the pressure before the debutant was bowled by Will Jacks.

Shadab’s fifty came off 49 balls, with a six over deep square leg against Crocombe. He then used his feet to Dawson, sweeping a full toss for four and carving another six over wide long-off.

Reverse-sweeps and crisp drives through cover kept the chase alive as England struggled to find the final breakthrough.

With Haris offering dogged support, Shadab brought up the 50-run stand for the last wicket and then moved into the 90s with a pull for four off Sam Curran.

He declined singles at times to retain the strike, taking responsibility for almost every scoring opportunity. His century made him only the third batter to score an ODI hundred at No. 8 or lower.

Pakistan’s bowling shines under Shaheen

Earlier, Ben Duckett had stood tall with a century as England crumbled around him, managing 241 in 46.4 overs.

Shaheen led Pakistan’s attack with 4-46, reducing the visitors to 19-3 inside five overs. Tom Banton fell for four, Joe Root made five and captain Harry Brook was run out for one. Haris then removed Jordan Cox for six as England slumped to 52-4.

Duckett rebuilt the innings, reaching his half-century off 56 balls and helping England past 100 in the 20th over.

He pulled Haris for four, launched Salman over deep midwicket for six and reverse-hit another boundary. Curran provided the only substantial support, scoring 42 off 52 balls as the pair added 93 for the fifth wicket.

Shaheen broke the stand by dismissing Curran, caught at fine leg, before Duckett reached his fifth ODI century off 104 balls — his first against Pakistan. He made 105 off 111 deliveries, including 10 fours and two sixes, before Arafat had him caught at short fine leg for 187-7.

Razaullah took two wickets, including Will Jacks for 13, while Arafat also dismissed Jamie Overton for 10. Atkinson’s unbeaten 36 off 28 balls, featuring three sixes, lifted England to 241 before Shaheen dismissed Crocombe for eight to finish with four wickets.

England’s total looked competitive when Pakistan collapsed, but Shadab’s extraordinary innings turned the match on its head and carried the hosts into the final.

Haris Rauf compounded England’s troubles when Jordan Cox edged behind to Babar Azam for six, leaving the visitors struggling at 52-4 in the 10th over.

Duckett, however, refused to let the innings unravel completely. The left-hander brought up his half-century off 56 balls as England reached 100 in the 20th over, keeping the scoreboard moving with well-timed cuts, drives and sweeps.

He pulled Haris through midwicket for four before launching Salman Ali Agha over deep midwicket for six. Duckett also produced a reverse-hit boundary against Salman and pierced the covers with a crisp drive off Shadab Khan.

At the other end, Sam Curran provided the only meaningful support, counter-attacking with a series of boundaries. He charged down the track to lift Saim over mid-on and later rocked back to dispatch the spinner through midwicket.

The pair added 93 runs for the fifth wicket, taking England from 52-4 to 145 before Shaheen returned to break the stand in the 27th over. Curran, who scored 42 off 52 balls with five fours, top-edged a pull off a short delivery to Salman at fine leg.

Duckett continued to hold the innings together, reaching his fifth ODI century off 104 balls and his first against Pakistan. He struck 105 off 111 deliveries, including 10 fours and two sixes, before Arafat dismissed him in the 37th over, with Salman taking the catch at short fine leg.

England then lost Will Jacks (13) to Razaullah, who took a sharp return catch for his maiden ODI wicket, while Liam Dawson (five) fell to another short ball, caught by Shadab at deep square leg. Arafat also removed Jamie Overton (10), caught by Babar at long-off.

Gus Atkinson offered late resistance with an unbeaten 36 off 28 balls, including three sixes, helping England cross 200. Shaheen eventually ended the innings by dismissing debutant Henry Crocombe for eight, with Babar completing the catch.

World.title: KP Governor Kundi says Sohail Afridi, assembly speaker 'in safe hands' after house arrest
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Sunday that Sohail Afridi and Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati were “in safe hands” after being placed under house arrest.

Afridi, who has become non-functional as the KP chief minister, has not been seen since the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in his province on Oct 11. After their whereabouts remained unknown that day, a federal minister confirmed the next day that he and some of his cabinet members were in preventative custody.

However, with no further details officially confirmed, Afridi’s brother and Swati’s cousin have approached the Peshawar High Court separately to seek their relative’s recovery.

Appearing on Geo News’ TV programme ‘Jirga’ aired on Sunday night, the governor — who now runs the province — was asked about the whereabouts of Afridi, Kundi said he had been placed under house arrest and was “in safe hands — there is no need to worry”.

He said that if there were cases against Afridi, action would be taken against him and he would be indicted. However, if there were no cases, he would be released.

Asked why Afridi was not being released if there were no cases against him, Kundi replied he could provide an update tomorrow regarding the matter.

The governor further said that Speaker Swati was also under house arrest and would also be freed if there were no charges against him. Responding to another question, Kundi accused the PTI member of committing “illegal and unconstitutional” acts in his role as the KP Assembly Speaker.

Asked how many people were self-arrested and how many were “genuinely” arrested, Kundi said he did not have these numbers but that about 40 or 50 per cent of them were “under self-imposed arrest or self-concealment”.

The governor also addressed the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, stressing that it had been the “absolute last option”.

Regarding the potential duration of the emergency, he said, “We will see … after six months are complete, we will talk about what will and will not happen.

“But in my opinion, maybe it will run longer,” he added, clarifying that this was a “personal opinion” and he could be wrong.

He said that the basis for saying this was that the Centre and province needed to be “on the same page” in the fight against terrorism and “streamline” efforts against it, and was making plans accordingly, which he believed would take some time.

Kundi also distanced himself and the state policy from purported remarks made by Malik Khan Marjan — a member of the newly formed Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) for 12 districts of KP — wherein he favoured dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

“I will definitely check on this, but our policy is very clear: for now, we will not be holding talks with Afghanistan,” he maintained.

The governor condemned acts of terrorism carried out against Pakistan from Afghan soil and criticised Kabul for “allowing” India to use its soil against Pakistan while also asking for dialogue.

“If there is terrorism from there … our army knows how to fix it,” he added. “There is no dialogue and no talks of any kind about this.”

“I think this is his (Marjan’s) personal opinion, but it is not our policy,” Kundi said.

World.title: Jhang DC removed over use of Pera vehicle for 'non-serious purposes' in jeep rally: CM Maryam
World.content:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said on Sunday that Jhang Deputy Commissioner Babar Sahib Din was being removed immediately over the recent use of an official vehicle of the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (Pera) in a jeep rally, terming it a breach of discipline.

A three-day Jhang Thal Jeep Rally, which concluded last week, was organised in collaboration with private sponsors, according to Jhang District Information Officer Riaz Marth. He added that the event had received appreciation from provincial government authorities.

The chief minister took notice of the incident when a video surfaced on social media showing a Pera vehicle participating in the rally alongside other vehicles.
