World.title: England 'gutted' after second extraordinary ODI defeat in as many games
World.content:
Shadab Khan hit an epic ODI century, and England suffered a second extraordinary defeat in as many games as Pakistan snatched a one-wicket victory on Sunday to secure its place in the cricket tri-series final.

Pakistan's chase looked doomed at 9-154 before a defiant 89-run, last-wicket stand between Shadab and number 11 Haris Rauf secured Pakistan a dazzling win. Shadab smashed his first one-day ton to take Pakistan to 9-243 in 47.1 overs.

Even within that 10th wicket stand, Pakistan seemed to have been beaten when Gus Atkinson won an LBW decision against Shadab with 21 runs still required.

Shadab threw his bat down and started congratulating England's players before asking for a speculative review, which showed the faintest inside edge, leaving Shadab screaming with joy at the reprieve.

"The boys are absolutely gutted," England coach Brendon McCullum told the BBC.

"Today they fought incredibly hard … we were in a pretty good position, well, a very good position and then obviously we weren't able to get across the line.

"The last game was, the boys were gutted after that, and you look in the dressing room now, they're also extremely gutted now."

England, which scored 429 and still lost in its last game against Sri Lanka, was earlier all out for 241 in 46.4 overs.

Playing his first game in the tournament, Shadab scored 113 not out off 96 balls and farmed most of the strike. Rauf (7 not out in 19 balls) hit the winning boundary as Pakistan enjoyed its third successive win.

It was the biggest last-wicket partnership in a successful chase in ODIs.

The 10th wicket partnership was the largest ever to win a game in ODI cricket. (Getty Images: Sameer Ali)

Left-handed opener Ben Duckett scored 105 for England — his fifth ODI century and first against Pakistan — after Shaheen Shah Afridi won his first toss in the tournament and elected to field after successfully defending 300-plus scores in the first two games.

It was England's third successive defeat in the tournament after losing to Pakistan by 87 runs and seeing Sri Lanka pull off the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history despite captain Harry Brook scoring a blistering 114-ball double century.

Pakistan will take on Sri Lanka in their last league game on Tuesday after beating the Sri Lankans by 37 runs in the opening game.

Rauf joined Shadab at 154-9 in the 34th over and launched a partnership neither side will quickly forget. While Shadab outsmarted England pace with his brilliant batting, Rauf gave him ample support by sensibly not going for expansive shots.

Shadab protected Rauf well by keeping the strike to himself and counterpunching the bowlers by hitting boundaries early in the over, completing his century by playing a late cut off Atkinson for his 12th boundary before hitting the fast bowler over long off for a six to reduce the target to three runs off the final three overs.

Rauf drilled debutant fast bowler Henry Crocombe for a straight boundary to cap a remarkable recovery for Pakistan.

Earlier, Jamie Overton (3-43) took two smart slip catches to remove both struggling opening batters Fakhar Zaman (10) and Saim Ayub (6) and Babar Azam will continue his search for a big innings after Atkinson pegged back his off stump as Pakistan slumped to 31-3 inside the first seven overs.

Brook then turned to Overton soon after the batting power play, and the fast bowler responded immediately in his first over when 19-year-old Saad Baig (32) cut straight to Will Jacks at point.

Left-arm spinner Liam Dawson (2-30) and Jacks (1-18) then bowled tidily and raised England's hopes of their first win.

Duckett revived England from a precarious 52-4 with a 93-run stand with Sam Curran, who made 42 off 52 balls.

Afridi picked up 4-46 and England lost four of the five top batters for single digits. That included the run-out of Brook, who went for a second run but fell short of his crease to an electrifying throw from debutant Razaullah.

England lost quick wickets and slipped to 201-9 after Afridi removed Curran in his return spell when he holed out to fine leg off a mistimed pull. Razaullah took 2-38, grabbing the wickets of Jacks and Dawson.

Duckett, who hit 10 fours and two sixes in his 111-ball knock, fell in the 37th over when he top-edged a sweep to fine leg against left-arm spinner Arafat Minhas before Atkinson (36 not out) shared a 40-run last-wicket stand with Crocombe.

AP/ABC

World.title: Police investigate bullet inscribed with 'RAT' found on Victorian MP's car
World.content:
Police are investigating after Victoria's emergency services minister found a bullet on his car bonnet.

Paul Edbrooke, a former firefighter and the Labor state MP for Frankston, found the bullet on his car on Saturday.

The ABC understands the bullet was inscribed with "RAT" and his old firefighter number, when he returned to his car on Saturday.

Mr Edbrooke said there was a "small minority" of people in the United Firefighters Union (UFU) who thought threats and intimidation were acceptable but that that was not representative of firefighters.

A bullet was found on Labor MP Paul Edbrooke's car on Saturday. (ABC News: Darryl Torpy)

"This is a new low in a pattern of threatening behaviour against politicians and it has been reported to Victoria Police," he said.

"All politicians need to call out these threats and stop campaigning with these UFU members."

The UFU has been locked in an industrial dispute with Fire Rescue Victoria since 2021, with the union currently taking action at the Fair Work Commission over an Enterprise Bargaining Agreement.

In a statement, the UFU condemned the threat against Mr Edbrooke "without qualification" and called on Victoria Police to investigate it fully.

"Threatening anyone, including a minister we strongly disagree with, is the opposite of everything this union stands for," UFU Victorian branch secretary Peter Marshall said.

"Whoever did this does not speak or act for firefighters or for this union. I want police to find the person responsible.

"On Friday I said the premier and the minister were 'in the gun'.

"I meant at the ballot box and anyone there, or seeing the video, would know that."

Victoria Police confirmed its Security Investigation Unit was "investigating a threat against a member of Victorian parliament which is alleged to have occurred in the greater Frankston area".

"Detectives will investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident," a police spokesperson said.

Former Victorian premier Jacinta Allan worried MP would be killed More than a dozen Victorian MPs tell the ABC they have concerns over their safety.

Mr Marshall said the government was seeking to weaken protections for firefighters ahead of fire season.

"That is why we will keep asking Victorians to put Labor last on 28 November," he said.

"We will make that case with votes, never with threats."

Last Monday's attack on federal independent MP Helen Haines outside her electorate office in Wangaratta has drawn attention to the safety of MPs and other officials.

Ms Haines, 65, lost both of her legs after a car struck her in what police believe was a deliberate attack.

Ms Haines remains in a serious but stable condition at the Alfred Hospital.

Ahead of Victoria's state election on November 28, Victoria Police Commissioner Mike Bush has said police were taking a "proactive" approach to the security of politicians and to address any threats that may arise.

World.title: SA premier refers $15b project to ICAC over bikie 'infiltration' fears
World.content:
The South Australian government has taken the extraordinary step of referring its flagship infrastructure project to the corruption watchdog over fears of bikie "infiltration" in subcontracting works.

The $15 billion Torrens to Darlington road project has been rocked in recent days by what the government has described as reports an outlaw gang member "attempted to take an interest" in a since-suspended company that had been contracted to work on the project.

In a statement, Premier Peter Malinauskas said while he had seen no evidence organised crime "gained access" to the project, he had written to the state's ICAC commissioner, Emma Townsend.

Mr Malinauskas said he had asked the ICAC to examine integrity safeguards surrounding the project as part of an "evaluation of the project's procurement and contracting arrangements".

The move comes after pressure from the state opposition, which last week raised concerns about major projects being hijacked by criminals.

The government said such an ICAC investigation could examine "safeguards against improper influence, conflicts of interest and infiltration by organised crime".

"Given the scale and importance of this project, we have a responsibility to make sure the right safeguards are in place and working as they should," Mr Malinauskas said in a statement on Monday morning.

"That's why I've written to ICAC to request the Commissioner consider an independent evaluation.

"There is no evidence before the state government that organised crime has gained access to the Torrens to Darlington project.

"South Australia has been fortunate not to witness the sort of behaviour on major projects that has been seen on the eastern seaboard. I'm determined to keep it that way."

The government said it would be up to the ICAC to determine whether it investigated the matter.

It said it had requested ICAC's involvement as a precautionary measure to ensure taxpayer funds did not end up in the hands of organised crime.

"An independent evaluation would provide additional assurance that these safeguards are working effectively in practice and can identify and respond to attempts to exploit the project for corrupt purposes," the government said.

Last week, opposition spokesperson Ben Hood raised concerns about outlaw motorcycle gang members' possible involvement in project works.

"South Australia can't afford this and have its major projects hijacked," he said.

With a price tag of more than $15 billion — an amount that is being jointly funded by the state and federal governments — the Torrens to Darlington transport corridor upgrade has been described as the biggest-ever infrastructure project in SA.

"Our track record of keeping criminal elements out of our projects has set us apart from other states," Infrastructure and Transport Minister Joe Szakacs said.

"We have zero tolerance for criminal behaviour, intimidation, or violence on our projects and have strong requirements and protections in place to enforce this."

World.title: Remote community devastated over closure of Indigenous youth organisation
World.content:
An Indigenous youth organisation in Western Australia's north has shut its service without warning, leaving locals confused and children without a designated night space.

The Wyndham Aboriginal Youth Corporation (WYAC) has operated programs in the remote community, around 3,100 kilometres north of Perth, since 2018.

Until recently, it delivered a range of services, including a cafe, mechanic workshop, educational programs with certification pathways and a safe night space for young people.

WYAC has been credited with reducing crime rates and fostering positive community-led solutions.

However, the ABC has been told services stopped in mid-September with no warning.

Crashing down

Former WYAC chief executive Neville D'Silva claims the National Indigenous Australians Agency (NIAA) reneged on funding commitments, which left the service with limited options.

In a statement, NIAA said it was unable to comment publicly on grant management discussions with individual organisations, but said it was "continuing to engage with WYAC".

Neville D'Silva is hoping youth services can restart in the Kimberley town of Wyndham. (Supplied: Neville D'Silva)

Mr D'Silva, who said he had now returned to help WYAC, said his heart went out to the at-risk children and staff.

"These kids need somebody to take up the fight for them … now it has come crashing down," Mr D'Silva said.

"WYAC was the one providing them with social enterprise, education … crime came right down."

The service had been put on hold because NIAA "is not paying their share", according to Mr D'Silva.

"They're supposed to give us the cash flow from July, they didn't pay us that money, and that's why WYAC is in the situation they are in," he said.

"So the workers are sitting at home, there are no jobs, they're not getting paid."

Mr D'Silva, who stepped down from the CEO position for a period of time this year, said he was uncertain when services would operate again.

'Devastating' impact

Shire of Wyndham East Kimberley president David Menzel said it was "devastating" programs had halted.

Mr Menzel said he was worried about the impact on residents.

David Menzel says youth services are needed in the northern WA town. (ABC Kimberley: Giulia Bertoglio)

"I think we've become quite accustomed to the high level of service WYAC's been providing, a high level of engagement, particularly in the space of at-risk youth," Mr Menzel said.

"I'm not sure there's any other organisation in place to take on all of that, it's inevitable there'll be some gaps and I'm not sure what the outcome of the current situation will be."

A source familiar with WYAC, who the ABC has chosen to keep anonymous, said the operation stopped on September 18.

The small town of Wyndham is about 100km west of Kununurra in WA's Kimberley region. (ABC Kimberley: Giulia Bertoglio)

They said staff and community members had not been informed about the future of the organisation, despite repeated attempts at contact.

"We had no idea it was heading in this direction, it was just business as usual up until mid-September," they said.

" No-one really knows what's going to happen in terms of employment, whether they should be looking for a new job, nothing's been communicated. "

They said children in Wyndham approached them daily, asking when services would start again.

"It's absolutely devastating. The most important thing is the young people and the diversionary programs are no longer functioning," they said.

"The night space, which was a big part of keeping young people away from the streets, giving them an alternate safe space to go, is no longer operational."

The community of Wyndham is based in the northern Kimberley in Western Australia. (ABC Kimberley: Ted O'Connor)

In a statement, the Department of Justice said it recognised the importance of youth services to the Wyndham community and was focused on understanding the implications of the current disruptions.

It said it was engaging with relevant stakeholders to explore the options available to support the continuity of services.

World.title: Manchester United booed off pitch after calamitous defeat
World.content:
Michael Carrick patted his chest and gave an apologetic salute to the Manchester United fans who were applauding him, before trudging down the tunnel at the end of another bruising afternoon at Old Trafford.

Then came a chorus of boos for the United players walking behind him.

United had just lost 3-0 to Bournemouth again in the Premier League, and the disgruntled home support made it clear who they were behind in this latest sorry episode for a team that, not too long ago, was the pinnacle of English football.

Indeed, the only person to escape censure was the manager overseeing an eight-match winless run that is bringing more embarrassment to the country's biggest club.

"It hurts an awful lot to see us going through this at this moment in time," said an emotional-looking Carrick, who spoke of his "mixed emotions" during a match that further exposed the weakness in his fragile United team.

"It wasn't a farewell from me," Carrick added of post-match actions that saw him lead his players on a walk around the field.

"What it looks like, what is next — I really don't know. But I'll always do what's best for this football club."

Carrick is trying everything to get United out its perilous position, which sees the club languishing in 16th place in the 20-team Premier League.

That includes even dropping captain Bruno Fernandes.

Bruno Fernandes and Manchester United players traipse off (Getty Images: Marc Atkins)

The humbling by Bournemouth came four days after a humiliating 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League that was followed by critical comments to the media by Fernandes about Carrick's tactics.

Carrick responded by leaving the Portugal star — the player of the year in England last season — out of the team in what the manager described as a "pure football" decision.

Fernandes briefly went out to warm up at one point but never made it onto the field, where United defended woefully as Bournemouth scored through Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson.

Carrick's job is under huge threat, barely five months after he signed a permanent deal as manager after leading the team back into the Champions League while on a short-term contract in the second half of last season.

But getting rid of Carrick would not solve the huge problems at United, whose fans also chanted against Jason Wilcox, the club's director of football who was the target of recent criticism from defender Lisandro Martinez, and the Glazer family, the majority owners, before letting rip on the players.

United has won one of its eight league games this season — and that was at home to promoted Ipswich on August 30.

"It's nowhere near good enough," United defender Harry Maguire said.

"Something needs to change."

Manchester United fans have rarely felt such dejection at their club's form. (Getty Images: CameraSport/Dave Howarth)

As for Bournemouth, it has now beaten United 3-0 at Old Trafford in three of the last four seasons. On its other visit in that stretch, there was a 4-4 draw.

Brighton run ends at Anfield, Newcastle win

Brighton, the league's surprise package this season, was beaten 2-0 at Liverpool for its first defeat since August, after which the south-coast team embarked on a stunning run since that included two 5-0 wins and a 3-0 victory over defending champion Arsenal.

That streak ended in a tight game at Anfield, with Liverpool's goals coming in a four-minute span midway through the first half. Pascal Gross deflected Florian Wirtz's shot into his own net before Alexander Isak turned home Bradley Barcola's cross.

It was Liverpool's first league win at home under Andoni Iraola, hired as manager over the summer, and it lifted the team into fourth spot — a point and a place behind Brighton

Brighton had 64 per cent possession and 17 shots — though just one on target — and manager Fabian Hurzeler called it a "missed opportunity" for his team to further underline its status as a growing force.

"I think everyone in the stadium saw that there was one team who really tried to create and try to win this game," Hurzeler said, "and therefore I have to praise my players."

Newcastle beat Crystal Palace 2-0 thanks to second-half goals from William Osula and Harvey Barnes.

Hull and Brentford drew 1-1, while Sunderland and Leeds finished 0-0.

AP

World.title: Man caves are evolving to become backyard social hubs — and pubs
World.content:
"Welcome to The Cane and Council," Toby Chester says as he opens the door to the replica English pub he has built in his backyard.

It seems out of place in the humidity and tropical surroundings of his garden in Cairns, but it is carefully designed to have the look and feel of an English pub, complete with leather couches, Union Jack cushions and a dartboard on the wall.

This is no basic man cave and just one example of how simple home sheds are being transformed into customised social hubs.

And it seems to be a growing trend.

Toby Chester enjoyed fitting out the bar to resemble an English pub. (ABC Far North: Amanda Cranston)

The inspiration

Mr Chester said the idea started during the COVID-19 pandemic when people were creating spaces at home and posting about them on social media.

He was watching YouTube videos of people in England building pub sheds in their backyards, and he told his wife Karen: "That's what we're going to do."

Ms Chester loved the idea because they were looking at creating a second living area to allow his mother-in-law to move into their house.

A copper-inlaid and etched wooden bar, upholstered with an English-style fabric, was the first item purchased. (ABC Far North: Amanda Cranston)

They already had a steel-framed, cyclone-rated and approved shed in their backyard they no longer used, so they decided to convert it.

It has now become a social hub, not just for the family, but for friends as well.

Toby Chester has added lots of small touches, like a red phone box. (ABC Far North: Amanda Cranston)

Investing in home

Psychologist and Relationships Australia chief executive Elisabeth Shaw said a lot of people invested in home renovations during pandemic to create more personalised spaces for work and comfort.

"Our homes have become our sanctuary to unwind and switch off from the outside world," she said.

"They've become a refuge, both mentally and physically."

Elisabeth Shaw says people are rethinking how they socialise since COVID. (Supplied: Elisabeth Shaw)

Ms Shaw said the increased cost of living was also making people rethink how they socialised and who they wanted to spend time with.

She said people still wanted to share a glass of wine and a conversation with friends, but without the crowds.

Toby Chester loves his collection of brass badges taken from horse and buggy carts. (ABC Far North: Amanda Cranston)

A name with meaning

The Chesters wanted to give their pub a cool name to personalise it.

"We were looking for a two-word name, and my wife actually came up with The Cane and Council," Mr Chester said.

"We named it after my father-in-law who was a cane farmer and also a councillor on the Mulgrave Shire Council and Cairns Regional Council for nearly 30 years."

A graphic artist mate designed the logo. (ABC Far North: Amanda Cranston)

A graphic artist mate designed the logo, and they had it printed to look authentic.

Mr Chester said it was now their preferred living area, and used it for everything from watching television in the evening to entertaining friends.

His close mates even have their own key to the pub so they can swing by whenever they like.

He said converting the shed to a pub was the best thing they ever did, and his mates agreed.

"I just open the door and they turn up," Mr Chester said.

Across town, the Youngs turned their old stables into a speak-easy, keeping the red bricks and many original features. (ABC Far North: Amanda Cranston)

Pub inspires Bar

Entertaining at home clearly runs in the family. Mr Chester's sister Amy and her husband Phil Young have also built a dedicated social hub in their Cairns backyard.

"We didn't really think about it until my brother converted his own shed into an English pub," Mrs Young said.

"We were so blown away by it, it inspired us to create a space of our own."

The stables are separate from the house, which the Youngs say is ideal for entertaining. (ABC Far North: Amanda Cranston)

They converted old stables on their property into a modern speak-easy, which is less man cave and more upmarket bar.

And living close to the centre of town, they have now become the social hub for friends dropping in on their way into town.

Honouring its history

"Our house is an old post office that was built in the late 40s and ceased being a post office in the early 90s," Mrs Young said.

"This building in the backyard was originally the stables for the horses that used to deliver the mail in the area.

"So, we called the bar The Stables."

Whether drinking cocktails or coffee, The Stables has become a real social hub for their family and friends. (ABC Far North: Amanda Cranston)

Wanting to maintain the historical features of the building, the original red bricks remained a feature after being cleaned up and waterproofed.

They also custom-designed glass cabinets and a long bar to create a whisky bar feel.

The cabinet at the back was specially made to fit the space. (ABC Far North: Amanda Cranston)

Entertainment hub

With double couches, large television screens on either side of the room and a good coffee machine, Mr Young said The Stables had become his second lounge room during the week.

"I wish we had converted the stables when we first moved in because the space has become a much-loved hub of the home," he said.

Amy and Phil Young wish they had built the speak-easy sooner. (ABC Far North: Amanda Cranston)

Mrs Young uses The Stables more on weekends when her girlfriends come over, even creating a signature cocktail for their bar.

Tying in with the horse theme, she created the Pink Pony Club cocktail.

But whether coffee or cocktails are the choice of beverage, the Youngs say The Stables has certainly become the social hub they hoped it would be.

World.title: A bullet on the windscreen, a firefighter’s old badge number: The message left on a Victorian minister’s car
World.content:

Emergency Services Minister Paul Edbrooke has hit out at the United Firefighters Union after a bullet engraved with the word “RAT” and his former firefighter number was left on his car windscreen in Frankston over the weekend. Police are investigating. A bullet left on the windscreen of Paul Edbrooke’s car over the weekend. The threat against Edbrooke came just days after federal MP Helen Haines was allegedly deliberately hit by a car outside her electorate office, an incident that has put the safety and security of elected officials at the forefront of national discourse. Haines remains serious but stable in the Alfred hospital, having lost both her legs in the car crash in Wangaratta. The driver, Brendan Nugent, is now behind bars, charged with several offences.



“This is a new low in a pattern of threatening behaviour against politicians,” Edbrooke said in a statement. “There is a small minority in the UFU who think threats and intimidation are acceptable - this does not represent our firefighters.” Edbrooke worked as a firefighter in Frankston for 14 years, during which he served as the station’s workplace representative for the UFU and fought the Black Saturday bushfires in Marysville and Kinglake. He told ABC radio, the threat was clearly linked to his firefighting past. Emergency Services Minister Paul Edbrooke has taken aim at the UFU after finding the engraved bullet. The Age Edbrooke said he suspected the UFU because very few people knew his five-digit ID number. “The only people I’m really getting aggressive threats from at the moment are members of that union,” he said.



“It’s one thing to be an armchair critic and say what you want from behind a computer. It’s another thing to follow somebody and put something on their car like a bullet.” Related Article Exclusive

Industrial relations Firefighters shocked after union sends them debt recovery letters He added that the small group of UFU members he was referring to “believe everything they are told by the leadership and think that by someone intimidating or bullying me, I will support them and give them a taxpayer-funded slush fund for the union. It ain’t gonna happen”. Edbrooke clarified that there was an issue with an income protection scheme going to the UFU, when he believed it should go to firefighters directly. “That’s what this is about. It’s not about firefighter safety or staffing. There is no threat to that from the state government.”



He urged candidates from other parties to stop campaigning with the UFU. “The message I’d like to get out there to all [election] candidates is: if you enjoy our democracy, the standard you walk past in the standard you accept,” he said. Opposition leader Jess Wilson said her thoughts were with Edbrooke. “I can’t imagine how upsetting it is for him and for his family,” she said. “There’s just no place for these sort of threats and intimidation in Victoria or this country.” Edbrooke has also recently been the target of a fresh campaign by the UFU: Since Wednesday, it has been running televised ads urging people to put Labor last in next month’s state election, angry that the government wants to end enforceable minimum staffing for firefighters.



“Firefighters beat these arguments in court when a Liberal government ran them. Now a Labor government is running the Liberals’ case against its own firefighters,” said UFU Secretary Peter Marshall in a statement announcing the ad blitz. “Minister Edbrooke can end this with the stroke of a pen. Until he does, firefighters will tell voters the truth.” Marshall also addressed union members on Friday, saying Edbrooke and Premier Ben Carroll would be “in the gun” if they affected his members. On Monday, Marshall clarified this comment. “I meant at the ballot box and anyone there, or seeing the video, would know that,” he said.



“Threatening anyone, including a minister we strongly disagree with, is the opposite of everything this union stands for. I condemn it without qualification.” Marshall said whoever had planted the bullet did not act for his union or for firefighters more generally, and that he hoped police found the culprit. The union has also been locked in a years-long pay dispute with the government, which remains before the Fair Work Commission. In August, Fire Rescue Victoria firefighters urged the government to intervene, alleging Marshall was stalling the negotiations. “We stand ready to give firefighters the pay rise they want, but we won’t be including any kind of slush fund in that agreement,” Edbrooke said. Michael Carrick is on the brink of being sacked as Manchester United manager. The 45-year-old’s future at Old Trafford is hanging by a thread after United slumped to a sixth loss in 12 games this season with a 3-0 thrashing at home to Bournemouth. Loading The result leaves them just a point above the relegation zone. The United hierarchy could be about to move for their third manager this year after a miserable day when furious fans unleashed their anger on co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the players.



As of 8pm on Sunday (Monday, 7am AEDT), it was understood that no formal decision had been taken on Carrick’s future. Asked whether he expected to be sacked, Carrick said: “I totally understand the situation. I’m not expecting anything either way. I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I’ll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made. Michael Carrick reacts to supporters after his team lost. AP Photo/Dave Thompson “It’s a tough situation; there’s no hiding from it. What it looks like and what’s next I really don’t know. I love what I do, and I feel the responsibility – we’ll have to wait and see. I take responsibility. I respect the position that I’m in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now?” ‘Carrick wants to be changed’



Carrick said he had yet to discuss his future with Wilcox or Omar Berrada, the chief executive, who shook his head in disbelief in the directors’ box when Bournemouth scored their second shortly before half-time. “No, just briefly they came down like they always do after a game, but nothing out of the ordinary,” Carrick said. Manchester United player Mason Mount after his side’s loss to Bournemouth. Getty Images Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher both believe Carrick will lose his job. “It’s become untenable,” Carragher said on Sky Sports. “Carrick wants to be changed. He doesn’t want to be sat in the dugout with those players. Can you imagine going into the training ground tomorrow with Bruno Fernandes after not bringing him on? He wants to be put out of his misery tonight.”



Neville, the former United captain, added: “It’s going to be ridiculously difficult for Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. Those two [Berrada and Wilcox] are probably going to make a decision that will disgust Manchester United fans but is probably necessary. It’s just an absolute mess. The football club is a mess right now.” Carrick, who had dropped captain Fernandes and refused to bring him on in the wake of the midfielder’s criticism of his tactics after Wednesday’s 4-1 trouncing by Como, was supported throughout the game by United fans in stark contrast to the abuse directed at the ownership, hierarchy and players. Loading As soon as Carrick had disappeared down the tunnel, the Stretford End – who had targeted the Glazers and Ratcliffe as well as Wilcox – rained down a torrent of boos on the players trailing behind the manager. Carrick had cut a forlorn figure as he walked around the pitch at the end, applauding the fans who sang his name and, at one point, placing a hand over his heart and banging his chest. But Carrick denied that this was him saying goodbye.



“It wasn’t a farewell from me,” he said. “I probably didn’t really expect that off the supporters, if I’m honest, but I’ve always felt the support and that connection with them. It will take a bit of time to digest, but I certainly appreciate their support. It’s difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion. Related Article Analysis

Premier League Foreign money is reshaping the A-League. The benefits come with strings attached “I’m feeling it for my players; they’re going through a tough spell. There’s a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there’s a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair. It’s not like they don’t care or they want to be in this position. The ones I’ve spoken to, it’s affecting them a lot.” However, Neville blasted the players and suggested they were no longer playing for Carrick. “They’ve downed tools and they’ve done this a number of times,” he said. “They decide when to switch it on and off like a tap.” Harry Maguire – who was captain in Fernandes’s absence – defended Carrick, despite another risible showing. This was the third 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in four games at Old Trafford during which time United have conceded 13 goals.



“At the moment we’re not doing enough as players,” Maguire said. “Michael turned our season on its head last year, and we played brilliant football and got brilliant results. This season we haven’t performed well enough as individuals. “We have got to find something, question yourself, look in the mirror; that’s the most important thing – think what you can do more and contribute to the team and if we do that we’ll get somewhere.” The Telegraph, London

World.content:
NationalNSWPublic transport Minns’ $6.8 billion election promise for key passenger train line Matt O'Sullivan and Jessica McSweeney October 26, 2026 — 9:38am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. About $6.8 billion will be funnelled into removing bottlenecks on the passenger train line from Sydney to the South Coast and electrifying it all the way to Bomaderry as part of a re-election pledge by the Minns Labor government. In the pitch to Illawarra and Shoalhaven voters ahead of the March state election, Labor has vowed to electrify the rail line between Kiama and Bomaderry, which would allow ageing diesel trains to be replaced by new electric double-deckers. It would give passengers a direct service to Central Station in Sydney by removing the need to switch trains at Kiama. Premier Chris Minns (right) and Transport Minister John Graham in the driver’s cabin of a refurbished Tangara passenger train last year. Peter Rae The work would also involve installing extra tracks and passing loops between Wollongong and Kiama, which is mostly single track. In addition, the two rail tracks between Hurstville and Sutherland in Sydney would be doubled to four, allowing the T4 Illawarra and South Coast lines to be separated in that congested section of the network.



Construction on extending the electrified line and duplicating tracks – if Labor is re-elected – is not expected to be completed until the mid to late 2030s. Detailed planning works would start next year. Related Article Trains New long-distance passenger trains will now be five years late The campaign pledge comes two days after the government backflipped on a shake-up to Sydney’s rail timetable following a backlash from train commuters. The new timetable would have led to longer journey times but extra services for passengers travelling on key corridors such as the T4 Eastern Suburbs and Illawarra, and the South Coast lines. The T4 and South Coast lines together carry about 250,000 passengers a day, or a quarter of Sydney Trains’ patronage. Premier Chris Minns said South Coast communities needed faster, more frequent and reliable trains, describing his government’s pledge as being the “largest investment in rail infrastructure in generations” for the region.



“For too long, the Liberals only funded Sydney metros, while regional communities missed out,” he said. Labor’s latest plan for the South Coast involves an immediate $621 million to upgrade critical infrastructure such as signalling and raising sections of track ahead of electrification and duplication work. The government will also consider within the next two months final business cases for extensions of metro or heavy rail lines in Sydney’s outer west. While the existing metro lines are popular with commuters, Minns has repeatedly said they are expensive projects and have come at the cost of the existing heavy rail passenger network. “Most people still use the heavy rail network ... [and] that needs some love because at the moment it’s too unreliable,” he said on Friday. The latest election commitment comes as the government anticipates a fight against One Nation in regions such as the South Coast, where Labor holds all seats from Bega to Wollongong after a 2025 byelection win in Kiama.



Local frustration about unreliable and ageing rail infrastructure was a significant bugbear for locals during the byelection campaign, which resulted in Labor winning the seat with a healthy swing. Related Article Public transport Sydney-Wollongong commuters finally get start date for new intercity trains During a visit to Eurobodalla in August, Minns said he was concerned about regions like the South Coast where he described the “threat” to Labor posed by people considering voting One Nation for the first time. And amid a threat from One Nation to Labor seats in the Hunter, the government’s signature $12 billion election commitment involves building a train manufacturing plant on a former mine site at Teralba in Lake Macquarie. Under that plan, the facility would build trains to replace the ageing Tangara fleet used predominantly on the T4 line. Election results are being tallied in Brazil, where confusion about extended polling hours at the last minute, forced counting to stop earlier this morning.

Brazil’s Supreme Court issued an extension of voting hours across the nation as some booths were closing for the day, while its electoral authorities began — and then suddenly paused — counting ballots in one of the most tightly contested elections in its history.

The order from Judge Cristiano Zanin came minutes after polls were due to close at 5pm Sunday (Brasilia time), and allowed voting to continue until 7pm. It followed requests from both candidates, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and challenger Flávio Bolsonaro.

The incumbent requested extensions nationwide over public transit problems in numerous states, including Sao Paulo — Brazil’s most populous — where 100 per cent of buses where supposed to run as per a weekday schedule but ran at 60 per cent, and Bahia, a key north-eastern stronghold for the leftist leader.

World.title: ‘Glad we checked our tickets’: First international flight departs Western Sydney
World.content:
Breaking BusinessCompaniesAviation ‘Glad we checked our tickets’: First international flight departs Western Sydney Chris Zappone October 26, 2026 — 9:24am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. As the new airport opens in western Sydney, we take a look at how it became a reality. See all stories .

The first international commercial flight from Western Sydney International (WSI) has departed this morning for Auckland. Air New Zealand flight NZ166 took off shortly after 9am as the first international departure from the airport. It comes after the plane touched down this morning after arriving from Auckland, marking the first international arrival for Sydney’s second airport. NZ165 landed at WSI at 7.27am from Auckland on Monday, 18 minutes earlier than expected. It marks the start of the airline’s travel to WSI, where it will fly three times weekly from Auckland. Matt and Serena Ross are among the passengers on the flight to Auckland. Chris Zappone NZ166 passengers Matt and Serena Ross said they were pleased with the option of a second airport in Sydney. “It’s a milestone event, so it’s special to be part of that,” said Serena. “Having more options for Kiwi travellers to come here will be great.”



“It’s nice to see a flash new airport up and running,” said Matt, but added the opening of WSI came as “a bit of surprise”. Related Article Western Sydney International ‘Final piece of the puzzle’: Western Sydney Airport opens for business The couple took a long Uber ride to arrive at WSI. They had assumed when they booked their tickets they would be leaving from Kingsford-Smith Airport at Mascot. “Glad we checked our tickets to verify what airport they were flying out of,” he said. Air New Zealand will fly three times weekly to Auckland, serving the existing community and business ties between western Sydney and New Zealand. It will be followed by Singapore Airlines in November, and Fiji Airways and Qatar Airways next year.



Air New Zealand chief operations officer Kate Boyer said in “Western Sydney for us there’s a huge Kiwi population here, a big expat community, so there are friends and family connections.” “There’s business and trade links, there’s cargo, so it’s a fantastic destination.” Air New Zealand has probably the strongest Pacific destination network in the world, Boyer said with “huge connections into all of the Pacific islands that we serve.” In opening flights to WSI, the airline expects to be “able to connect people back to their family in New Zealand or the broader Pacific region.”



There are hopes by the federal government that this curfew-free airport offers the kind of flexibility for international carriers that helps bring in more business and visitors and allows for more flexibility for Australians going abroad. While Sydney’s time difference with New Zealand is only two hours, coordinating connections for long-haul flights at much more distant hubs in Asia or the Middle East is more difficult from Australian airports where curfews apply. Being able to take off and land 24 hours a day is expected to aid long-haul carriers serving Australia. People arrive to the brand new Western Sydney International Airport on opening day. Audrey Richardson WSI’s first domestic flight – a Jetstar flight to the Gold Coast – took place yesterday.



And some are hopeful that flying from WSI will give Air New Zealand a bigger slice of the trans-Tasman travel. Trans-Tasman corporate bookings are on the rise, increasing 8.4 per cent year-on-year, according to Flight Centre data. Flight capacity across all carriers on the Australia-New Zealand route is also on track to grow through the rest of the year, Flight Centre said, with seat numbers rising seven and eight per cent year-on-year in the final three months of the year. Air New Zealand’s flight will give the western Sydney business community “direct access to New Zealand for the first time,” said Renos Rologas, ANZ General Manager of FCM Travel, Flight Centre Travel Group’s corporate travel outfit.



“It’s also a fitting backdrop for this quarter’s booking growth, led by construction, manufacturing, and healthcare and social assistance – sectors with people and projects on the ground on both sides of the Tasman.” Air New Zealand general manager of short haul, Lucy Hall, said that for businesses and travellers across western Sydney, WSI “provides a new, convenient gateway to New Zealand” that also gives the wider Sydney market a fresh choice of two airports. Related Article Airports ‘Slow burn’: Western Sydney Airport’s real challenge awaits after launch For some customers, it will ease the journey to and from the airport, and for those who travel for work, this will be a plus.



“Together, the additional capacity, new airport options and greater flexibility give us real confidence about the opportunity for trans-Tasman business travel over the year ahead,” Hall said. World.content:
NationalQueenslandCrime Victim shot in head remains critical as hunt for gunmen continues Cameron Atfield and Courtney Kruk October 26, 2026 — 9:15am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. A manhunt is under way for the shooter and accomplices behind a drive-by shooting in Logan on Saturday night that injured four people, including a teenage bystander who was shot in the head. Police responded to reports of gunshots fired from a vehicle outside the Fitzy’s Loganholme centre on Bryants Road, where a boxing event was being held, about 8.15pm on Saturday. A 19-year-old Jimboomba woman was shot in the head and neck and rushed to Brisbane’s Princess Alexandra Hospital in a critical condition. People had gathered outside during an intermission of the boxing event when they were fired upon by masked gunmen. Cameron Atfield She remained in a critical condition on Monday.



Three other people – a 38-year-old Browns Plains man, a 37-year-old Salisbury man and a 27-year-old Cornubia man – were shot in the abdomen and received surgery. All were in a stable condition on Sunday. Loading Detective Inspector Ian Galpin said he was appalled the young woman’s life now hung in the balance, telling reporters on Sunday she was not believed to be the group’s intended target. “I believe she is an innocent bystander,” Galpin said.



“It’s horrific. It’s something that her family should never have to go through.” Galpin said event organisers told police there was nothing to suggest something might occur before “at least half-a-dozen shots” were fired at people standing near a drop-off zone outside the venue from the front passenger window of a Mitsubishi. Witnesses and CCTV saw two men wearing balaclavas and gloves in the vehicle. Police continue to search for them and at least one other person believed to have picked them up after they set the Mitsubishi on fire.



The car was found set alight on Maloney Road at Waterford West. A second vehicle collected the pair and Galpin said they had reason to believe one of them might have been burnt. A dual-cab ute was also set alight on Beaudesert Road at Tamborine. Galpin said investigations were under way to see if that second vehicle was involved in the incident. Related Article Updated

Queensland Police Young woman critical, multiple people hospitalised in drive-by shooting south of Brisbane Taskforce Maxima, the Queensland police bikie squad, is involved in the investigation. Logan Mayor Jon Raven said he was not aware of any significant bikie activity in his city.



“Police said there is no further threat and we have to trust our men and women in blue and their assessment,” Raven said. “But more than that, the people that you see every day in the streets of Logan are good people. They’re your friends. They’re your neighbours. They’re part of your community. Police at the scene on Sunday. Cameron Atfield “These individuals do not represent the people of Logan, and they do not represent what we’re about.” In a statement on Sunday, organisers for the boxing event – Logan City Tiles – said they were “heartbroken” and were praying for the full recovery of all victims.



“These types of incidents have no place in the boxing community or any part of the broader community. Right now, our thoughts go out to the victims and all that were affected.” Premier David Crisafulli said he hoped the offenders would be brought to justice swiftly and he pledged to exercise strong new laws to prosecute the shooters. “Earlier this year, we passed amongst the strongest new laws for drive-by shooting in the country, and it’s my hope that these people responsible for it are arrested and that those new laws apply to them,” he said. Police will provide an update on the incident on Monday. Get alerts on significant breaking news as happens.

World.title: ‘An A-plus character’: The prospect from a family of Essendon diehards who could kickstart the Dons
World.content:
SportAFLAFL 2026 ‘An A-plus character’: The prospect from a family of Essendon diehards who could kickstart the Dons Marc McGowan Updated October 26, 2026 — 9:09am ,first published 5:00am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. A decade after Essendon overlooked future All-Australian Hugh McCluggage for Andy McGrath, the Bombers have the chance for a do-over-of-sorts. Next month’s draft marks the first time since that 2016 edition that Essendon will have the No.1 pick, which they have privately committed to using on Port Adelaide’s academy prodigy Dougie Cochrane. Ethan Drever could be the No.2 pick in next month’s AFL draft. AFL Photos The Power will match the Bombers’ bid on Cochrane – this year’s consensus best prospect – but what Essendon do next is the fascinating part. They could place another bid on Carlton’s father-son gun Cody Walker, but the expectation is they will select someone not linked to another club. Ethan Drever, a 188-centimetre midfielder from Ballarat, may be that player.



Editor's pick AFL 2026 Exquisitely talented, daring, smart: This Brighton Grammar footy captain is shaking up the draft Like McCluggage, Drever came through the GWV Rebels program and has emerged as one of the outstanding options at the pointy end of the draft. The similarities don’t end with the club and positions they play, either. “Ethan’s an A-plus type of character,” Rebels talent operations lead Brooke Brown told The Age. “He’s the most beautiful individual, both on and off the field, in regards to how he’s interacted with all the Rebels staff, players and families. This kid couldn’t get into trouble if he tried. “I worked with Hugh McCluggage when he was at the Rebels, and I see so many Hugh McCluggage traits [in Drever]. Nothing fazes him, and he just gets on with the job. As a leader, he’s not boisterous or in your face. He leads by example and by skill.”



Drever is in the mix at Essendon’s top selection. AFL Photos McCluggage joined Harris Andrews and Josh Dunkley as a Brisbane Lions co-captain this past season after long being highly regarded for his leadership, standard-setting and emotional intelligence. Another commonality between the Rebels graduates is that they can both seriously play, although Drever’s smooth-moving playing style and ability to impact the game inside and outside the contest is most often likened to GWS star Finn Callaghan. Drever honed in on Callaghan when those comparisons started flooding in, but also closely studied McCluggage, Hawk Will Day and Adelaide captain Jordan Dawson. “I want to be a powerful player,” Drever said. “I love running out the front of the stoppage and being attacking, but I’d also love to be [known as] a two-way runner and really good defensive midfielder.”



The defensive side of Drever’s game was not a strength in the early part of his Rebels tenure, according to Brown, but he quickly changed that and has a reputation as a quick learner. Related Article AFL 2026 ‘Spelling mistakes everywhere’: How an email from the heart got this AFL prospect a scholarship He is a great athlete, too, which was rammed home at the draft combine, where he finished fifth in the 20-metre sprint and top 10 in both vertical jump tests. After spending much of the previous two seasons across halfback and on a wing, Rebels coach David “Deeks” Loader unleashed Drever – as promised – through the midfield with great effect in 2026. He averaged 28 disposals, 14 contested possessions and seven clearances. The 18-year-old won Vic Country’s MVP award at this year’s AFL under-18 championships, was an All-Australian, made the Talent League’s team of the year, and claimed the Rebels’ best-and-fairest award.



“‘Deeks’ put me at half-back in my bottom-age 18s season, just to start my Rebels journey, which was really good, but this year I was always going to move into the middle,” he said. “He just wanted me to get used to the speed of the game, and I think it really helped me.” Drever could join Essendon’s top draftees from last year: (from left) Jacob Farrow, Sullivan Robey and Dyson Sharp. Justin McManus Drever is now viewed as the prototypical big-bodied midfielder for the modern game, but it was not that long ago that he was a more modest 178 centimetres and regularly being blocked at the rim in his previous sporting life as a basketballer. The Rebels don’t have their own resident gym like some other Talent League clubs, but he has also taken it upon himself to become more physically imposing.



Related Article AFL 2026 Who the players rate as the cream of the crop in this year’s AFL draft “It’s made a big difference. Being a bit taller, and putting on some size helps so much with my power and confidence as well,” Drever said. “Having that confidence is massive because you know you can take a hit and not be afraid to get tackled as you’re coming out of a stoppage. I think confidence is a huge part of sport – mentally and physically – and it’s something I’ve tried to really improve.” The rebuilding Bombers used first-round picks last year on Sullivan Robey, Jacob Farrow and Dyson Sharp, who could all end up part of a new-look on-ball brigade. Drever’s skillset – if they draft him – would complement that group. He ticks numerous boxes for what Essendon need, and even comes from a family of Bomber diehards. “I’ve heard they’ve got a bit of interest, which is pretty cool, and it’s awesome to be in consideration,” Drever said. “My whole family’s excited about that because they’re all Essendon supporters.”

Residents of south-east Queensland are bracing for another wet week as a weather system bringing heavy rain and possible storms persists across the region. Rain soaked broad parts of eastern and south-eastern Australia at the weekend, with Queensland copping the highest rainfall totals, according to the Bureau of Meteorology. The inland Wide Bay-Burnett region north of Brisbane and the Central Ranges recorded between 200-300 millimetres of rain by the end of Sunday. More rain is on the way for soaked parts of Queensland. Catherine Strohfeldt “[It’s been an] incredibly wet weekend across southern Queensland, which has continued over the last week due to a blocking high-pressure system in the Tasman Sea,” senior meteorologist Sarah Scully said.



“Many parts of Queensland have seen two to four times their average October rainfall in the last week.” Related Article Extreme weather Storms over south-east lifting but system threatens supercells on way Scully said a severe storm “stalled” over the Darling Downs in the early hours of Monday morning, dropping more than 100 millimetres of rain over 12 hours in parts. A severe thunderstorm warning in place across south-east Queensland, including the south-east coast, Darling Downs and Granite Belt, was cancelled just after 7am. Senior meteorologist Angus Hines said the storms had weakened and were moving out across the water, but with warmer temperatures could return after midday, particularly over the border in the Northern Rivers region of NSW.



“The temperature [today] is back to that 30–31 degrees range,” Hines said. “[It’s] fairly humid as well, lots of moisture around after the recent rainfall. “So about lunchtime or perhaps early afternoon, we could see more severe storms around the area.” Hines said the week ahead would bring “longer nice weather gaps” between rain, cloud cover and cooler temperatures, with conditions easing by the weekend. “Thursday [and] Friday looks like overall much brighter conditions with just a lower chance of showers.



“More of this week should be bright and clean.” Get alerts on significant breaking news as happens.

World.title: A bullet on the windscreen, a firefighter’s old badge number: The message left on a Victorian minister’s car
World.content:
NationalVictoriaEmergency services A bullet on the windscreen, a firefighter’s old badge number: The message left on a Victorian minister’s car Alexander Darling October 26, 2026 — 10:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Emergency Services Minister Paul Edbrooke has hit out at the United Firefighters Union after a bullet engraved with the word “RAT” and his former firefighter number was left on his car windscreen in Frankston over the weekend. Police are investigating. A bullet left on the windscreen of Paul Edbrooke’s car over the weekend. The threat against Edbrooke came just days after federal MP Helen Haines was allegedly deliberately hit by a car outside her electorate office, an incident that has put the safety and security of elected officials at the forefront of national discourse. Haines remains serious but stable in the Alfred hospital, having lost both her legs in the car crash in Wangaratta. The driver, Brendan Nugent, is now behind bars, charged with several offences.



“This is a new low in a pattern of threatening behaviour against politicians,” Edbrooke said in a statement. “There is a small minority in the UFU who think threats and intimidation are acceptable - this does not represent our firefighters.” Edbrooke worked as a firefighter in Frankston for 14 years, during which he served as the station’s workplace representative for the UFU and fought the Black Saturday bushfires in Marysville and Kinglake. He told ABC radio, the threat was clearly linked to his firefighting past. Emergency Services Minister Paul Edbrooke has taken aim at the UFU after finding the engraved bullet. The Age Edbrooke said he suspected the UFU because very few people knew his five-digit ID number. “The only people I’m really getting aggressive threats from at the moment are members of that union,” he said.



“It’s one thing to be an armchair critic and say what you want from behind a computer. It’s another thing to follow somebody and put something on their car like a bullet.” Related Article Exclusive

Industrial relations Firefighters shocked after union sends them debt recovery letters He added that the small group of UFU members he was referring to “believe everything they are told by the leadership and think that by someone intimidating or bullying me, I will support them and give them a taxpayer-funded slush fund for the union. It ain’t gonna happen”. Edbrooke clarified that there was an issue with an income protection scheme going to the UFU, when he believed it should go to firefighters directly. “That’s what this is about. It’s not about firefighter safety or staffing. There is no threat to that from the state government.”



He urged candidates from other parties to stop campaigning with the UFU. “The message I’d like to get out there to all [election] candidates is: if you enjoy our democracy, the standard you walk past in the standard you accept,” he said. Opposition leader Jess Wilson said her thoughts were with Edbrooke. “I can’t imagine how upsetting it is for him and for his family,” she said. “There’s just no place for these sort of threats and intimidation in Victoria or this country.” Edbrooke has also recently been the target of a fresh campaign by the UFU: Since Wednesday, it has been running televised ads urging people to put Labor last in next month’s state election, angry that the government wants to end enforceable minimum staffing for firefighters.



“Firefighters beat these arguments in court when a Liberal government ran them. Now a Labor government is running the Liberals’ case against its own firefighters,” said UFU Secretary Peter Marshall in a statement announcing the ad blitz. “Minister Edbrooke can end this with the stroke of a pen. Until he does, firefighters will tell voters the truth.” Marshall also addressed union members on Friday, saying Edbrooke and Premier Ben Carroll would be “in the gun” if they affected his members. On Monday, Marshall clarified this comment. “I meant at the ballot box and anyone there, or seeing the video, would know that,” he said.



“Threatening anyone, including a minister we strongly disagree with, is the opposite of everything this union stands for. I condemn it without qualification.” Marshall said whoever had planted the bullet did not act for his union or for firefighters more generally, and that he hoped police found the culprit. The union has also been locked in a years-long pay dispute with the government, which remains before the Fair Work Commission. In August, Fire Rescue Victoria firefighters urged the government to intervene, alleging Marshall was stalling the negotiations. “We stand ready to give firefighters the pay rise they want, but we won’t be including any kind of slush fund in that agreement,” Edbrooke said. Michael Carrick is on the brink of being sacked as Manchester United manager. The 45-year-old’s future at Old Trafford is hanging by a thread after United slumped to a sixth loss in 12 games this season with a 3-0 thrashing at home to Bournemouth. Loading The result leaves them just a point above the relegation zone. The United hierarchy could be about to move for their third manager this year after a miserable day when furious fans unleashed their anger on co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the players.



As of 8pm on Sunday (Monday, 7am AEDT), it was understood that no formal decision had been taken on Carrick’s future. Asked whether he expected to be sacked, Carrick said: “I totally understand the situation. I’m not expecting anything either way. I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I’ll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made. Michael Carrick reacts to supporters after his team lost. AP Photo/Dave Thompson “It’s a tough situation; there’s no hiding from it. What it looks like and what’s next I really don’t know. I love what I do, and I feel the responsibility – we’ll have to wait and see. I take responsibility. I respect the position that I’m in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now?” ‘Carrick wants to be changed’



Carrick said he had yet to discuss his future with Wilcox or Omar Berrada, the chief executive, who shook his head in disbelief in the directors’ box when Bournemouth scored their second shortly before half-time. “No, just briefly they came down like they always do after a game, but nothing out of the ordinary,” Carrick said. Manchester United player Mason Mount after his side’s loss to Bournemouth. Getty Images Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher both believe Carrick will lose his job. “It’s become untenable,” Carragher said on Sky Sports. “Carrick wants to be changed. He doesn’t want to be sat in the dugout with those players. Can you imagine going into the training ground tomorrow with Bruno Fernandes after not bringing him on? He wants to be put out of his misery tonight.”



Neville, the former United captain, added: “It’s going to be ridiculously difficult for Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. Those two [Berrada and Wilcox] are probably going to make a decision that will disgust Manchester United fans but is probably necessary. It’s just an absolute mess. The football club is a mess right now.” Carrick, who had dropped captain Fernandes and refused to bring him on in the wake of the midfielder’s criticism of his tactics after Wednesday’s 4-1 trouncing by Como, was supported throughout the game by United fans in stark contrast to the abuse directed at the ownership, hierarchy and players. Loading As soon as Carrick had disappeared down the tunnel, the Stretford End – who had targeted the Glazers and Ratcliffe as well as Wilcox – rained down a torrent of boos on the players trailing behind the manager. Carrick had cut a forlorn figure as he walked around the pitch at the end, applauding the fans who sang his name and, at one point, placing a hand over his heart and banging his chest. But Carrick denied that this was him saying goodbye.



“It wasn’t a farewell from me,” he said. “I probably didn’t really expect that off the supporters, if I’m honest, but I’ve always felt the support and that connection with them. It will take a bit of time to digest, but I certainly appreciate their support. It’s difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion. Related Article Analysis

Premier League Foreign money is reshaping the A-League. The benefits come with strings attached “I’m feeling it for my players; they’re going through a tough spell. There’s a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there’s a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair. It’s not like they don’t care or they want to be in this position. The ones I’ve spoken to, it’s affecting them a lot.” However, Neville blasted the players and suggested they were no longer playing for Carrick. “They’ve downed tools and they’ve done this a number of times,” he said. “They decide when to switch it on and off like a tap.” Harry Maguire – who was captain in Fernandes’s absence – defended Carrick, despite another risible showing. This was the third 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in four games at Old Trafford during which time United have conceded 13 goals.



“At the moment we’re not doing enough as players,” Maguire said. “Michael turned our season on its head last year, and we played brilliant football and got brilliant results. This season we haven’t performed well enough as individuals. “We have got to find something, question yourself, look in the mirror; that’s the most important thing – think what you can do more and contribute to the team and if we do that we’ll get somewhere.” The Telegraph, London

World.title: Minns’ $6.8 billion election promise for key passenger train line
World.content:
NationalNSWPublic transport Minns’ $6.8 billion election promise for key passenger train line Matt O'Sullivan and Jessica McSweeney October 26, 2026 — 9:38am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. About $6.8 billion will be funnelled into removing bottlenecks on the passenger train line from Sydney to the South Coast and electrifying it all the way to Bomaderry as part of a re-election pledge by the Minns Labor government. In the pitch to Illawarra and Shoalhaven voters ahead of the March state election, Labor has vowed to electrify the rail line between Kiama and Bomaderry, which would allow ageing diesel trains to be replaced by new electric double-deckers. It would give passengers a direct service to Central Station in Sydney by removing the need to switch trains at Kiama. Premier Chris Minns (right) and Transport Minister John Graham in the driver’s cabin of a refurbished Tangara passenger train last year. Peter Rae The work would also involve installing extra tracks and passing loops between Wollongong and Kiama, which is mostly single track. In addition, the two rail tracks between Hurstville and Sutherland in Sydney would be doubled to four, allowing the T4 Illawarra and South Coast lines to be separated in that congested section of the network.



Construction on extending the electrified line and duplicating tracks – if Labor is re-elected – is not expected to be completed until the mid to late 2030s. Detailed planning works would start next year. Related Article Trains New long-distance passenger trains will now be five years late The campaign pledge comes two days after the government backflipped on a shake-up to Sydney’s rail timetable following a backlash from train commuters. The new timetable would have led to longer journey times but extra services for passengers travelling on key corridors such as the T4 Eastern Suburbs and Illawarra, and the South Coast lines. The T4 and South Coast lines together carry about 250,000 passengers a day, or a quarter of Sydney Trains’ patronage. Premier Chris Minns said South Coast communities needed faster, more frequent and reliable trains, describing his government’s pledge as being the “largest investment in rail infrastructure in generations” for the region.



“For too long, the Liberals only funded Sydney metros, while regional communities missed out,” he said. Labor’s latest plan for the South Coast involves an immediate $621 million to upgrade critical infrastructure such as signalling and raising sections of track ahead of electrification and duplication work. The government will also consider within the next two months final business cases for extensions of metro or heavy rail lines in Sydney’s outer west. While the existing metro lines are popular with commuters, Minns has repeatedly said they are expensive projects and have come at the cost of the existing heavy rail passenger network. “Most people still use the heavy rail network ... [and] that needs some love because at the moment it’s too unreliable,” he said on Friday. The latest election commitment comes as the government anticipates a fight against One Nation in regions such as the South Coast, where Labor holds all seats from Bega to Wollongong after a 2025 byelection win in Kiama.



Local frustration about unreliable and ageing rail infrastructure was a significant bugbear for locals during the byelection campaign, which resulted in Labor winning the seat with a healthy swing. Related Article Public transport Sydney-Wollongong commuters finally get start date for new intercity trains During a visit to Eurobodalla in August, Minns said he was concerned about regions like the South Coast where he described the “threat” to Labor posed by people considering voting One Nation for the first time. And amid a threat from One Nation to Labor seats in the Hunter, the government’s signature $12 billion election commitment involves building a train manufacturing plant on a former mine site at Teralba in Lake Macquarie. Under that plan, the facility would build trains to replace the ageing Tangara fleet used predominantly on the T4 line. World.title: Australia news LIVE: Haines tributes to open parliamentary proceedings today; Hanson refuses to apologise for cartoon depicting Thorpe being run over by bus
World.content:
Election results are being tallied in Brazil, where confusion about extended polling hours at the last minute, forced counting to stop earlier this morning.

Brazil’s Supreme Court issued an extension of voting hours across the nation as some booths were closing for the day, while its electoral authorities began — and then suddenly paused — counting ballots in one of the most tightly contested elections in its history.

The order from Judge Cristiano Zanin came minutes after polls were due to close at 5pm Sunday (Brasilia time), and allowed voting to continue until 7pm. It followed requests from both candidates, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and challenger Flávio Bolsonaro.

The incumbent requested extensions nationwide over public transit problems in numerous states, including Sao Paulo — Brazil’s most populous — where 100 per cent of buses where supposed to run as per a weekday schedule but ran at 60 per cent, and Bahia, a key north-eastern stronghold for the leftist leader.

World.title: ‘Glad we checked our tickets’: First international flight departs Western Sydney
World.content:
Breaking BusinessCompaniesAviation ‘Glad we checked our tickets’: First international flight departs Western Sydney Chris Zappone October 26, 2026 — 9:24am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. As the new airport opens in western Sydney, we take a look at how it became a reality. See all stories .

The first international commercial flight from Western Sydney International (WSI) has departed this morning for Auckland. Air New Zealand flight NZ166 took off shortly after 9am as the first international departure from the airport. It comes after the plane touched down this morning after arriving from Auckland, marking the first international arrival for Sydney’s second airport. NZ165 landed at WSI at 7.27am from Auckland on Monday, 18 minutes earlier than expected. It marks the start of the airline’s travel to WSI, where it will fly three times weekly from Auckland. Matt and Serena Ross are among the passengers on the flight to Auckland. Chris Zappone NZ166 passengers Matt and Serena Ross said they were pleased with the option of a second airport in Sydney. “It’s a milestone event, so it’s special to be part of that,” said Serena. “Having more options for Kiwi travellers to come here will be great.”



“It’s nice to see a flash new airport up and running,” said Matt, but added the opening of WSI came as “a bit of surprise”. Related Article Western Sydney International ‘Final piece of the puzzle’: Western Sydney Airport opens for business The couple took a long Uber ride to arrive at WSI. They had assumed when they booked their tickets they would be leaving from Kingsford-Smith Airport at Mascot. “Glad we checked our tickets to verify what airport they were flying out of,” he said. Air New Zealand will fly three times weekly to Auckland, serving the existing community and business ties between western Sydney and New Zealand. It will be followed by Singapore Airlines in November, and Fiji Airways and Qatar Airways next year.



Air New Zealand chief operations officer Kate Boyer said in “Western Sydney for us there’s a huge Kiwi population here, a big expat community, so there are friends and family connections.” “There’s business and trade links, there’s cargo, so it’s a fantastic destination.” Air New Zealand has probably the strongest Pacific destination network in the world, Boyer said with “huge connections into all of the Pacific islands that we serve.” In opening flights to WSI, the airline expects to be “able to connect people back to their family in New Zealand or the broader Pacific region.”



There are hopes by the federal government that this curfew-free airport offers the kind of flexibility for international carriers that helps bring in more business and visitors and allows for more flexibility for Australians going abroad. While Sydney’s time difference with New Zealand is only two hours, coordinating connections for long-haul flights at much more distant hubs in Asia or the Middle East is more difficult from Australian airports where curfews apply. Being able to take off and land 24 hours a day is expected to aid long-haul carriers serving Australia. People arrive to the brand new Western Sydney International Airport on opening day. Audrey Richardson WSI’s first domestic flight – a Jetstar flight to the Gold Coast – took place yesterday.



And some are hopeful that flying from WSI will give Air New Zealand a bigger slice of the trans-Tasman travel. Trans-Tasman corporate bookings are on the rise, increasing 8.4 per cent year-on-year, according to Flight Centre data. Flight capacity across all carriers on the Australia-New Zealand route is also on track to grow through the rest of the year, Flight Centre said, with seat numbers rising seven and eight per cent year-on-year in the final three months of the year. Air New Zealand’s flight will give the western Sydney business community “direct access to New Zealand for the first time,” said Renos Rologas, ANZ General Manager of FCM Travel, Flight Centre Travel Group’s corporate travel outfit.



“It’s also a fitting backdrop for this quarter’s booking growth, led by construction, manufacturing, and healthcare and social assistance – sectors with people and projects on the ground on both sides of the Tasman.” Air New Zealand general manager of short haul, Lucy Hall, said that for businesses and travellers across western Sydney, WSI “provides a new, convenient gateway to New Zealand” that also gives the wider Sydney market a fresh choice of two airports. Related Article Airports ‘Slow burn’: Western Sydney Airport’s real challenge awaits after launch For some customers, it will ease the journey to and from the airport, and for those who travel for work, this will be a plus.



“Together, the additional capacity, new airport options and greater flexibility give us real confidence about the opportunity for trans-Tasman business travel over the year ahead,” Hall said. World.title: Victim shot in head remains critical as hunt for gunmen continues
World.content:
NationalQueenslandCrime Victim shot in head remains critical as hunt for gunmen continues Cameron Atfield and Courtney Kruk October 26, 2026 — 9:15am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
