A manhunt is under way for the shooter and accomplices behind a drive-by shooting in Logan on Saturday night that injured four people, including a teenage bystander who was shot in the head. Police responded to reports of gunshots fired from a vehicle outside the Fitzy’s Loganholme centre on Bryants Road, where a boxing event was being held, about 8.15pm on Saturday. A 19-year-old Jimboomba woman was shot in the head and neck and rushed to Brisbane’s Princess Alexandra Hospital in a critical condition. People had gathered outside during an intermission of the boxing event when they were fired upon by masked gunmen. Cameron Atfield She remained in a critical condition on Monday.



Three other people – a 38-year-old Browns Plains man, a 37-year-old Salisbury man and a 27-year-old Cornubia man – were shot in the abdomen and received surgery. All were in a stable condition on Sunday. Loading Detective Inspector Ian Galpin said he was appalled the young woman’s life now hung in the balance, telling reporters on Sunday she was not believed to be the group’s intended target. “I believe she is an innocent bystander,” Galpin said.



“It’s horrific. It’s something that her family should never have to go through.” Galpin said event organisers told police there was nothing to suggest something might occur before “at least half-a-dozen shots” were fired at people standing near a drop-off zone outside the venue from the front passenger window of a Mitsubishi. Witnesses and CCTV saw two men wearing balaclavas and gloves in the vehicle. Police continue to search for them and at least one other person believed to have picked them up after they set the Mitsubishi on fire.



The car was found set alight on Maloney Road at Waterford West. A second vehicle collected the pair and Galpin said they had reason to believe one of them might have been burnt. A dual-cab ute was also set alight on Beaudesert Road at Tamborine. Galpin said investigations were under way to see if that second vehicle was involved in the incident. Related Article Updated

Queensland Police Young woman critical, multiple people hospitalised in drive-by shooting south of Brisbane Taskforce Maxima, the Queensland police bikie squad, is involved in the investigation. Logan Mayor Jon Raven said he was not aware of any significant bikie activity in his city.



“Police said there is no further threat and we have to trust our men and women in blue and their assessment,” Raven said. “But more than that, the people that you see every day in the streets of Logan are good people. They’re your friends. They’re your neighbours. They’re part of your community. Police at the scene on Sunday. Cameron Atfield “These individuals do not represent the people of Logan, and they do not represent what we’re about.” In a statement on Sunday, organisers for the boxing event – Logan City Tiles – said they were “heartbroken” and were praying for the full recovery of all victims.



“These types of incidents have no place in the boxing community or any part of the broader community. Right now, our thoughts go out to the victims and all that were affected.” Premier David Crisafulli said he hoped the offenders would be brought to justice swiftly and he pledged to exercise strong new laws to prosecute the shooters. “Earlier this year, we passed amongst the strongest new laws for drive-by shooting in the country, and it’s my hope that these people responsible for it are arrested and that those new laws apply to them,” he said. Police will provide an update on the incident on Monday. Get alerts on significant breaking news as happens.

World.title: ‘An A-plus character’: The prospect from a family of Essendon diehards who could kickstart the Dons
World.content:
SportAFLAFL 2026 ‘An A-plus character’: The prospect from a family of Essendon diehards who could kickstart the Dons Marc McGowan Updated October 26, 2026 — 9:09am ,first published 5:00am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

A decade after Essendon overlooked future All-Australian Hugh McCluggage for Andy McGrath, the Bombers have the chance for a do-over-of-sorts. Next month’s draft marks the first time since that 2016 edition that Essendon will have the No.1 pick, which they have privately committed to using on Port Adelaide’s academy prodigy Dougie Cochrane. Ethan Drever could be the No.2 pick in next month’s AFL draft. AFL Photos The Power will match the Bombers’ bid on Cochrane – this year’s consensus best prospect – but what Essendon do next is the fascinating part. They could place another bid on Carlton’s father-son gun Cody Walker, but the expectation is they will select someone not linked to another club. Ethan Drever, a 188-centimetre midfielder from Ballarat, may be that player.



Editor's pick AFL 2026 Exquisitely talented, daring, smart: This Brighton Grammar footy captain is shaking up the draft Like McCluggage, Drever came through the GWV Rebels program and has emerged as one of the outstanding options at the pointy end of the draft. The similarities don’t end with the club and positions they play, either. “Ethan’s an A-plus type of character,” Rebels talent operations lead Brooke Brown told The Age. “He’s the most beautiful individual, both on and off the field, in regards to how he’s interacted with all the Rebels staff, players and families. This kid couldn’t get into trouble if he tried. “I worked with Hugh McCluggage when he was at the Rebels, and I see so many Hugh McCluggage traits [in Drever]. Nothing fazes him, and he just gets on with the job. As a leader, he’s not boisterous or in your face. He leads by example and by skill.”



Drever is in the mix at Essendon’s top selection. AFL Photos McCluggage joined Harris Andrews and Josh Dunkley as a Brisbane Lions co-captain this past season after long being highly regarded for his leadership, standard-setting and emotional intelligence. Another commonality between the Rebels graduates is that they can both seriously play, although Drever’s smooth-moving playing style and ability to impact the game inside and outside the contest is most often likened to GWS star Finn Callaghan. Drever honed in on Callaghan when those comparisons started flooding in, but also closely studied McCluggage, Hawk Will Day and Adelaide captain Jordan Dawson. “I want to be a powerful player,” Drever said. “I love running out the front of the stoppage and being attacking, but I’d also love to be [known as] a two-way runner and really good defensive midfielder.”



The defensive side of Drever’s game was not a strength in the early part of his Rebels tenure, according to Brown, but he quickly changed that and has a reputation as a quick learner. Related Article AFL 2026 ‘Spelling mistakes everywhere’: How an email from the heart got this AFL prospect a scholarship He is a great athlete, too, which was rammed home at the draft combine, where he finished fifth in the 20-metre sprint and top 10 in both vertical jump tests. After spending much of the previous two seasons across halfback and on a wing, Rebels coach David “Deeks” Loader unleashed Drever – as promised – through the midfield with great effect in 2026. He averaged 28 disposals, 14 contested possessions and seven clearances. The 18-year-old won Vic Country’s MVP award at this year’s AFL under-18 championships, was an All-Australian, made the Talent League’s team of the year, and claimed the Rebels’ best-and-fairest award.



“‘Deeks’ put me at half-back in my bottom-age 18s season, just to start my Rebels journey, which was really good, but this year I was always going to move into the middle,” he said. “He just wanted me to get used to the speed of the game, and I think it really helped me.” Drever could join Essendon’s top draftees from last year: (from left) Jacob Farrow, Sullivan Robey and Dyson Sharp. Justin McManus Drever is now viewed as the prototypical big-bodied midfielder for the modern game, but it was not that long ago that he was a more modest 178 centimetres and regularly being blocked at the rim in his previous sporting life as a basketballer. The Rebels don’t have their own resident gym like some other Talent League clubs, but he has also taken it upon himself to become more physically imposing.



Related Article AFL 2026 Who the players rate as the cream of the crop in this year’s AFL draft “It’s made a big difference. Being a bit taller, and putting on some size helps so much with my power and confidence as well,” Drever said. “Having that confidence is massive because you know you can take a hit and not be afraid to get tackled as you’re coming out of a stoppage. I think confidence is a huge part of sport – mentally and physically – and it’s something I’ve tried to really improve.” The rebuilding Bombers used first-round picks last year on Sullivan Robey, Jacob Farrow and Dyson Sharp, who could all end up part of a new-look on-ball brigade. Drever’s skillset – if they draft him – would complement that group. He ticks numerous boxes for what Essendon need, and even comes from a family of Bomber diehards. “I’ve heard they’ve got a bit of interest, which is pretty cool, and it’s awesome to be in consideration,” Drever said. “My whole family’s excited about that because they’re all Essendon supporters.”

World.title: Wet and stormy start to the week, but ‘bright and clean’ conditions coming
World.content:
NationalQueenslandWeather Wet and stormy start to the week, but ‘bright and clean’ conditions coming Courtney Kruk October 26, 2026 — 8:39am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Residents of south-east Queensland are bracing for another wet week as a weather system bringing heavy rain and possible storms persists across the region. Rain soaked broad parts of eastern and south-eastern Australia at the weekend, with Queensland copping the highest rainfall totals, according to the Bureau of Meteorology. The inland Wide Bay-Burnett region north of Brisbane and the Central Ranges recorded between 200-300 millimetres of rain by the end of Sunday. More rain is on the way for soaked parts of Queensland. Catherine Strohfeldt “[It’s been an] incredibly wet weekend across southern Queensland, which has continued over the last week due to a blocking high-pressure system in the Tasman Sea,” senior meteorologist Sarah Scully said.



“Many parts of Queensland have seen two to four times their average October rainfall in the last week.” Related Article Extreme weather Storms over south-east lifting but system threatens supercells on way Scully said a severe storm “stalled” over the Darling Downs in the early hours of Monday morning, dropping more than 100 millimetres of rain over 12 hours in parts. A severe thunderstorm warning in place across south-east Queensland, including the south-east coast, Darling Downs and Granite Belt, was cancelled just after 7am. Senior meteorologist Angus Hines said the storms had weakened and were moving out across the water, but with warmer temperatures could return after midday, particularly over the border in the Northern Rivers region of NSW.



“The temperature [today] is back to that 30–31 degrees range,” Hines said. “[It’s] fairly humid as well, lots of moisture around after the recent rainfall. “So about lunchtime or perhaps early afternoon, we could see more severe storms around the area.” Hines said the week ahead would bring “longer nice weather gaps” between rain, cloud cover and cooler temperatures, with conditions easing by the weekend. “Thursday [and] Friday looks like overall much brighter conditions with just a lower chance of showers.



“More of this week should be bright and clean.” Get alerts on significant breaking news as happens.

World.title: Wet and windy end to Labour day weekend for parts of the country
World.content:
Parts of the South Island are being lashed by heavy rain and severe gales as an active front moves up the country.

Westland and Fiordland are under orange rain warnings, with up to 250 millimetres of rain expected about the ranges of Westland.

People travelling home after the long weekend are advised keep an eye on weather and road conditions.

Metservice issued rain and wind warnings and watches for some of the South Island on Sunday, but more warnings are now in place for parts of the lower North Island.

An orange strong wind warning is in place for Wellington, Wairarapa, the Canterbury High Country and Plains, Otago, Fiordland, Marlborough, Southland and Stewart Island, with gusts up to 120km/h possible in exposed places.

These warnings expire from 7pm Monday in the south and 9am Tuesday in Wellington.

A strong wind watch has also been issued for Christchurch from 6pm Monday, the Tararua District from 11pm Monday and in Horowhenua and Kāpiti from 3am Tuesday.

Metservice said gusts of around 140 km/h can be expected in the most exposed parts of the Canterbury High Country.

An orange heavy rain warning is in place for Grey and Buller districts, Westland, the headwaters of the Canterbury lakes and rivers about and south of Arthur's Pass, the headwaters of the Otago lakes and rivers, and Fiordland.

An orange heavy rain warning will go in place for the Tararua Range from 2am Tuesday.

There is a heavy rain watch for the Queenstown Lakes district away from the headwaters and Southland and Stewart Island, expiring from 11pm Monday in the south to 11am Tuesday in the north.

Westland can expect the heaviest falls, with 200 to 250mm forecast about the ranges and 300mm possible about isolated peaks.

Most of the warnings expire from Tuesday morning with those in the lower South Island expiring on Monday.

Metservice said there is a low to minimal chance of its orange wind and rain warnings being upgraded to red.

World.title: Cordons come down at Auckland playground where child critically injured
World.content:
The cordons around a playground in a central-city park in Auckland have been taken down after a child suffered critical injuries.

Police say a person was assaulted by a man at the park about 4.45pm on Sunday.

Inspector Jim Wilson said the man was not known to the victim.

A 20-year-old man was taken into custody and both the victim and the man required medical treatment.

St John says one person was taken to Auckland City Hospital in a serious condition and the other to Starship Children's Hospital critically injured.

World.title: Southland scrub fire still burning as wind hampers firefighting efforts
World.content:
Fire and Emergency says a scrub fire in Southland is still actively burning, with the weather hampering firefighting efforts.

Nearly 80 hectares of land has been affected by the blaze in the Centre Hill area.

A FENZ spokesperson said high winds were preventing aircraft from operating and ground crews had not been deployed due to the terrain of the high country grazing and conversation land where the fire was located.

They said investigators would be looking into the cause of the blaze and firefighting would resume when conditions allowed.

FENZ was first alerted to the fire on Sunday afternoon. Six helicopters worked with monsoon buckets to protect two communications towers in the area.

Later on Sunday night, FENZ said helicopter pilots had done an excellent job to protect the telecommunications infrastructure and there was no immediate risk to people or homes in the area.

Crews were stood down overnight.

MetService has a strong wind warning in place for Southland on Monday, with severe gales expected to reach up to 120 km/h in exposed places.

World.title: Coroner calls for tougher safety standards after forestry worker crushed under falling tree
World.content:
A coroner is calling on Worksafe to look at strengthening safety regulations in the forestry sector, after a 39-year-old father of two was crushed to death by a falling tree.

Mykhailo Tremel was working on a forestry block in Clevedon, south of Auckland, in June 2022, when he radioed fellow workers for help.

They found Tremel down a steep bank, lying on the ground injured, with his chainsaw still running. He was initially conscious, but deteriorated.

The two workers administered CPR and called emergency services, but Tremel was pronounced dead at the scene.

The tree had crushed his chest and abdomen, and he had significant internal injuries.

Worksafe prosecuted Turoa Logging Limited - who had hired Tremmel - and Pulley Contracting Limited - who was managing the harvesting.

After pleading guilty in the Manukau District Court, they were fined and ordered to pay reparations totalling more than $300,000.

In her finding, released to the public on Monday, coroner Rachael Schmidt-McCleave said Tremel was originally from Ukraine and arrived in New Zealand in 2016.

She said, had a logging machine been used, Tremel's death would likely have been prevented.

"I further find that better observation techniques, call-in procedures and emergency response procedures would have (on the balance of probabilities) improved the chances of Mr Tremel having a favourable outcome after the accident."

Coroner Schmidt-McCleave received expert advice from health and safety expert Michael Cosman.

Cosman told the coroner research showed people who felled trees without a machine were 300 times more likely to die at work than others in the New Zealand workforce.

He said, as more machines were used to cut down trees, the number of deaths in the industry had steadily declined.

The coroner said advice from the Ministry of Business Innovation and Employment (MBIE), as well as WorkSafe, suggested regulatory work on forestry had been on hold since 2022.

There were plans to include provisions in the Health and Safety at Work Amendment Act, which would have applied to the forestry sector, Coroner Schmidt-McCleave said.

"Cabinet agreed in May 2021 to make the regulations and drafting began, but this was paused in later 2022," she said in her finding.

While there was an approved code of practice (ACOP), these were not mandatory.

The coroner referred to a 2021 coronial finding into the death of another forestry worker, which encouraged MBIE to prioritise "regulatory frameworks".

"Decisions about the content and relative priority of that programme, including whether particular regulatory work should be pursued or prioritised, are for the minister, with MBIE providing advice," Schmidt-McCleave said.

The coroner recommended WorkSafe review the current code of practice to make it clear that no wind-damaged trees should be cut down manually.

She also recommended WorkSafe consult and consider whether an observer be required to help with decision-making, look out for loose branches and to give medical help in an emergency.

The coroner noted that, while Tremel had an 'observer', they were operating an excavator and couldn't see Tremel.

World.title: One dead after car collides with tree in Christchurch
World.content:
One person is dead after a car collided with a tree in central Christchurch early on Monday morning.

Police were called to the intersection of Montreal and Armagh streets at 3.20am after reports that a car had collided with a nearby tree.

Senior Sergeant Craig Ellison said the sole occupant of the vehicle was found dead at the scene.

The road was closed while the Serious Crash Unit attended. It reopened just after 7am.

World.title: Police seek offender as Māngere assault victim remains critical
World.content:
Police continue to make enquiries after a serious assault in Māngere early on Sunday left one person in hospital in a critical condition.

The injured person was transported to hospital after police were called to an incident on Massey Road around 12.10am.

The victim remained in hospital in a stable but critical condition, Detective Senior Sergeant Kevin Tiernan said.

The alleged offender fled the scene.

Tiernan confirmed the incident was isolated and that there were no public safety concerns.

No arrests had yet been made as police followed "positive lines of enquiry", he said.

World.title: Chris Hipkins promises his government would be formed by Christmas
World.content:
Chris Hipkins promised a Labour-led government would be formed by Christmas, as he cast his vote on the first day of advance voting for the election.

He's also set out five things he would tackle in his first week as prime minister.

If Labour's elected, bringing down the cost of living and fixing healthcare are its priorities, Hipkins said on Monday.

"New Zealanders don't want more political arguments. They want a government that gets things done.

"That's why I'm committing to forming a Labour-led Government before Christmas and getting straight to work. Kiwis can't afford to wait any longer for things to get better."

Hipkins said his Cabinet would take five immediate actions:

End what he calls the "Health New Zealand hiring freeze" and start delivering Labour's guarantee of a job for every eligible New Zealand-trained graduate nurse.

Launch Labour's Emergency Department Recovery Plan, urgently assessing what hospitals need to open more staffed beds and get patients into wards faster

Start work on a new Medicard providing three free GP visits and free prescriptions each year

Approve a three-year fuel tax freeze, progress public transport fare caps of $20 a week in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch and $10 elsewhere, and prepare for a 10 percent student loan balance reduction for eligible borrowers from 1 July 2027

Agree to legislation banning price gouging on groceries, power and petrol illegal, ban hidden fees and unfair charges, and meet supermarket leaders to set out plans to separate their wholesale and retail operations.

Hipkins said he would hold every minister accountable for delivering those things.

World.title: Election live: Advance voting begins as party leaders head to the polls
World.content: Follow our daily live coverage of all the happening on the 2026 election campaign trail. We'll have updates, breaking news and analysis from Political Editor Jo Moir, Deputy Editor Craig McCulloch and their team through to election day on 7 November.

World.title: Smith will be 'fine' as Australia returns to Cape Town
World.content:
Australia returns to the scene of one of the darkest days in the country's cricket history when the series-deciding third Test against South Africa starts at Newlands on Tuesday.

ABC Sport will have live blog coverage and radio commentary of the third Test.

The battle may be mental as much as one of skill for several of the Australian players, not least former captain Steve Smith, who was at the centre of the Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal in 2018.

Current skipper Pat Cummins was part of that side, as were fellow seamer Josh Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon, though they say they had no knowledge of the attempt to alter the condition of the ball with a piece of sandpaper.

Smith bore the brunt of the considerable fallout in Australia eight years ago and, having not reached the heights he might have expected on this tour, averaging a little over 20 with the bat, he would see this as the perfect time to put that right.

How Sandpapergate rocked Australian cricket In 2018, Sandpapergate rocked Australian cricket to its very core. Here's how a febrile atmosphere colluded with a team persistently testing the limits of acceptability to change the game.

There has so far been little chatter in South Africa about Sandpapergate but that could change at Newlands, where the first three days' ticket sales have been strong after sparse crowds at the first two Tests in Durban and Gqeberha.

"He'll be fine," Australian opener Travis Head said of Smith.

"I think he showed that in 2019 in England. We support him.

"He's been through a lot in that space and handles it well. Sometimes it brings the best out of him, as we've seen in the past."

The series is level at 1-1 after big wins for both sides in the opening two games, and Australian wicketkeeper Alex Carey told reporters on Sunday that it looked to be another good Test-match pitch.

"We are still a couple of days out but it looks another great surface," he said.

"If you look back at Durban it was a five-day Test match and a great contest between bat and ball. The same in Port Elizabeth [Gqeberha] and this should be no different."

There has never been a Test match played at Newlands in October, and just three in November, all against Australia.

The tourists won the first two in 1902 and 1921, but the most recent November fixture was an eight-wicket victory for South Africa in 2011 when Australia was famously bowled out for 47 in the second innings.

South Africa will be without fast bowler Anrich Nortje, who injured his groin in the second Test.

Captain Temba Bavuma said the hosts would pick horses for courses in terms of his replacement.

"You've got guys like Gerald [Coetzee], Pato [Dane Paterson], as well as [Corbin] Bosch, and we have Sen [Senuran Muthusamy] as well, so the options are there," he said.

"Whoever we decide, we'll be confident they form part of our best XI for the conditions."

Reuters

World.title: England legend Anderson disappointed over Lancashire exit
World.content:
England legend Jimmy Anderson says he was disappointed when Lancashire decided not to renew his contract.

The 44-year-old fast bowler, England's all-time leading Test wicket taker, has played for his home county for 25 years.

Anderson, who claimed 704 Test wickets for England, will leave Lancashire as the county looks to rebuild its squad for a promotion push from Division Two of the County Championship.

The veteran bowler made 112 first-class appearances for Lancashire, claiming 443 wickets, and was involved in its County Championship title triumph in 2011.

"I've supported Lancashire since I was a kid, and so to get to play for them for 25 years was a dream come true," Anderson said in a statement.

"I have always found it special walking out to play at Old Trafford and have some incredible memories of doing so including the honour of being captain.

"If it was up to me it wouldn't have ended like this but I wish the players and fans all the best for the future."

Anderson, who was appointed Lancashire's red-ball captain for the first time in his career in the 2026 season, took 50 wickets at an average of 17.68 this summer, but the county finished seventh out of eight teams in the second division.

That was the seventh-best return of any bowler in Division Two, while his average was fourth-best of any bowler to bowl over 100 overs in the season, and considerably better than any other Lancashire player.

"I spoke to Jimmy about our ambitions to rebuild our men's squad that is capable of securing promotion from Division Two of the County Championship and then challenging to win Division One over the next three to four years," said Paul Farbrace, Lancashire's incoming director of cricket.

"We are keen to begin that rebuild now, both in terms of the playing squad and the wider professional cricket set-up, and to make important progress over the coming months.

"As part of those plans, I informed Jimmy that we had taken the incredibly difficult decision not to extend his playing contract for the 2027 season."

Lancashire Cricket had honoured Anderson's contribution to the club by renaming the Pavilion End at Old Trafford the James Anderson End. He was also knighted in 2025 in recognition of his services to cricket.

Reuters/ABC

World.title: Essendon sack coach after one-win AFLW season
World.content:
Hawthorn will remain anxious after their win over Essendon, though they are not faring worse than the Bombers, who sacked their coach after her one-win season.

The Bombers told Natalie Wood this week they would not renew her contract, but both parties chose to wait until after Sunday's 3.7 (25) to 3.2 (20) loss to the Hawks to inform players, coaches and staff.

The scores were level at half-time and Essendon's defensive structure was impressive, keeping the Hawks scoreless in the final quarter.

However, the Dons gave up nine intercept marks in Hawthorn's attacking half and it proved costly.

It was a needed win for Hawthorn, which found itself in eighth spot on the ladder, one win clear from Fremantle and Adelaide.

But its finals spot is not cemented with one round remaining.

If the Dockers and Crows win next weekend, and Hawthorn lose to West Coast in Perth, the all-important ladder position will be determined by percentage points.

The Hawks ran away from the Bombers in the second half. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Daniel Pockett)

Wood will see out the season, aiming to claim one more win against fellow cellar dwellers Collingwood at Windy Hill next Sunday.

"This was a difficult decision and we thank her for the role she has played in our history," Essendon chief executive Tim Roberts said.

"When we entered the competition in 2022, Natalie set the standards and culture of our team, and our back-to-back finals in 2023 and 2024 reflected that work."

Roberts added this season had been "challenging".

"We have fallen short of what we wanted on field. We believe a change is the right step," he said.

"Natalie has handled this with real integrity, and her commitment to coaching out the season says a lot about her and how much she cares about the players.

"We thank Natalie for everything she has given the club over five seasons, and we wish her all the best for the next step in her football journey."

GWS coach Cameron Bernasconi has escaped a similar fate.

His side has finished in the bottom three on the ladder for the past three seasons, but he penned a two-year contract extension at the start of the year.

His Giants team performed similarly to the Dons against Carlton.

Carlton kept their top four hopes alive with a win over struggling GWS. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Michael Willson)

The scores were level at three-quarter time, but the Blues found two more goals in the final term to secure the 5.8 (38) to 3.5 (23) win and keep their top-four hopes alive.

Essendon said the club would commence its search for a new AFLW coach, while also assessing "every part of the program to make sure it continues to grow with the competition and is positioned to improve".

Wood joined the Bombers in March 2022, ahead of their inaugural AFLW season.

During her tenure, Wood became the first woman to coach 50 AFLW games and she led Essendon to finals appearances in 2023 and 2024.

"Building an AFLW program from the ground up takes an enormous collective effort. I'm proud to have led that work and supported our players to grow as footballers and people," Wood said.

"It has been a privilege to be Essendon's inaugural AFLW senior coach."

AAP

World.title: Weather ruins MotoGP but Phillip Island goes out on high
World.content:
The phrase "die hard" doesn't sufficiently describe the passion of the MotoGP fan.

Not only did enthusiasts travel for hours in traffic to get onto Victoria's Phillip Island, but they sat all day Sunday in the rain, waiting under the looming prospect the final race on the island's iconic circuit would be cancelled.

Finally, the crowd was put out of its misery.

After delay upon delay, the final MotoGP to be held on the island was no more, unceremoniously cancelled due to poor visibility and rain that had been falling steadily overnight and into the day.

The breadth of the weekend's weather suited the mood of the final weekend of MotoGP racing.

Fans stood on Friday under a blazing spring sun to watch their heroes do practice laps at the island track, the azure waters of the Bass Strait blazing on the horizon, before conditions shifted to a wintry deluge on the last two days of racing.

Stephen Greenwood rode his bike from Campbelltown in New South Wales, and was part of the heaving crowds swarming the island in a haze of adrenaline, nostalgia, and bittersweet sense of loss.

Stephen Greenwood was one of the 500 riders who made the pilgrimage onto Phillip Island to farewell the MotoGP. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

He has hopes the race could some day return to the island.

"It's such a shame to lose it from here. It's one of the best tracks in the world and I just love coming here," Mr Greenwood said.

He said the community and atmosphere of the event was intoxicating, and draw him back each year.

"You walk the streets, you see the riders in cafes. I've seen a couple of the riders at the Italian restaurant. The track is phenomenal," he said.

"I have friends who rode down from Arlie Beach … everyone just wants to support it."

More than 500 riders took part in the final TAC Homecoming Ride last Thursday. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

One final roar

When the MotoGP makes its annual pilgrimage to the Gippsland region, the island becomes a melting pot of cliche and chaos, with the roar and hum of motorcycles in their thousands set against the backdrop of a blue ocean that could be the envy of any Greek Island.

Aria Bie from Knox near Melbourne has had her licence for three years, and travelled to the island on her Triumph Daytona 660 for the Homecoming Ride.

"Coming to Phillip Island is really exciting, because I'm still getting used to the long ride for the whole day," she said.

"But it makes it special. This is the national event, and we have lots of bikers here with passion. It just feels really nice to be part of the group and the biker community as well."

Arie Bie took park in the Homecoming Ride. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

The MotoGP has drawn thousands of motoring fans to the island to watch the annual race since 1989.

And the island pulled out all stops in its farewell to the sport.

Chequered flags hung from street lights and snapped in the coastal wind. Shop fronts were decorated welcoming the motorbikes to town. And business owners braced themselves for one of their busiest weekends of the year, coming back to life after a seasonal winter hibernation.

Pino's Trattoria owner Rosa Scarlato, almost a MotoGP celebrity in her own right, is the race's number one ticketholder.

She was part of the local push to save the race earlier this year.

And as she rode onto the iconic circuit last Thursday for the Homecoming Ride, she shed a tear.

"It's a shame we've lost it," she said.

"Driving into the track this morning, I cried just a little bit, because we've got such a beautiful venue."

She said the loss would be felt by all islanders because people worked together and made it a "very successful weekend".

Marking the occasion

Newer residents to the island have readily embraced the electric atmosphere of island life during the MotoGP weekend.

Connor Cardus, who has lived in Cowes for five years, isn't a huge motoring fan.

But as a business owner in town, he admits to getting swept up in the atmosphere every time the bikes roll in.

He even marked the occasion this year with a MotoGP-inspired tattoo.

Connor Cardus and tattoo artist Jack Montgomery commemorating the final MotoGP on Phillip Island with some fresh ink. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

"It's amazing. There are so many people, and it's such an injection for local industries, and the money that comes through," he said.

"As a punter, going down to the local pubs and seeing all the businesses so busy after a quiet winter, it's amazing. It's really what we need, and it's going to be missed.

"Over the next few years, it's going to be very clear that we had a good thing, and we lost it."

Connor Cardus's tattoo marking the last MotoGP on Phillip Island. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

One last dance

Standing beside hundreds of idling motorcycles and feeling the road rumble beneath your feet as they pass you by, it's easy to understand why riders tolerate all conditions to see their heroes tear down Gardner Straight one final time.

But despite the delays, the cancellation of the race's grand finale, and an entire day spent sitting in the cold and the rain, motoring fans were treated to one last roar, as rider and fan alike bid farewell to one of the sport's most beloved tracks.

Wet weather plagued the final day of motor racing at the Phillip Island circuit. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

World.title: Antonelli wins in US but must wait one more week for F1 world championship
World.content:
Kimi Antonelli will have to wait one more week to claim his maiden F1 drivers' championship, but the 20-year-old all but sealed the title with a near-flawless win from pole position at the United States Grand Prix.

The Mercedes ace, who needed to win on Monday morning (AEDT) to have a chance of sealing the title in Texas, was magnificent as his Mercedes team made sure he was on the correct tyre strategy to win his ninth grand prix of the season.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finished fourth, and Mercedes' George Russell placed eighth, meaning they can mathematically still win a championship that is all but decided.

Kimi Antonelli beat Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen for the win. (Getty Images: Rudy Carezzevoli)

Antonelli leads Russell by 123 points, and Hamilton by 124 points, with a maximum of 125 points left to win from the final five rounds.

Antonelli had the perfect start from pole position to hold a comfortable lead over Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

Red Bull and Ferrari elected for a two-stop strategy in Texas, bringing their drivers in early. But Mercedes did not react, believing the one-stop would be the fastest option.

It was the right call from the Mercedes team and allowed Antonelli to win the race by more than 13 seconds.

"It was a result we needed; the whole team deserve it so much," Antonelli said.

"It was perfect execution from strategy to make the one-stop [work]."

Verstappen and Leclerc pitted early, showing their hand that they were going for the two-stop strategy.

Mercedes held their nerve and kept Antonelli out, believing he would have enough pace at the end of the grand prix to hold off the fast-finishing duo who would be flying on track after their second stops.

But any hope of Verstappen and Leclerc making the final laps of the US Grand Prix exciting were thwarted by McLaren's Lando Norris, who surprisingly elected to stop just once but was fast enough to hold up Antonelli's challengers. Verstappen and Leclerc would pass Norris, who ultimately finished fifth, on lap 47 of 56, but did not have enough time to chase Antonelli.

Kimi Antonelli wins the United States Grand Prix, all but sealing the F1 drivers' championship. (Getty Images: LAT Images/Simon Galloway)

Antonelli will win the drivers' championship next week in Mexico City if he finishes ninth or higher, or Russell and Hamilton fail to win the race.

"We are very close, but we try to finish on a high and we try to clinch [the title] very soon," he said.

Leclerc, with fresher tyres, passed Verstappen for second place with five laps remaining.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, who started third, placed sixth.

Australian Oscar Piastri finished seventh, where he started, after being ordered by McLaren early to let a faster Norris overtake him.

Russell finished a disappointing eighth, copping a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage on the first lap.

New Zealand's Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) and Frenchman Pierre Gasly (Alpine) rounded out the points positions, finishing ninth and 10th respectively.

Relive the action of the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix on the blog below.

World.title: Kangaroos escape with World Cup win after Fiji threatens upset
World.content:
The Kangaroos have locked in their semifinal spot at the Rugby League World Cup, beating Fiji 36-22 after receiving an almighty scare in Brisbane.

Tom Trbojevic's second-half hat-trick helped Australia over the line after the Bati twice took the lead either side of half-time at Lang Park.

Fijian five-eighth Kurt Donoghoe was rightly named player of the match after laying on three tries and dictating terms for much of the game.

"I think we need more from everyone," Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters said after the game.

"We know we can play better but let's give Fiji a lot of credit. At times it seemed like we were getting on top and they pulled themselves back into the game."

Taane Milne's try gave Fiji an early lead. (Getty Images: Bradley Kanaris)

Despite coming into the game as 50-1 outsiders, making three early errors and conceding the first try of the night, Fiji hit back through Semi Valemei and Taane Milne to lead 10-6 after half an hour.

For the second straight game, Kevin Walters's side looked vulnerable in defence and struggled with their last-tackle options, but still led at half-time after some James Tedesco brilliance led to a try for Sam Walker on debut.

But again the Fijians hit back, with Valemei's second retaking the lead for the underdogs just after the break and Solomone Saukuru appearing to extend soon after, only for the bunker to rule a line-ball obstruction.

The Kangaroos immediately went up the other end and Tom Trbojevic dove in for his first of three straight tries to snuff out the Fijian challenge.

Valemei completed his hat-trick late on before Jacob Preston added Australia's sixth shortly before full-time to lock in their semifinal berth, playing a double-header with the similarly undefeated Jillaroos at the Sydney Football Stadium next Sunday.

Fiji will have a chance to push for a surprise final-four spot if it can pull off an upset win over New Zealand next week, which suddenly does not seem so far-fetched.

Look back at all the action in our live blog below.

World.title: Diamonds great says coach 'safe for now' after Constellation Cup loss
World.content:
Australia has lost game three of the Constellation Cup 52-49 to New Zealand to hand the trophy back to the Silver Ferns in Sydney.

After leading 41-39 heading into the final quarter of a gripping contest, the Ferns rattled off seven straight goals after three-quarter-time to establish a five-goal lead.

The Diamonds went on their own run to square the ledger at 47-47 as the Test headed into its final five minutes, but costly turnovers and penalties by Australia allowed New Zealand to win the final quarter 13-8.

After falling behind 3-0 in the four-game series, the Diamonds will be playing for pride at Melbourne's John Cain Arena on Wednesday.

The Diamonds are also a chance of losing their world number one netball ranking to New Zealand after the Ferns won gold at the Commonwealth Games in August, while Australia claimed bronze.

Head coach Stacey Marinkovich now has just a 50 per cent series winning record in the Constellation Cup.

Sophie Garbin shot 47/63 in game three. (Getty Images: Mark Metcalfe)

Before she took charge in 2020, the Silver Ferns had claimed the trophy once in 10 series. In the six series since, the Kiwis have claimed it three times.

Marinkovich is contracted through to the end of 2027. This is the last time her team will be together before next August for the Netball World Cup in Sydney.

The result looks ominous for the Diamonds' chances.

However, former Diamond Bianca Chatfield believes Marinkovich's role is safe, alluding to the challenges of the unlimited import rule in Australia's Super Netball league.

Loading Instagram content

"I think she's safe for now … unlike male sports there's not the money just to pay out coaches and get rid of them, and you do that in the heat of the moment," Chatfield told ABC's Offsiders.

"She deserves a chance to go through to the World Cup … She's facing different pressures to what other Australian coaches have in the past."

New Zealand head coach Noeline Taurua said the victory was a massive result for the Ferns after a challenging 12 months.

Taurua was suspended from coaching her team this time last year by Netball New Zealand and missed tours of Australia, England and Scotland before being reinstated.

Jessie Grenvold nabbed the Diamonds' only two intercepts of the game. (Getty Images: Mark Metcalfe)

The New Zealand Premiership has also been in fast decline due to poor broadcast deals and management by the national body. Most Silver Ferns jumped ship and signed with Australian teams to ensure they could earn a full-time wage.

"This is our opportunity to write the next chapter of our book," Taurua said.

"Commonwealth Games gold was obviously the start of that and now backing that up with the Constellation Cup.

"Whether the world number one [is next] or not, we're within cooee of Australia and getting closer, knowing that we're building towards the World Cup.

"We're just riding the wave and enjoying the moment."

Look back at all the action in our live blog of game three.

World.title: Antonelli on pole as he eyes record-setting world F1 title
World.content:
Kimi Antonelli has blasted to pole position for the United States Grand Prix on a weekend when he could claim his place as Formula One's youngest world champion.

The 20-year-old Italian turned the tables on Ferrari as the Scuderia, who had led the way for all three practice sessions, again fell flat when it came to the crunch on Sunday AEST.

Antonelli pipped Max Verstappen, winner of the past two races, to first spot on the grid by 0.179 seconds, with Isack Hadjar third in the second Red Bull.

Australia's Oscar Piastri and his McLaren teammate Lando Norris managed seventh and eighth respectively.

How Kimi Antonelli can win the F1 title Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli can secure his maiden Formula 1 drivers' championship with victory at the United States Grand Prix.

For Antonelli to claim the crown in the Lone Star State is a tall order; he would need to win Monday's race (AEST) and hope that George Russell finishes lower than ninth and Lewis Hamilton lower than fifth.

But he did the first part of his job in supreme fashion, delivering a stellar lap to blow away his rivals and underline why he is the champion-in-waiting.

Russell struggled and will line up sixth, while Charles Leclerc and Hamilton managed only fourth and fifth as Ferrari's pace disappeared when it mattered.

The race represents 20-year-old Antonelli's first shot at clinching the crown, but with a 102-point lead and only a maximum 150 left up for grabs, it appears merely a matter of when the Italian becomes champion.

Ferrari have not been on pole since Leclerc in Hungary in 2025, while Hamilton's wait for top spot in qualifying extends to that same race two years earlier, 1,190 days ago.

Hamilton is a five-time winner around the Circuit of the Americas and an upgraded Ferrari appeared to have put him in the mix to end his long wait for a pole position.

Ferrari president John Elkann was watching on from the garage, with pressure on the team to finally deliver in qualifying after a difficult run of races and increased speculation over the future of team principal Fred Vasseur.

This weekend could be bigger than Texas for Kimi Antonelli if he can clinch the world title. (Getty Images: Clive Mason)

But Hamilton, 41, whose sole Ferrari win came in Barcelona in June, and Leclerc were again unable to pull it out of the bag.

Meanwhile, both Williams were among the stragglers knocked out in Q1 as their miserable season continued, with Alex Albon fuming "what a s***show".

Norris topped Q1 but McLaren chief executive Zak Brown told Sky Sports that Ferrari were "in a league of their own".

Leclerc hit back to lead Q2 but Antonelli and Russell had also come to the fore to suggest the battle for pole would be a tight one.

Antonelli soared to the top of the charts after the first run in Q3 and the Italian's challengers fell by the wayside.

AAP/PA

Tech.title: iFixit’s look inside the iPhone Duo may explain those broken screens and hinges
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

As is tradition, iFixit has torn open the latest iPhone and laid its parts bare on a table. It found some interesting details about how Apple might be hiding the crease on the Duo’s folding screen and gave it a 5/10 repairability score. That might not seem particularly high, but it’s the best score the site has given to a foldable yet.

The internal screen’s matte nano-texture cover doesn’t just make it more readable in bright sunlight; it also helps mask the crease by scattering reflections. When looking at the display under a microscope, iFixit also found oval-shaped subpixels arranged at various angles, which the site believes are designed to reduce artifacts and further mask the crease down the middle of the display.

The nano-texture outer layer is relatively easy to replace without swapping out the OLED underneath. If you do need to repair the display itself, however, good luck. As is the case with other foldables, it’s an expensive nightmare. Dust did make it into the USB-C port, speaker grills, and the hinge — making it a bit crunchy. But noticeably less of the glow dust found its way inside the phone than the Z Fold8 or Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

As for reports of damaged screens and cracking hinges, iFixit has some theories. The hinge on the iPhone Duo is incredibly complex, and they suspect part of it sometimes isn’t descending properly. There is also an accordion cable that passes over that exact spot, and it’s near the edge of the battery. It’s possible this is concentrating pressure and leading to the “audible crack” reported by some and the broken screens. Apple did not immediately return a request for comment.

Tech.title: Scott Walker’s The Drift will get under your skin
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

In my mind, Spooky Season music comes in two distinct flavors. There are the fun, occasionally goofy songs like “The Monster Mash” and John Carpenter’s “Halloween Theme.” Then there is the genuinely terrifying: Throbbing Gristle, The Body, or Scott Walker’s The Drift.

This 2006 album from the singer-songwriter is truly upsetting. On it, Walker explores death, disease, and tragedy. But not just from some abstract perspective. There are visceral descriptions of the hanging of Benito Mussolini and his mistress Clara Petacci. He sings about 9/11, his stillborn twin brother, and the Srebrenica genocide. Lyrically, it’s about as dark as an album gets.

But it’s the experimental backdrop that drives it all home.

At times, the record sounds more like the score to an Ari Aster film than anything that could be called pop music under even the most generous definitions. Seasick guitars in the verses of “Jesse” give way to dissonant strings that drone oppressively over the chorus. You can feel the low-bitrate MP3 noise that opens “Clara” in your jaw, which also allegedly features the sound of his percussionist punching a pig carcass as part of the rhythm track.

Songs stop on a dime, linger in uncomfortable silence, then erupt in bursts of mechanical noise. Animal bleating, foley work, and atonal orchestra sections grind against Walker’s warble. Nothing is ever quite in tune, and it can be challenging to get through the record in a single sitting if you’re not in a very particular mood. But sticking with it can be quite rewarding.

Some songs and performances are so beautiful they send shivers down your spine or give you goosebumps. Scott Walker’s The Drift is the opposite of that. You will still have an involuntary physical reaction, but it’s more shudders than shivers. It will make your skin crawl.

Scott Walker’s The Drift is available on Bandcamp and most major streaming services, including YouTube Music, Apple Music, Qobuz, Deezer, and Spotify.

Tech.title: A YouTuber dissected an iPhone Duo and thinks he found the cause of crackgate
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Social media and the iPhone Duo subreddit are filled with reports of Apple’s foldable failing quickly and in spectacular fashion. Some users report having the phone for only a few hours before the hinge seems to catch on something, then audibly crack and break the screen. Tellingly, the cracks all seem to happen in the same place.

YouTuber CuriousHagi was able to reproduce the cracked screen during some durability testing of the iPhone Duo. Then he pulled it apart to try and find the culprit. What he found is that the Duo’s hinge is quite complex, consisting of a gear-like central hinge and two different types of linking hinges.

The piece that broke is one of the links in the middle of the phone that happens to be thinner than the links below or above it, and it snapped at a small notch where it would be weakest. He also found marks where the hinge met the support plate, indicating where it may have gotten caught.

Tech.title: Zen Browser is the Arc replacement I was looking for
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

I know many of you are mourning the loss of the Arc browser, and I get it. It felt like the first app in a long time to really offer a new approach to browser design. Atlassian bought the company last year and shifted its focus to developing Dia, its even more AI-focused browser. And soon enough, Arc will officially be no more, leaving dedicated users in a lurch. But I abandoned Arc quite some time ago for the Zen Browser and haven’t really missed it. If you’re willing to deal with some minor inconveniences, I think you’ll find Zen is the Arc replacement you’re looking for.

Zen unabashedly rips off all the best bits of Arc. Visually, they’re almost indistinguishable. It has the launcher-like pinned sites, tab bar on the left, siloed spaces, and mods that let you customize the browser’s UI to your liking. It takes the bits that made Arc’s interface feel fresh, then strips out everything that made it bloated and drove me into the arms of another.

Most notably, Zen is AI-free.

There’s no agent in a sidebar hounding me to let it handle tasks. I’m not worried about Zen training an LLM on my browsing activity. It’s just a web browser.

Zen prides itself on its privacy features: “Beautifully designed, privacy-focused, and packed with features. We care about your experience, not your data,” it proudly proclaims. Now, I’m no fool. I know that nothing I do on the internet is really private, but with Arc, it always felt like my data was an integral part of the business plan. That’s not the case with Zen. It’s a free and open-source project that relies on volunteers and donations.

In addition to Zen Mods that can do anything from tweak the look of an active tab to overhaul how PiP videos are handled, you can also install Firefox extensions. Yes, you can install Chrome extensions in Arc, but anecdotally, I’ve found that Zen handles extensions better. Both Zen and Arc are different enough from a UI perspective that not all extensions display properly, but Zen offers more workarounds.

Zen also just kind of lets me focus on the task at hand. Links open in “glance” view, which is a temporary pop-over tab, which is really great when you’re doing some window shopping or light research. If I want to open it in a proper tab, it’s just a click away. Zen also has a floating bar that pops up whenever you press Command+T or CTRL+T. From here you can launch a new tab, switch to an existing tab, perform a search from the search engine of your choice, and even trigger an extension.

Zen isn’t perfect. I love its clean UI and organizational features, but it can’t play DRM-protected video content right now. That means Netflix, Spotify, HBO, Disney+, and more do not work in Zen. The Zen Team is working to obtain a Widevine license from Google. In the meantime, I use Chrome when I want to watch a movie, which is fine. Zen is built on Firefox, and Firefox’s Web MIDI support is lacking. So I have to fire up Chrome semi-regularly anyway.

I also miss Arc’s Boosts in some cases, but I’ve learned to accept the web as it is. Zen implemented a similar Boost feature in May, but it’s not super obvious and, if there is an official, easily browsable repository of installable Boosts, I’ve yet to find it. Instead, you have to tweak individual sites’ appearance yourself.

If you tried Zen a long time ago and were turned off by its buggy early builds, rest assured it’s come a long way. Look, if you are all in on Arc’s AI features, Dia is probably more your speed. Personally, I always loved Arc’s interface, but never really dug the vibes. Zen just feels right.

Update October 25th: Added information about Zen’s implementation of Boosts.

Tech.title: This Switch 2 sequel accessory was a few millimeters away from being good
Tech.content:
is an editor covering deals and gaming hardware. He joined in 2018, and after a two-year stint at Polygon, he rejoined The Verge in May 2025.

The Crkd Nitro Deck was a saving grace for the original Nintendo Switch. The slide-on $59.99 accessory brought Hall effect sticks to drift-plagued consoles — no need to open up your Joy-Con for a complicated repair. The Nitro Deck 2, made for both the original Switch and the larger Switch 2, continues the tradition of having better sticks than what Nintendo puts in even the newest Joy-Con (though these aren’t Hall effect or TMR). But it doesn’t feel as essential, and there’s one thing I really can’t stand about it.

It’s too difficult to use the Nitro Deck 2’s ABXY face buttons without the right stick getting in the way. The stick-to-button arrangement is a big step down from the original Nitro Deck (and especially bad compared with the symmetrical Steam Deck-like stick layout in the video output-ready Nitro Deck Plus). I’m surprised Crkd’s team thought this was an improvement. My patience with the run-based gameplay in Echo Weaver is already tested enough, and trying to quickly hammer inputs on the Deck 2 only adds to the frustration.

Your preference may differ, but I like having a little breathing room between the right stick and the face buttons. Some companies choose to space them out or, in the case of the Switch 2’s Joy-Con, make the stick small enough to allow my thumb to hover over it so I can press the buttons. The Deck 2 makes me adjust my thumb’s angle of approach outside of what’s comfortable. It’s just a few millimeters off.

The original’s superior slide-in design was traded for a vice-grip design to ensure compatibility with both the newer and older Switch consoles. The Deck 2 has a twisting mechanism on the back that you can loosen, tighten, or lock. It’s clever, though the tradeoff for broader compatibility is a design that feels inherently less secure. Crkd is asking Switch 2 owners to put a ton of faith in this mechanism staying tight around their $500 consoles. My Switch 2 didn’t feel wobbly during testing, but I’d rather not have to think about its safety at all when I’m gaming. I would have preferred a slide-in design for the Deck 2 made expressly for the Switch 2.

It’s disappointing that Crkd’s Joy-Con-replacing solution isn’t as good because I like some things about it more than the original. For instance, the accessory has adjustable tension on both sticks, so they can snap back to their original position faster or slower than the default speed. Also, the accessory’s bulkier design makes the console more comfortable in my medium-size hands to use in handheld mode. It also has a bunch of customizable buttons: four on its back and an extra near the triggers.

Not many similar accessories are out there yet, and the other one I tried (the abxylute N6) wasn’t all that good, either. I plan to test Mobapad’s latest take on Joy-Con soon, and it seems promising. Alternatively, you can add a bunch of comfort to your Switch 2 in handheld mode with either the Dbrand Killswitch 2 or the Mechanism Basecase. And with the money left over, you could buy a good wireless Switch 2 controller with long-lasting sticks and better rumble.

Tech.title: Now you can watch Instagram Reels on your Apple TV
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Instagram is continuing its expansion into living rooms with Instagram for TV, for Apple TV. The company first started testing a version of the platform focused on Reels, live streams, and other video content, blown up for a bigger screen in December of last year. Then, in June, it launched a slew of new features for the app, which is available for Amazon’s Fire TV, Samsung Smart TVs, and Google TV.

Now Meta is bringing the app to Apple TV, though there’s been little fanfare. MacRumors spotted an updated Instagram app in the App Store that added Apple TV to its list of compatible platforms on October 23rd. Archived versions of the app page from as recently as October 18th listed only the iPad and iOS.

The app will likely be an important part of Instagram’s strategy going forward as it tries to push into longer-form, episodic content, and cash in on the growing popularity of microdramas.

Tech.title: r/opensource just banned AI, non-English speakers, and more
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

The mods at r/opensource posted new submission rules that, among other things, banned projects that use AI. The post made Saturday evening opens by saying, “If your project uses AI, is made by AI, or is intended for AI, it’s not welcome on r/opensource. AI, as it exists today, is incongruent to this Open Source community.”

The new rules have set off a firestorm in the comments, and even spurred the creation of a rival sub r/trueopensource. Moderator Wolvereness has waded into the comments to explain that there’s nuance and room for selective enforcement, such as “software that incidentally has accessibility features that use AI,” including automatic captioning. But that hasn’t slowed complaints from the community who feel the new rules are too broad, misguided, or vague. Many have pointed out that the Linux kernel now contains some AI-generated code, and so projects using it could be banned under the new rules.

While the AI ban is getting most of the attention, mods are placing other restrictions on posts as well. Projects submitted must be at least one year old, actively maintained, and have multiple contributors. That would bar solo developers with new projects from looking for help. The mods even say “we can no longer field requests asking for maintainers or people to contribute.”

The mods also effectively banned any non-English-speaking members of the community. “If you don’t speak English, you need to find a different community,” the post reads. “We cannot distinguish between AI-written and AI-translated. Since you don’t speak English, you can’t even verify yourself if it translated correctly.”

Tech.title: Google’s AI search changes upended online publishing
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more about AI’s impact on the web, follow Emma Roth. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here.

How it started

The digital publishing industry has relied on Google for a very long time. Many outlets spent time and money optimizing their webpages to show up at the top of the search engine, with the goal of getting readers to click on their articles or discover their websites for the first time. For years, the relationship between Google and publishers was largely reciprocal; online publishers filled out Google’s search index with content, while Google supplied publications with exposure and traffic.

But that relationship has changed. The launch of Google’s AI search features — coupled with changes to the way it ranks search results — has made it harder for publishers to survive on traffic from Google alone. In 2024, Google rolled out AI Overviews, a feature that slots an AI-generated search result summarizing pages from across the web at the very top of Google Search, with links to sources its AI system determines to be the most useful placed below the summary. Instead of vying for clicks on the first page of Search, publishers became beholden to an AI system that regurgitates results, with no guarantee that users will actually click on the source of that information.

Though Google’s AI Overviews got off to a shaky start, the feature immediately raised concerns among publishers, with the News/Media Alliance saying it will be “catastrophic” to web traffic. A 2024 investigation from the Press Gazette found that Google’s AI Overviews appeared for almost a quarter of news-related searches in May 2024. By August, the outlet found that AI Overviews had begun impacting the visibility of publishers by replacing media sites that previously held the top spots on Google’s search engine for certain queries.

A future where Google could eventually stop sending traffic to outside sites on the web has only gotten closer as the company builds out its vision for an AI-powered search. In May 2025, it launched AI Mode, a feature that replaces Google’s standard search engine with a chatbot-like interface that provides detailed summaries from results on the web.

How it’s going

The concerns raised by the News/Media Alliance were real: Traffic to online publishers tanked following the launch of Google’s AI search features. A June 2025 report from The Wall Street Journal revealed how traffic to Business Insider, The Washington Post, HuffPost, and the WSJ itself has declined since 2022. Data from analytics company Similarweb suggested that search traffic to The New York Times sank from 44 percent to 35.5 percent in three years, the WSJ reported.

A report from Digiday pointed to similar dips at Digital Content Next (DCN), a trade association that represents outlets and media companies like Bloomberg, The Associated Press, The New York Times, Condé Nast, and Vox Media. Between May and June 2025, DCN says 19 of its members experienced a traffic loss on Google, ranging from 1 to 25 percent, Digiday reported. DMG Media, which owns Daily Mail and Metro, told the UK’s Competition and Markets Authority that click-through rates dropped by up to 89 percent between June and July 2025, citing impacts from AI Overviews. On top of all of this, Pew Research found that people are “less likely” to click on links to other websites when they see an AI Overview.

These numbers starkly contrast with Google’s claims that its AI search features are helping the web. Last year, Google Search head Liz Reid said click volume from the search engine remained “relatively stable,” adding that AI search is sending more clicks to different types of websites — especially those “with forums, videos, podcasts, and posts” from other users. Nick Fox, Google’s senior vice president of knowledge and information, told the BBC, “From our point of view, the web is thriving.”

What happens next

Online publishers have had to adjust their strategies in the wake of falling search traffic, with many leaning on social media, newsletters, and subscriptions to promote and make money from their work. Others are using a toggle that allows them to opt out of appearing in AI Mode and AI Overviews without affecting their visibility in search — an option Google broadly rolled out following an order from the UK. But this still doesn’t fix sinking traffic.

Pushback from online publishers appears to have resulted in some changes to Google’s AI search features. The company has begun to make sources more prominent in AI Mode and AI Overviews, as hovering over a link in either feature will show a pop-up with a list of articles and accompanying images. Another AI search change puts in-line links “higher up in responses more frequently.”

Google will likely continue making changes to how it presents sources in AI search, while coming up with ways to compensate publishers that inform its results. The company says 400 publishers, including The Washington Post, CNN, Axios, and the Financial Times, are now part of its News AI pilot program, which licenses content to develop new AI features. It’s also testing a program that pays publishers for the use of their content in AI Overviews and AI Mode, according to reports from The Information and Digiday. Whether this program is enough to repair Google’s relationship with publishers remains to be seen.

By the way

Google is burying blue links even further beneath AI Overviews. The search summaries have started to automatically expand for some queries, instead of requiring users to manually click a “Show more” button.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Reddit is also considering cutting off Google due to dropping traffic.

It’s not just publishers and online forums that are concerned about AI Overviews — the nonprofit Common Sense Media claims the search summaries pose an “unacceptable” risk to kids by failing to respond appropriately to children in crisis.
